We evaluate SemWeaver on 39 KNighter-derived CSA checkers from Linux kernel fixes. With analyzer evidence, refinement reaches 23 warning-positive vulnerable revisions (vs. 15 for KNighter's loop) and raises version-level $F_1$ from 0.448 to 0.575. An ablation removing internal evidence recovers fewer silent cases and produces different checker edits, indicating that the two evidence configurations address complementary recognition gaps. Additional experiments cover three editor models on a 12-subject subset, a CodeQL query refinement, and controlled source-form variations. A qualitative follow-up on all 11 non-tied comparisons traces each warning-count change to a specific checker repair, such as recognizing a lowered callback or unwrapping an expression cast.

title: Learning Direct Control from Optimization for Dynamic Target Tracking
summary: Dynamic target tracking requires a mobile robot to maintain target visibility while navigating obstacles with smooth, feasible controls. Online trajectory optimization explicitly encodes these objectives but requires repeated numerical solving, whereas waypoint-based neural policies separate geometric prediction from control execution. We introduce LECO, a framework that transfers tracking optimization into offline learning of a direct-control policy. LECO predicts control sequences and maps them to trajectories through a differentiable kinematic model, allowing trajectory-level objectives to directly guide control learning. A decaying expert-guidance curriculum initializes effective tracking behavior and progressively shifts learning toward these task objectives. At deployment, a predictive safety lock checks short-horizon obstacle clearance and invokes a classical planning and control fallback when the predicted motion is unsafe or the target prediction is invalid. Across three simulated obstacle densities, LECO reduces root-mean-square linear jerk by 14.1--31.2\% relative to the best competing method for this metric and achieves the highest tracking success rate, with per-cycle computation times of 4.25--5.63\,ms. Experiments on two robot platforms further demonstrate tracking through indoor narrow passages and outdoor forest environments. These results demonstrate that learning direct control from optimization enables smooth and robust dynamic target tracking.

title: A Multi-Asset Dataset and Tail-Risk Framework for DeFi Yield Trading Derivatives
summary: Yield trading has emerged as a pivotal innovation in Decentralized Finance (DeFi) by decoupling principal from yield streams to enhance capital efficiency. Despite its significance, the field lacks fine-grained datasets for systematic empirical analysis. We address this gap by constructing the first large-scale benchmark dataset for Pendle, the pioneering on-chain interest rate derivatives protocol, spanning 24 months across 340 active markets with complete lifecycle observations. Our analysis reveals a structural market transition toward stablecoin-dominated "flight-to-quality" dynamics. To tackle the heavy-tailed nature of yield data, we propose Tail-MSE, an asymmetric loss function that prioritizes tail risk awareness through dynamic penalty weighting. Experiments across six state-of-the-art time series models demonstrate consistent improvements in volatility forecasting robustness, enabling the Tail-MSE Sniper strategy to achieve superior risk-adjusted returns in over half of all markets.

title: A Hierarchical Method for Environmental Sounds Recognition in Complex Acoustic Scenes
summary: Environmental noise identification is essential for noise control, yet conventional single-stage classifiers suffer from class confusion under imbalanced multiclass conditions. This paper proposes a lightweight hierarchical model integrating a Frequency-Time Adaptive Network (FTANet) with a two-stage classification mechanism. FTANet employs parallel asymmetric one-dimensional convolutions to capture temporal dynamics and frequency-band distributions, while adaptive fusion attention (AFA) enhances discriminative acoustic features. In the first stage, FTANet classifies sounds into five coarse-grained categories covering 25 fine-grained classes. In the second stage, samples are routed to the corresponding category-specific classifiers for fine-grained recognition. On a self-constructed dataset, FTANet achieves 95.45% coarse-grained accuracy with only 0.2004M parameters. On UrbanSound8K, it achieves 79.24% mean accuracy and 80.37% mean F1-score in ten-fold evaluation, outperforming compared convolutional models. Field tests on the Tianjin Online Acoustic Environment Monitoring Platform yield 87.94% coarse-grained accuracy and 97.21% conditional fine-grained accuracy for natural sounds correctly routed to C2. The complete hierarchical model achieves 87.18% overall accuracy and 87.40% weighted-average F1-score, demonstrating its feasibility for urban environmental noise monitoring.

title: What Will Replace Pull Requests? Rethinking Software Collaboration for AI Agents
summary: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents has put pull requests under pressure: agents open millions of pull requests per month, while some open-source projects have begun to restrict or disable external contributions. We investigate which alternatives to pull requests practitioners are proposing or adopting and what these changes mean for empirical software engineering research. We reviewed 50 gray-literature documents from 31 organizations or individuals published between October 2025 and October 2026, coding the problems each named, the mechanisms it proposed or adopted, which of five roles of pull requests (integration, review, rationale, accountability, and external contribution) each mechanism takes over, and the evidence offered. Most responses retained pull requests in some form, whether by adding tooling, attaching a new artifact, or restricting access, and restriction was the response most often reported as adopted. Several proposed alternatives moved review and rationale into agent conversations and session records, but only Zed reported using a replacement in practice. Only two documents outlined a replacement for external contribution, and neither reported adoption. Pull requests are changing in ways that pull-request datasets will not capture: reviews conducted in agent conversations leave no pull-request comments, and projects that disable pull requests disappear from samples of newly opened ones. We outline a research agenda on the effectiveness of the emerging alternatives, their consequences for open-source participation, and the adaptation of empirical methods.

title: A Certified Robustness Framework for Backdoor Poisoning Attacks using $f$-Divergences
summary: Machine learning systems trained on untrusted data are vulnerable to data and backdoor poisoning attacks, in which an adversary corrupts training and test samples to manipulate predictions at inference time. Randomized smoothing yields provable defenses against such attacks, but existing applications to train-time robustness are limited to specific threat models and smoothing mechanisms. We propose a general framework that allows expressing complex adversary constraints on the number of corrupted training examples, feature and label perturbation magnitudes, and test-time corruptions. Our framework randomizes inputs by combining data subsampling with feature, label and test-sample noising. We develop a composable certification procedure based on $f$-divergences that handles arbitrary combinations of threat models and noising strategies, and recovers several prior certification regimes exactly as special cases. We demonstrate our framework experimentally by certifying, for the first time, robustness under general $\ell_p$-constrained poisoning adversaries under bagging with additive Laplace, Gaussian, and Uniform noises.

title: Subcodes with Prescribed Hull Dimensions in Linear Codes:Enumeration, Containment, and Asymptotic Distributions
summary:
Mass formulas for prescribed hull dimensions have mainly been studied for linear codes viewed as subspaces of the whole space. We study internal enumeration for an arbitrary fixed parent code. Let $C$ be an $[n,k]_q$ linear code with an $\ell$-dimensional hull, and let $s$ be the subcode dimension. We determine the number of subcodes with prescribed dimension, hull dimension, and type over finite fields of both even and odd characteristic. We decompose the parent code into an LCD complement and its hull, and use projection to reduce enumeration to the corresponding problem inside the LCD complement. This yields explicit formulas refined by complete type and shows that the counts depend only on the relevant parameters, not on the particular parent code or its length. The known whole-space mass formulas and the enumeration of LCD subcodes of LCD codes arise as special cases.
  Motivated by code extension, we also study the dual containment problem: for a fixed code, we enumerate larger codes containing it with prescribed hull dimension and type. By duality, this problem is converted into the subcode enumeration problem already solved above, leading to corresponding conditional mass formulas.
  Finally, we investigate the asymptotic distributions arising from the exact enumeration formulas. When both the subcode dimension $s$ and $k-\ell-s$ tend to infinity, the hull distribution is governed by the LCD complement, and the limiting proportions are explicit constants determined by the field, the prescribed hull dimension, and the relevant type. When $s$ approaches or exceeds the dimension $k-\ell$ of the LCD complement, we determine the asymptotic proportion of subcodes attaining the minimum possible hull dimension and establish the associated concentration behavior. Analogous asymptotic results are obtained for the containment problem.

title: How Do Coding-Agent Harnesses Self-Evolve? An Empirical Study of Retrospective Adaptation
summary: Coding agents can adapt their harnesses, the software, configuration, and instructions used to run them, based on experience from earlier tasks, but whether these adaptations improve their behavior on later tasks remains unclear. We study \retro, a skill that asks an agent to review a completed session and propose harness changes, and ask what changes it proposes and whether implemented changes reduce repeated work on later tasks. We ran Claude Code on 30 SWE-bench Verified issues, qualitatively coded the 125 proposals from \retro, implemented 24, and evaluated 12 harness changes on later issues from the same repositories in fresh sessions with and without each change. Most proposals referred to an event in the session, but 18 of 43 lint-related proposals recommended a practice regardless of what had happened. Among the seven evaluations in which sessions without the change encountered the targeted problem, two changes eliminated the targeted action, one reduced its occurrence, four showed no reduction, and some changes added work on unrelated issues. Harness self-evolution requires more than generating and implementing changes: it needs ways to establish whether a change helps on later tasks and to revise or remove changes that do not.

title: Fed-MAPTrack: Federated Modality-aware Prompt Tuning for RGB-X Tracking
summary: RGB-X tracking complements RGB appearance with thermal, depth, or event observations, but centralized training requires collecting multimodal videos at a single location. Federated training keeps raw videos local, but sensor heterogeneity can create a mismatch between parameter-sharing domains and the clients contributing to them. This mismatch is particularly relevant when RGB-only clients coexist with sensor-equipped clients: their RGB observations remain useful, but they provide no auxiliary measurements for learning sensor-dependent interactions. We propose Fed-MAPTrack, a modality-aware federated prompt tuning framework for RGB-X tracking. The pretrained tracking backbone and prediction head are frozen, and clients optimize and exchange only prompt-related parameters. The server aggregates RGB-shared parameters globally and maintains separate thermal, event, and depth banks for auxiliary-specific, fusion, and normalization parameters. Selective participation retains RGB-only clients' contributions to the global RGB bank while excluding their fusion and normalization updates from modality-specific aggregation. Across three matched training repetitions under a fixed client partition, Fed-MAPTrack improves the mean FedAvg scores by 2.35 AUC points on LasHeR, 3.45 SR points on VisEvent, and 2.11 F-score points on DepthTrack. Among the nine evaluated methods, it achieves the highest mean thermal AUC and depth F-score, while its mean event SR is 0.07 points below that of Independent FL. Controlled ablations show that extending the bucketing scope without a compatible participation rule can reduce performance. These results highlight the need to jointly define the sharing domain and eligible contributors for each parameter group.

title: Stop or Clarify? Experience-Conditioned Active Fact Verification
summary: Fact-verification benchmarks score the final label, while an interactive verifier must first decide whether the available evidence is sufficient. We focus on that intermediate Stop-or-Clarify Decision. Uncertainty alone is insufficient, because the benefit of another evidence-acquisition step is unknown before the step is taken. Sequential Experience-Adaptive Clarification (SEAC) wraps a fixed verifier with a lightweight evidence-acquisition policy. For each claim, SEAC retrieves evidence, runs the verifier, forms a label-free decision state, and combines stop risk with an observational clarification-utility estimate from earlier executed trajectories. Clarification is requested only when this score exceeds the action cost and decision threshold. On SciFact, LIAR, and FEVER, SEAC improves mean accuracy and macro-F1 over the compared fact-verification and active-retrieval baselines. Equal-budget and formula-level diagnostics support selective clarification as a contributor to the gain, while the small SciFact split leaves its paired improvement inconclusive.

title: Intellectual Property Protection of Hyperdimensional Computing Classifiers: Black-Box Ownership Verification via Model Watermarking
summary: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) offers efficient learning and inference for resource-constrained systems, yet ownership verification of its models remains underexplored. We present the first systematic investigation of model watermarking in HDC by adapting backdoor-based embedding to three classifiers with different prototype-learning mechanisms. Across four benchmarks, with conventional neural networks as references, we examine whether watermarks can be learned without compromising task accuracy and whether they survive subsequent model modification and replication. The error-driven classifiers, AdaptHD and OnlineHD, support verification at a nominal trigger exposure of 1% with at most 0.58 percentage points of mean accuracy loss, whereas single-pass Vanilla HDC requires greater exposure and can incur substantial accuracy costs. The error-driven models retain verification under native continued training, but extraction produces surrogates that reproduce much of the task behavior without verifiable watermarks. Watermark overwriting readily embeds attacker watermarks into HDC prototypes and erodes the owner's watermark more strongly than in the neural network references, although the strongest erosion coincides with large accuracy losses. We further deploy watermarked AdaptHD on an FPGA and stress its execution through undervolting and overclocking. Verification survives substantial computation errors, whereas more severe stress either causes verification failure together with accuracy collapse or results in inference timeouts. These findings establish the feasibility of watermarking in HDC while identifying limitations in retention under extraction and sensitivity to overwriting.

title: Reasoning Patterns for Efficient AI Coding: An Empirical Study
summary: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) generate long reasoning traces that expose intermediate inference behavior, offering opportunities to study and control reasoning in AI coding. However, the underlying patterns in these traces and their potential for analyzing and guiding coding models remain poorly understood, limiting systematic characterization and inference-time control of LRM reasoning. We conduct an empirical study of reasoning patterns across four representative coding tasks. We transform reasoning traces into structured action sequences and mine recurring fragments using within-task support, cross-task contrasts, and valid--invalid support contrasts. We characterize four general reasoning patterns by coding agents: design-to-implementation for code generation, state tracing for execution reasoning, evidence--fix--recheck for debugging, and semantic mapping for translation. We further identify positive and negative patterns associated with valid and invalid reasoning traces, respectively. Positive patterns reflect verification-driven convergence, whereas negative patterns reflect repeated design revision, reflection, and knowledge recall without closure. To demonstrate their practical utility, we evaluate three pattern-based applications: task identification, pattern-guided prompting, and pattern-aware early stopping. Features capturing general reasoning patterns enable accurate task identification from reasoning traces without accessing task descriptions or final answers. Prompting guided by positive and negative patterns improves the overall accuracy of downstream tasks, while negative pattern-aware early stopping substantially reduces API-reported token usage with only a modest decrease in pass@1. All three applications also generalize to previously unseen models, showing that reasoning patterns can support both the analysis and control of LRM behavior in AI coding.

title: Relational Composition as Parallel Transport: What Per-Entity Frames Force in Attention
summary: A dot product means something only when both vectors share a coordinate system. Content words have one; a fresh entity does not: rotating its coordinates alone changes nothing. We take this per-entity frame freedom as a symmetry and ask what it forces in attention. For orthogonal transports, invariant scores depend only on norms and the transported inner product $\langle x_i,T_{ij}x_j\rangle$; equivariant messages lie in the span of $x_i$ and $T_{ij}x_j$. Endpoint channel count bounds transport rank, so with one vector per entity relations must be supplied; standard attention is the flat sector of a shared frame. Representation theory attaches an integer to each mechanism; the readout decides which. With orthogonal transitions, a convex-cell readout composes a finite group exactly only at or above its smallest faithful real representation dimension. At this minimum, exactness forces a faithful representation. An even readout can decode a cover at smaller width, and the gap is unbounded. Below its threshold, the part of the group a mechanism cannot see sets an accuracy ceiling computable before training. 17/17 fitting seeds at minimal width passed tests through length 1000, versus 7/18 at twice the width; 12 models carry correctness certificates to explicit lengths, from the weights alone. On $C_3\times A_4$ (faithful width 5), descent at width 4 learned the 72-state double cover under sign-blind attention (6/48 seeds; monotone 0/48); on a frozen cover the cross-entropy-optimal affine head is uniform, a quadratic head exact. On parsed CLUTRR, transported composition beats a matched transformer by 41 points at 4-10 hops, but forcing isometries costs 65 points; on StepGame's commutative algebra, isometries help. Static embeddings gave each word one vector; contextual models gave each occurrence its own; per-entity frames make each relation an operator, the unit in which relations compose.

title: Correlation-Aware Exploration for Long-Trace Reasoning
comments: 28 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the Workshop on Long-Context Foundation Models (LCFM), NeurIPS 2026
summary: Reasoning models trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) now produce chains of thought thousands of tokens long, and recent studies reveal that such training is prone to policy collapse. Entropy regularization is the standard remedy, but it works by pushing probability mass away from the few tokens that carry it and toward the vast low-probability tail of the vocabulary, and it applies this force once for every token of the reasoning trace. This puts the bonus in direct conflict with the entropy decay that convergence requires, and makes its coefficient difficult to set in the long-trace regime. To resolve this tension, we propose Info-GRPO, an information-theoretic framework that cultivates correlation between the policy and a latent prior. Rather than raising entropy everywhere, Info-GRPO builds on the mutual information between a latent variable and the trajectory it induces: augmenting prompts with latent seeds during training lets the model explore diverse policies correlated with the prior, while the seed-conditioned entropy is guided toward convergence. Diversity is therefore carried across whole reasoning traces rather than by per-token randomness, and exploration no longer fights entropy reduction. Experiments show that Info-GRPO outperforms vanilla GRPO and entropy-regularized GRPO across diverse reasoning benchmarks. On AIME24, it improves $Avg@8$ over GRPO by 3.75%, 1.66%, 4.16%, and 4.17% on four backbones, and it reaches the same majority-vote accuracy with $8\times$ fewer samples. Code and models will be publicly released.
comment: 28 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the Workshop on Long-Context Foundation Models (LCFM), NeurIPS 2026

title: MINT: Mitigating Structural Inconsistency via Attentive Message Passing for Financial Anomaly Detection
summary: Illicit account detection is a critical task for financial risk control systems, aiming to pinpoint malicious actors within transaction networks. Existing efforts typically recast transaction networks into directed multigraphs and leverage graph neural networks (GNNs) to detect anomalies via topological structures under the homophily assumption. However, directly grafting GNNs onto transaction graphs is faced with at least two pivotal challenges, i.e., structural inconsistency and label scarcity. The former arises from deceptive connections forged by malicious actors, while the latter stems from the lack of annotated data. In light of these, we introduce MINT, a novel graph neural framework that mitigates structural inconsistency via an attentive message-passing scheme on transaction graphs. Specifically, MINT introduces a discrepancy-aware feature propagation, which tracks malicious actors by quantifying deviations between nodes across bi-directional transaction flows. A transaction salience module is proposed to mitigate structural inconsistency by adaptively regularizing the interaction strength between nodes. Furthermore, to alleviate label scarcity, MINT is optimized via Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning, which exploits only a minority of illicit nodes coupled with a majority of unlabeled ones. Extensive experiments conducted on three financial transaction benchmarks, including two large-scale public and one in-house real-world datasets, validate the superior effectiveness of MINT over several cutting-edge baselines.

title: Improving Reasoning with Rollout Agreement for Group-Based Policy Optimization
summary: Recent methods for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) use rollout diversity to improve reasoning performance or training efficiency. Despite these gains, the extent to which differences among correct-answer rollouts reflect useful alternative reasoning or unresolved errors remains poorly understood. We investigate this question through a blind paired analysis of a model trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), comparing the highest- and lowest-agreement correct-answer traces for the same problem. Across 126 pairs, low-agreement traces have more spurious reasoning than high-agreement traces (35% vs. 22%), including internal inconsistencies and misuse of problem conditions. Based on these findings, we propose RoAR (Rollout-Agreement Reward), which adds reasoning-level agreement to GRPO's rewards for verified-correct rollouts. RoAR computes this signal from existing on-policy rollout groups, requiring no human-written rationales, additional sampling, or separately trained process evaluator. On five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the 1.5B GRPO-RoAR model reaches 55.5% mean pass@1 under zero-shot evaluation using 7K training examples, exceeding GRPO and GRPO-CARE by 6.0 and 5.5 percentage points. A separate blind audit of 100 problems answered correctly by all four 1.5B models finds spurious rates of 18% for GRPO-RoAR, 32% for GRPO, 27% for GRPO-CARE, and 37% for DRA-GRPO. Our findings identify reasoning validity as an important consideration when using rollout differences to guide learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/ldi-kyunghee/RoAR.

title: DimFlow: Bidirectional Grid-Expert Learning for Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction
summary: Dynamic Gaussian reconstruction requires compact scene features to support coordinated changes in geometry and appearance. A factorized grid provides efficient local queries, but accurate interpolation alone does not ensure that the resulting dynamic attributes remain compatible across space and time. We introduce DimFlow, a framework that learns these features through bidirectional interaction between a multi-resolution grid and a coordinate-based expert branch. Feature-level adversarial alignment connects their distributions, adaptive fusion transfers complementary information, and activation-masked residual feedback refines the grid during training. Four attribute experts organize deformation, rotation, opacity, and temporal information before Gaussian rendering. In the aggregate comparison across D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, and DAVIS, DimFlow achieves 39.73 dB PSNR, improving on 4D-GS by 1.92 dB while matching its reported 85 FPS rendering speed. The model occupies 18.9 MB, compared with 18.3 MB for 4D-GS. Component and attribute-expert ablations reveal complementary contributions from feature alignment, adaptive exchange, and temporal processing.

title: Decision Model Factory: Building Specialized Sovereign Decision Models
summary: Decision needs vary with each application, language, and deployment environment. The Decision Model Factory turns those needs into specialized, sovereign models on demand. A brief recipe guides the training, calibration, verification, and evaluation of a selected backbone, delivering a deployable decision model under the operator's control. The same workflow creates a new specialist whenever the requirements change. Across Japanese decision tasks, compact deployment, and long-context passage ranking, five factory-built models improve upon their backbones; three surpass the strongest results in a fixed public Japanese benchmark comparison. A dedicated runner computes only permitted-answer probabilities and reuses shared context, more than doubling serving speed on matched multi-question workloads with essentially unchanged decision scores. Together, the factory and runner make fast, task-specific decision models practical to build and deploy whenever needed.

title: Consequence-guided clarification: releasing minimum-compliance topology-optimized designs from incomplete specifications
comments: 24 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Supplementary Information (40 pages) and the two author adjudication records are ancillary files. Code and data: https://github.com/nbbllxx0/consequence-guided-clarification
summary: A converged topology optimization can solve the wrong problem when loads, supports, or the domain are underspecified. Assuming defaults, or asking the problem's author about every detail, ignores how much each answer changes the design. We propose consequence-guided clarification (CGC), which bases acceptance on computed mechanical consequences. CGC computes a reference design for each of a finite list of complete specifications, called readings. A design is accepted only if its compliance is at most 5% above the reference at every reading consistent with the answers. Otherwise, CGC asks the question whose worst answer leaves the smallest worst-case excess, and withholds acceptance at its question limit. To save optimizations, the screening variant CGC-S postpones some references until a candidate must be checked. We developed and evaluated both on 36 arXiv-derived tasks, treating each of 134 readings in turn as intended and simulating correct answers. In 26 tasks, the default-reading design failed another reading. Apart from always-asked questions on load direction, sign, and material budget, asking everything took 188 questions; CGC and CGC-S each took 105. The acceptance test supplied most of this saving: applying it to the default design alone took 117. Relative to asking everything, CGC-S requested 4.6 extra reference designs per avoided question, each from two optimization starts, counting optimization time only. References are not certified optima: better ones pushed three accepted cases above tolerance, and finer meshes changed some decisions. Within these limits, the test shows which readings a design covers and which details block acceptance.
comment: 24 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Supplementary Information (40 pages) and the two author adjudication records are ancillary files. Code and data: https://github.com/nbbllxx0/consequence-guided-clarification

title: GUIFlow: Temporal Redundancy-Aware Incremental Inference for GUI Agents
summary: GUI agents built on vision-language models interact with continuously evolving interfaces, yet conventional inference repeatedly recomputes representations of largely overlapping observations and histories. This mismatch makes multi-step interaction costly, while changes in context, interface content, and action arguments prevent straightforward cache reuse. We introduce GUIFlow, a framework for full-pipeline incremental inference in multi-image GUI interaction. Our central insight is that advancing a decision need not require rebuilding all supporting representations: each interaction step can instead selectively update computational states maintained across the trajectory. To support new decisions as the context evolves, GUIFlow adapts how past computation is reused: historical KV states are position-aligned and injected into the current context; change signals guide selective updates of current-observation states in the vision encoder and language model; and earlier action responses serve as speculative drafts verified by the target model. Together, these mechanisms enable cross-step reuse throughout visual encoding, prefill, and decoding without additional training, a separate draft model, or changes to the model-visible inputs and action interface. Experiments demonstrate up to 3.39x geometric-mean speedup across offline multi-image benchmarks and up to 3.49x in online, closed-loop interaction on OSWorld, while maintaining task performance broadly comparable to the dense baseline.

title: C-SafeGen: Certified Safe LLM Generation with Claim-Based Streaming Guardrails
summary: Despite the remarkable capabilities of large language models (LLMs) across diverse applications, they remain vulnerable to generating content that violates safety regulations and policies. To mitigate these risks, LLMs undergo safety alignment; however, they can still be effectively jailbroken. Off-the-shelf guardrail models are commonly deployed to monitor generations, but these models primarily focus on detection rather than ensuring safe decoding of LLM outputs. Moreover, existing efforts lack rigorous safety guarantees, which are crucial for the universal deployment of LLMs and certifiable compliance with regulatory standards. In this paper, we propose a Claim-based Stream Decoding (CSD) algorithm coupled with a statistical risk guarantee framework using conformal analysis. Specifically, our CSD algorithm integrates a stream guardrail model to safeguard sequential claims generated by LLMs and incorporates a backtracking mechanism to revise claims flagged with high safety risks. We provide theoretical guarantees demonstrating that the CSD algorithm achieves the desired generation distribution subject to safety constraints. Furthermore, we introduce a generation risk certification framework and derive a high-probability upper bound on the safety risk of the proposed CSD algorithm. We prove that our method can asymptotically control safety risk to any desired level. Empirical evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the CSD algorithm compared to state-of-the-art safety decoding approaches. Additionally, we validate the soundness and tightness of the derived safety risk upper bound using realistic data.

title: Beyond feature attribution: Recovering latent interaction structures in machine learning models via localized CBFI
summary: Background: Understanding individual predictions in complex tabular models remains challenging, as existing additive frameworks like SHAP and LIME often obscure structural logic by absorbing nonlinear interactions into individual feature scores. Exposing these latent interaction structures is essential for automated auditing in high-stakes environments where understanding the logic of model behavior is as essential as predictive accuracy. Methods: To address this limitation, we introduce the localized case-based feature importance (CBFI) framework. Unlike traditional numerical attribution, our method decomposes instance-specific predictions into structurally distinct components, effectively separating independent main effects (G1) from pure interactions (G4) to capture explicit feature synergies and provide a principled approach for diagnosing feature combinations. Results: Comprehensive experiments on wine quality classification and medical insurance regression demonstrate that localized CBFI successfully disentangles complex interactions hidden by additive models. Furthermore, fidelity tests and synthetic ground-truth benchmarks confirm that the identified interactions correspond precisely to the nonlinear structural dependency patterns embedded in complex architectures, including gradient boosting and deep neural networks, thereby successfully shifting the explainable AI paradigm from simple numerical attribution to the recovery of interaction-driven contributions.

title: Randomized Krylov Subspace Methods for Shifted Linear Systems
summary: We propose several novel Krylov subspace algorithms termed shifted randomized GMRES (RandGMRES-Sh), shifted randomized FOM (RandFOM-Sh), shifted randomized GMRES with deflated restarting (RandGMRES-Sh-DR), and shifted randomized FOM with deflated restarting (RandFOM-Sh-DR), for solving shifted linear systems. These methods are designed to significantly reduce the computational overhead of orthogonal basis generation while preserving orthogonality under specific conditions. Besides, this unified framework makes it possible to solve all shifted linear systems at the same time by using a single shared basis. These new approaches combine multiple advanced techniques together effectively, such as randomized sketching, the control of collinear residual directions, and deflated restarting methods. Compared with the standard versions of traditional algorithms, the new algorithms show a steady but moderate improvement in convergence speed. Furthermore, we theoretically prove that although GMRES and sketched GMRES have different algorithmic solution steps, their iterates are all confined to and together span the same basic Krylov subspace. We also work out the theoretical relationship between the solutions produced by RandGMRES-Sh and RandFOM-Sh at the same iteration step before the first restart. Moreover, we strictly prove how the solutions of RandGMRES-Sh and RandFOM-Sh are related to those of their traditional versions, GMRES-Sh and FOM-Sh, respectively.

title: The Target Agent Is Its Own Best Critic but a Poor Proposer: Self-Improved Red Teaming
summary: Automatic red teaming increasingly relies on large language models (LLMs) to iteratively diagnose failed attacks and propose improved adversarial prompts or injections. Although prior work strengthens this loop through prompt engineering and search-harness design, the mechanisms underlying its two core roles, criticism and attack proposal, has not been explored. To further investigate the core roles and therefore improve red teaming effectiveness, we disentangle two design choices: whether criticism is generated by the target session itself (self-criticism) or by a separately instantiated critic (external criticism), and whether that criticism is translated into the next attack by the target session (self-proposal) or by a separate attacker (external proposal). Through our analysis, we find that self-criticism is more effective because it is grounded in the target's live execution context, including observations, constraints, and available reasoning; removing reasoning reduces downstream attack success by 6%-17%. In contrast, self-proposal is substantially less effective because awareness of the adversarial objective induces explicit refusal and non-refusal sandbagging. These findings motivate a role-separated red-teaming approach: the target session diagnoses why an attack failed, while a separately instantiated attacker generates the next proposal. On DTAP-BENCH, spanning Telecom, Workflow, CRM, and Code domains, under both direct misuse and indirect threat models, as well as multiple agent frameworks, this configuration achieves 63.2% overall attack success rate (ASR), much higher than baselines. Our results show that effective automatic red teaming depends not only on model capability and search strategy, but also on how execution context and adversarial responsibility are distributed across model sessions.

title: Rivet: Utility-Preserving Context Control for Repository-Level Coding Agents
summary: Repository-level code generation asks an agent to implement a task requirement inside an existing repository. To produce code that works in the repository, the agent needs repository evidence, such as target locations, helper definitions, caller usages, and configuration constraints, which determine how the code should be located, integrated, and executed. Because the context budget cannot hold the entire repository, existing retrieval, compression, and structure-aware methods select context by task similarity, context length, or structural proximity, but these criteria do not directly measure whether the selected context contains this evidence. As a result, the selected context can appear relevant to the task yet miss the evidence that the implementation depends on. We call this failure mode context utility dilution. In this paper, we propose Rivet, a context control framework that preserves repository evidence for coding agents under a fixed context budget. Rivet, first uses Signal Grounding to select task-related code anchors by fusing lexical, semantic, and structural signals. Utility Linking then expands these anchors through dependency, usage, and configuration relations to collect repository evidence. Finally, Budget Shaping packs the evidence by priority and, when the budget is tight, reduces snippets to signatures or summaries before dropping them. We evaluate Rivet, on two executable repository-level benchmarks, DevEval and RepoExec, with four backbone models, two context budgets (4K and 8K tokens), and eight baselines. Rivet, achieves the highest Pass@1 in all 16 settings and improves over the strongest baseline by 3.73--5.15 percentage points on average. Moreover, GPT-5-mini with Rivet, outperforms GPT-5 without Rivet,on both benchmarks while reducing inference cost by 73.3%--84.5%.

title: Guarded Agent-in-the-Loop Residual Adaptation for Evolving Wind Power Regimes
summary: Wind power forecasting models are often deployed as fixed temporal backbones, but the errors they make can vary across meteorological regimes such as cold waves, heat-and-calm periods, productive typhoon, and destructive storms. We present a guarded Agent-in-the-loop residual adaptation framework that leaves the temporal backbone unchanged and adapts only a small set of scene-conditioned residual experts. An Agent layer interprets external scene information, identifies the current regime, selects residual experts, and applies a correction only when recent observed errors support it. New experts enter the pool after they outperform their initializations on a validation set, keeping model growth under explicit control. Backbone-only and Agent-enhanced forecasts are compared at lead times of 4, 8, 12, 24, and 48 across nine time-series backbones. Across these runs, the guarded framework lowers both MAE and RMSE for all 45 backbone-horizon combinations, with average MAE reductions ranging from 11.21% to 20.26% across backbones. Online-selection baselines, component ablations, and routing analyses identify the roles of residual experts, scene-aware routing, and the online acceptance rule. Candidate-scene runs evaluate the promotion path under controlled conditions; long-term unattended deployment was not evaluated.

title: SVD-Attention: Efficiently Analyzing Attention Blocks in Transformers
summary: Pretrained transformers spend a large share of their inference compute inside self-attention, yet the per-head query-key interaction is structurally low-rank by construction. We ask a diagnostic question: across layers and architectures, which heads actually use the full rank budget on real data, and which do not? We propose SVD-Attention, a post-hoc method that decomposes the per-head interaction matrix $M_h$ and scores every singular mode by both its spectral magnitude and its activation variance across tokens on a small calibration set. The score keeps the modes the head can amplify and that real data actually activates, and discards the rest; the resulting factorization is exact for the retained modes and needs no finetuning. Across seven pretrained models and five task types, the diagnostic finds a task-dependent pattern: redundancy sits in the early to middle layers for sentiment and image classification and for generation, and in the late layers for dense prediction and extractive question answering. It is also predictive: truncating the layers it flags costs at most $1.75$ F1, while truncating the same number of layers elsewhere in the same model costs up to $50$ F1. SVD-Attention is an analysis tool rather than a compression method: acting on it reduces inference FLOPs by $0.8$-$1.5\%$ on its own and by $8$-$11\%$ when composed with weight pruning, with $0$-$4\%$ change in task quality.

title: Toward Methods and Tools for Critical Examination of Disparate Systems for Discovery of Hidden Dependencies in Engineering of Autonomous and Semi-Autonomous Systems
summary: We present a methodology, an initial AI Skill package, and emerging results, for enhancing software engineers' acquisition and application of domain knowledge and system-wide engineering perspectives towards the development of an autonomous or semi-autonomous system in a domain that may be new to them. At the core of the approach is a process involving proactive adversarial critiquing of videos of disparate systems in related environments. Among other things, the engineers and automated AI tools look for interactions, dependencies, and environment assumptions manifested in the observed systems, which are applicable also to the target system, but that otherwise might remain unarticulated in project artifacts. The approach and its supporting tools can enhance the quality of the target system, the individual engineer's skills and the organization's engineering practices.

title: Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup for Robust Camera-Based 3D Object Detection
summary: Camera-based bird's-eye view (BEV) perception methods such as Fast-BEV have demonstrated promising results with fast inference speed and competitive accuracy. However, their robustness to real-world corruptions remains insufficiently explored, posing risks for autonomous driving deployment where environmental variations are inevitable. In this paper, we propose Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup (SR-BEVS), a sparse recovery learning approach that simultaneously improves clean accuracy and corruption robustness without requiring additional data or architectural modifications. Our method identifies pruning candidates based on layer-wise weight magnitudes, applies random pruning to create diverse sparse models, and retrains each model with a randomly sampled learning rate. By averaging these diverse recovered models into a single dense model, we achieve enhanced robustness against various corruptions while introducing zero inference overhead. We further provide a mode connectivity analysis demonstrating that our pruning-based diversification preserves the connected low-loss basin necessary for stable weight averaging. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate up to 33.8% improvement in corruption robustness and a 1.8% gain in clean accuracy over the Fast-BEV baseline, with consistent improvements across sensor noise, weather distortions, and illumination changes. Our simple yet effective approach may be applicable to other BEV models.

title: Adaptive Memory Index Evolution for Agents
summary: Long-horizon agents continually accumulate experience, yet retaining a memory does not guarantee access when it is needed. Existing systems can adapt both memory content and access; we isolate persistent access updates as a separately controlled adaptation layer. We formulate this target as Memory Index Evolution and instantiate it with Adaptive Memory Index Evolution (AMIE), a lightweight plug-in layer that evolves per-memory access state from deployment retrievals without modifying stored content or retraining the host memory system. AMIE distils a semantic teacher's keep/suppress judgments into a retrieval-conditioned policy and accumulates its selective actions into bounded state that reweights subsequent host retrievals. Surprisingly, even a zero-call policy that simply accumulates retrieval frequency can match or outperform semantic policies in several settings, revealing retrieval traffic itself as a strong signal for access adaptation, while learned selectivity improves robustness when frequently retrieved memories remain useful. Across five retrieval-based hosts and three benchmarks, trained AMIE improves downstream F1 or accuracy in all 15 comparisons, by 0.70--3.37 percentage points (up to 25% relative), and improves retrieval in all 10 comparisons. Controlled analyses show that persistent competitor suppression can expose previously unseen evidence, while suppressing repeatedly useful memories creates the complementary failure mode. Together, these results establish persistent memory access as a practical adaptation layer, distinct from the content it serves, in retrieval-based agent memory systems.

title: AskGLP1: A Knowledge Graph LLM Agent for Exploring GLP-1 Experience from Online Patient Narratives
summary: GLP-1 medications are increasingly used for weight management, and many people share their experiences online. These narratives show why people take the drugs and what they experience, but they remain unstructured and disconnected from formal pharmacovigilance. We therefore present AskGLP1, a system that transforms online patient narratives into a knowledge graph (KG) and answers questions about medication experiences. Through an LLM-assisted pipeline grounded in the MedDRA terminology, AskGLP1 screens nearly 8.5 million Reddit posts for medication experiences and distills 163,135 of them, with 2,506 WebMD reviews, into a KG of 385,790 drug-side-effect and drug-purpose relations. We find that GLP-1 experiences are source- and drug-specific. Online narratives share the most common gastrointestinal symptoms with FAERS, but they foreground everyday burdens such as fatigue and food aversion, whereas FAERS reports more often include injection-site reactions and selected serious diagnoses such as pancreatitis. We further find that posts report less nausea and vomiting for tirzepatide than for semaglutide, more fatigue for Wegovy than Ozempic and for Zepbound than Mounjaro. Evaluations show that the agent answers with verifiable evidence and declines requests for medical advice. Our findings reveal gaps between what FAERS captures and what people report online, and they call for patient-centered approaches to pharmacovigilance. Code, prompts, and evaluation questions are available at https://github.com/ZhaoqianXue/AskGLP1.

AI.title_translation: AskGLP1：用于从在线患者叙述中探索 GLP-1 用药体验的知识图谱大语言模型智能体
AI.tldr: 本文提出 AskGLP1，一个结合 MedDRA 术语构建的知识图谱 LLM 智能体，可从数百万条网络叙述中提炼 GLP-1 用药体验，弥补了网络真实反馈与传统药物警戒系统之间的鸿沟。
AI.motivation: GLP-1 药物在体重管理中被广泛使用，大量患者在网络上分享了用药原因和实际感受，但这些叙述多为非结构化文本，且与正规药物警戒监测系统脱节。
AI.method: 基于 MedDRA 术语构建大语言模型辅助流程，从近 850 万条 Reddit 帖子中筛选出 163,135 条用药体验，并结合 2,506 条 WebMD 评论，提炼构建包含 385,790 条“药物-副作用”和“药物-用途”关系的知识图谱，进而开发出支持带凭据问答且能拒绝医疗咨询的 LLM 智能体。
AI.result: GLP-1 体验具有数据源和药物特异性：在线叙述与 FAERS 在常见胃肠道症状上一致，但更多强调疲劳、食物厌恶等日常负担，而 FAERS 则侧重注射部位反应及胰腺炎等严重反应；此外，替尔泊肽引起的恶心呕吐报告少于司美格鲁肽，且特定品牌间（如 Wegovy 对比 Ozempic、Zepbound 对比 Mounjaro）在疲劳报告上存在差异。Agent 评估显示其可提供可验证的证据并安全拒绝提供医疗建议。
AI.conclusion: 研究揭示了官方药物警戒系统（FAERS）捕获的数据与患者网络真实反馈之间的显著差距，证明了利用网络叙述构建知识图谱的有效性，并呼吁建立以患者为中心的药物警戒新方法。
AI.translation: GLP-1 药物越来越广泛地用于体重管理，许多人在网络上分享了他们的使用体验。这些叙述展现了人们为何使用这些药物以及具体的体验感受，但它们仍处于非结构化状态，且与正规药物警戒系统脱节。因此，我们提出了 AskGLP1，这是一个将在线患者叙述转化为知识图谱（KG）并能回答药物体验相关问题的系统。通过基于 MedDRA 术语的大语言模型辅助处理流程，AskGLP1 从近 850 万条 Reddit 帖子中筛选用药体验，并将其中 163,135 条帖子与 2,506 条 WebMD 评论提炼成一个包含 385,790 条“药物-副作用”和“药物-用途”关系的知识图谱。我们发现 GLP-1 的用药体验具有来源和药物特异性。在线叙述与 FAERS 共享了最常见的胃肠道症状，但在线叙述更加突出了疲劳和食物厌恶等日常负担，而 FAERS 报告则更多包含注射部位反应以及胰腺炎等特定严重诊断。我们进一步发现，帖子中关于替尔泊肽（tirzepatide）恶心和呕吐的报告少于司美格鲁肽（semaglutide），关于 Wegovy 疲劳的报告多于 Ozempic，Zepbound 多于 Mounjaro。评估表明，该智能体能够基于可验证的证据进行回答，并会拒绝医疗建议请求。我们的研究结果揭示了 FAERS 所捕获的信息与人们在网上报告的内容之间的差距，并呼吁在药物警戒中采用以患者为中心的方法。代码、提示词和评估问题已在 https://github.com/ZhaoqianXue/AskGLP1 开源。
AI.summary: 本文提出了 AskGLP1 系统，通过大语言模型与 MedDRA 术语结合，从数百万条网络患者叙述中提炼构建了包含数十万条药物关联的知识图谱，并开发了可验证检索的智能体。研究不仅定量对比了不同 GLP-1 药物的副作用分布，还揭示了网络患者反馈与传统药物警戒系统（FAERS）之间的互补价值。
AI.keywords: GLP-1, 知识图谱, 大语言模型智能体, 药物警戒, 患者叙述
AI.comments: 该研究具有显著的创新性和实用价值：一方面，它将大语言模型（LLM）与标准化医学术语（MedDRA）结合，构建起从海量非结构化社交媒体中提取真实世界患者体验（PRO）的知识图谱智能体；另一方面，它揭示了在线患者自述与传统监管数据库（FAERS）之间的信息互补性，强调了日常不适（如疲劳、厌食）对患者依从性的潜在影响。局限性在于社交网络数据可能存在幸存者偏差和自发报告的主观性，且分析受限于 Reddit 和 WebMD 用户群体的代表性。

title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Long-Session Degradation in Full-Duplex Speech Models
comments: The project page is available at https://kimjunho333.github.io/dmlsd-fdsm/
summary: End-to-end full-duplex spoken dialogue models enable natural, real-time spoken interactions with interruptions, backchannels, and overlapping speech. Prior evaluations have assessed diverse interaction capabilities and identified some degradation patterns across conversational turns. However, how model behavior evolves over extended sessions remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we address this gap by systematically characterizing long-session degradation and developing efficient methods to mitigate it. We introduce a closed-loop evaluation framework for long-session stability and apply it to several publicly available full-duplex speech models, revealing degradation over time in responsiveness, spoken content quality, and voice consistency. To mitigate this degradation, we propose a self-distillation-based training framework for lightweight LoRA adaptation that improves long-session stability with a small amount of additional training. We further introduce a two-resolution context (TRC) architecture that preserves recent interactions in full detail while compressing older interaction history into key-value representations. We evaluate our methods on three models with distinct architectures, assessing long-session stability, information retention, and computational efficiency. Across all three models, we show that LoRA adaptation mitigates performance degradation over ten-minute sessions, while adding TRC extends these gains beyond the training session length and reduces KV-cache growth by more than 90%.
comment: The project page is available at https://kimjunho333.github.io/dmlsd-fdsm/

AI.title_translation: 全双工语音模型中长会话性能衰减的诊断与缓解
AI.tldr: 本文针对全双工语音对话模型的长会话衰减问题，提出了闭环评估框架、自蒸馏LoRA微调以及双分辨率上下文（TRC）架构，有效缓解了性能退化并使KV缓存增长降低了90%以上。
AI.motivation: 全双工语音对话模型在较长会话过程中行为如何演变尚缺乏充分了解，需要系统性地表征长会话中的性能退化现象并开发高效的缓解方法。
AI.method: 1. 构建用于评估长会话稳定性的闭环评估框架；2. 提出基于自蒸馏的轻量级LoRA适配训练框架，通过少量训练提升稳定性；3. 提出双分辨率上下文（TRC）架构，完整保留近期交互细节并将较早历史压缩为键值（KV）表示。
AI.result: 闭环评估揭示了公开模型在响应度、口语内容质量和声音一致性上随时间推移的退化；在三种不同架构模型上，LoRA适配显著缓解了10分钟会话的退化；结合TRC架构进一步将稳定性收益扩展到训练长度之外，并将KV缓存增长减少了90%以上。
AI.conclusion: 研究所提出的自蒸馏LoRA适配与双分辨率上下文（TRC）架构，能有效诊断并缓解全双工语音模型在长会话中的多维度性能衰减，在大幅降低KV缓存开销的同时，实现了超越训练长度的长期会话稳定性。
AI.translation: 端到端全双工语音对话模型能够实现包含打断、反馈词和重叠语音的自然、实时语音交互。先前的评估虽然考查了多种交互能力并发现了跨对话轮次的一些退化模式，但模型在长时间会话中的行为如何演变仍未得到充分理解。在本文中，我们通过系统地表征长会话退化现象并开发高效的缓解方法来填补这一空白。我们引入了一个用于长会话稳定性的闭环评估框架，并将其应用于多个公开可用的全双工语音模型，揭示了响应度、语音内容质量和声音一致性随时间的退化情况。为了缓解这种退化，我们提出了一个基于自蒸馏的训练框架，用于轻量级LoRA适配，仅需少量额外训练即可提高长会话稳定性。我们进一步引入了一种双分辨率上下文（TRC）架构，该架构在完全保留近期交互细节的同时，将较早的交互历史压缩为键值（KV）表示。我们在三种具有不同架构的模型上评估了我们的方法，考察了长会话稳定性、信息保留能力和计算效率。在所有三个模型中，我们表明LoRA适配缓解了10分钟会话中的性能退化，而加入TRC则将这些收益扩展到了训练会话长度之外，并将KV缓存的增长减少了90%以上。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了端到端全双工语音对话模型在长会话中出现的性能退化问题。作者提出了长会话稳定性的闭环评估框架，揭示了响应度、内容质量和音色随时间衰减的现象；随后提出了基于自蒸馏的轻量级LoRA训练框架与双分辨率上下文（TRC）架构。在三种架构模型上的测试表明，该方法有效缓解了长会话退化并减少了90%以上的KV缓存增长。
AI.keywords: 全双工语音模型, 长会话退化, 自蒸馏, 双分辨率上下文, KV缓存压缩
AI.comments: 本研究针对全双工语音模型在长会话中行为退化这一关键却常被忽视的实际问题展开，具有很高的实用价值和工程指导意义。其创新点在于不仅提出了闭环评估体系全面揭示了长会话在响应度、内容质量与音色一致性上的退化，还结合自蒸馏LoRA与双分辨率上下文（TRC）架构，在显著提升长程稳定性的同时将KV缓存增长压缩了90%以上，兼顾了效果与计算效率。

title: Reason or Recite: Complementary Specialists with an LLM Judge for Traffic Anomaly Reasoning
comments: 18 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the AI City Challenge Workshop, ECCV 2026. 1st place in Track 3 (Traffic Anomaly Reasoning)
summary: Road anomalies such as collisions, violations, and sudden hazards demand more from video understanding than detection: a practical system must verify what happened, describe the scene, and explain the cause. We find these competences pull in opposite directions for vision-language models: closed-form questions reward precise, evidence-grounded reasoning, while open-ended answers are scored by similarity to reference text, where matching the annotation style matters as much as reasoning correctly. We present Reason-or-Recite (RoR), a two-specialist framework for the Traffic Anomaly Reasoning track of the 2026 AI City Challenge. RoR (1) rewrites the official chain-of-thought annotations into a structured, temporally grounded schema and LoRA-tunes a 9B vision-language model on the enhanced traces; (2) fine-tunes a 4-bit-quantized 27B model on answers alone, absorbing the annotation style; and (3) selects between the two candidates per question with a training-free LLM judge. RoR ranks first on the in-domain leaderboard with mean score 0.6788.
comment: 18 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the AI City Challenge Workshop, ECCV 2026. 1st place in Track 3 (Traffic Anomaly Reasoning)

AI.title_translation: 推理或复述：具有LLM判官的互补专家用于交通异常推理
AI.tldr: 该论文提出了Reason-or-Recite (RoR)，一个双专家框架，利用LLM判官解决交通异常推理任务，并在2026年AI城市挑战赛中取得了第一名。
AI.motivation: 道路异常（如碰撞、违规和突发危险）要求视频理解不仅限于检测，一个实用的系统必须验证发生了什么，描述场景，并解释原因。研究发现，对于视觉-语言模型而言，这些能力会产生矛盾：封闭式问题需要精确、有证据支持的推理，而开放式答案则根据与参考文本的相似性评分，其中匹配注释风格与正确推理同样重要。
AI.method: Reason-or-Recite (RoR) 框架包含三个部分：1) 将官方的思维链注释重写为结构化、时间接地的模式，并对一个9B视觉-语言模型进行LoRA微调；2) 仅在答案上微调一个4位量化的27B模型，以吸收注释风格；3) 使用一个免训练的LLM判官在每个问题上从两个候选者中进行选择。
AI.result: RoR 在域内排行榜上排名第一，平均得分0.6788。
AI.conclusion: Reason-or-Recite (RoR) 框架通过结合处理精确推理和注释风格匹配的互补专家以及一个免训练的LLM判官，有效解决了交通异常推理的挑战，并在相关竞赛中取得了领先性能。
AI.translation:
论文标题：推理或复述：具有LLM判官的互补专家用于交通异常推理

论文摘要：道路异常，如碰撞、违规和突发危险，对视频理解的要求不仅仅是检测：一个实用的系统必须验证发生了什么，描述场景，并解释原因。我们发现这些能力在视觉-语言模型中会产生相反的方向：封闭式问题奖励精确的、有证据支持的推理，而开放式答案则通过与参考文本的相似性进行评分，其中匹配注释风格与正确推理同样重要。我们提出了Reason-or-Recite (RoR)，一个用于2026年AI城市挑战赛交通异常推理赛道的双专家框架。RoR (1) 将官方的思维链注释重写为结构化、时间接地的模式，并对一个9B视觉-语言模型进行LoRA微调；(2) 仅在答案上微调一个4位量化的27B模型，以吸收注释风格；(3) 使用一个免训练的LLM判官在每个问题上从两个候选者中进行选择。RoR 在域内排行榜上排名第一，平均得分0.6788。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了Reason-or-Recite (RoR) 框架，旨在解决交通异常视频理解中视觉-语言模型在精确推理和注释风格匹配之间的矛盾。RoR 采用双专家系统，一个专家专注于结构化、证据支持的推理，另一个专家则学习注释风格，并通过一个免训练的LLM判官来选择最佳答案。该框架在2026年AI城市挑战赛的交通异常推理赛道中取得了第一名，平均得分0.6788。
AI.keywords: 交通异常推理, 视觉-语言模型, LLM判官, 互补专家, AI城市挑战赛
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于提出了一个“推理或复述”的双专家框架，巧妙地解决了视觉-语言模型在处理交通异常推理任务时，对精确推理和匹配注释风格这两种不同能力的需求之间的冲突。通过引入一个免训练的LLM判官来动态选择最佳输出，该方法在实用性和性能上都展现了显著的优势，对于未来交通监控和智能分析系统具有重要意义。

title: Why Are LLMs Confidently Wrong? Correcting Overconfident Errors via Causal Head Intervention
comments: The paper has been accepted by NeurIPS 2026
summary: Modern large language models (LLMs) often exhibit overconfident errors, assigning high confidence to incorrect predictions and thereby undermining reliability in real-world use. Existing calibration methods typically rely on post-hoc adjustment or retraining, operating at the output level without addressing the underlying causes of miscalibration. We propose CoCHI, (Class-oriented Causal Head Intervention), a framework that improves calibration by identifying and intervening on internal components responsible for distinct confidence behaviours. By analysing predictions through correctness-confidence patterns, CoCHI enables targeted intervention on model internals, reducing overconfident errors while preserving correct predictions. Our approach provides a mechanistic perspective on calibration, linking reliability to identifiable structures within the model rather than treating it as an output-level issue. Experiments across multiple LLMs show consistent improvements in calibration metrics, including Expected Calibration Error, Negative Log-Likelihood, and Brier Score, while maintaining accuracy on five multiple-choice question answering benchmarks. These results suggest that effective calibration requires not only adjusting outputs, but also addressing the underlying causal mechanisms within the model.
comment: The paper has been accepted by NeurIPS 2026

AI.title_translation: 为什么大语言模型会自信地犯错？通过因果头干预纠正过度自信错误
AI.tldr: 提出了CoCHI框架，通过定位并干预导致过度自信的内部注意力头，在不牺牲准确率的前提下有效降低LLM的校准误差。
AI.motivation: 现有LLM校准方法主要依赖事后调整或重新训练，仅停留在输出层面，未能解决模型产生过度自信错误的深层内部成因，从而损害了模型在实际应用中的可靠性。
AI.method: 提出面向类别的因果头干预框架（CoCHI），通过分析正确性-置信度模式来识别负责特定置信度行为的模型内部组件（注意力头），进而实施靶向内部干预，在减少过度自信错误的同时保留正确预测。
AI.result: 在多个LLM和五个多项选择问答基准上的实验表明，该方法在保持模型原有准确率的同时，一致改善了预期校准误差（ECE）、负对数似然（NLL）和Brier分数等关键校准指标。
AI.conclusion: 有效的模型校准不仅需要在输出层面进行调整，更需要干预和解决模型内部的因果机制，将可靠性与内部结构特征直接关联。
AI.translation: 现代大语言模型（LLM）常常表现出过度自信的错误，即对错误的预测赋予很高的置信度，从而削弱了其在实际应用中的可靠性。现有的校准方法通常依赖于事后调整或重新训练，仅在输出层面上操作，而未能解决导致校准不良的深层原因。我们提出了CoCHI（面向类别的因果头干预）框架，该框架通过识别并干预导致不同置信度行为的内部组件来改善校准。通过根据“正确性-置信度”模式分析预测，CoCHI能够对模型内部进行针对性干预，在减少过度自信错误的同时保留正确预测。我们的方法为校准提供了一种机制性视角，将可靠性与模型内部的可识别结构相联系，而不仅仅将其视为输出层面的问题。在多个LLM上的实验表明，在五个多项选择问答基准上保持准确率的同时，预期校准误差（ECE）、负对数似然（NLL）和Brier分数等校准指标均有一致的改善。这些结果表明，有效的校准不仅需要调整输出，还需要解决模型内部底层的因果机制。
AI.summary: 针对大语言模型频繁出现高置信度错误的问题，本文提出了从机制层面切入的CoCHI框架。该方法通过因果干预识别并调控模型内部导致过度自信的注意力头，在维持多选问答任务准确率的同时，显著提升了模型的校准表现与可靠性。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型, 模型校准, 过度自信, 因果干预, 机制可解释性
AI.comments: 本研究的创新点在于打破了以往仅在模型输出端进行后处理校准的传统思路，从可解释性与因果机制视角出发，精确定位并干预导致过度自信的内部注意力头；其重要性体现在有效提升了LLM在高风险决策场景中的可靠性；局限性在于摘要仅在多选题基准上进行了评估，该方法在开放式生成与长文本任务上的泛化性尚待进一步验证。

title: More Memory, Better Videos? A Controlled Study of Visual Memory in Long-Video Generation
summary: Long-video generators increasingly retrieve past visual observations to prevent identity drift. The intuition is compelling: more access to history should make future video more consistent. But an image can be faithful to the past and wrong for the present. Does visual memory always improve the generated story? We investigate this question through VMem-Bench, a two-track diagnostic study. Track-A measures which references are selected from 92 real films (16,548 segments), before generation and without generator confounds. Track-B compares four retrieval policies with no-memory and gold-informed last-seen controls on 30 causally generated stories (2,824 segments) using a shared generator. Retrieval increases entity recall from 0.559 to 0.628-0.693 and improves similarity to past appearances, but decreases precision from 0.977 to 0.915-0.938 and forbidden-entity avoidance from 0.968 to 0.845-0.898. It can also reinforce obsolete appearances after the story changes them. Conversely, high long-gap recall can arise without memory when the prompt itself supplies the appearance; an appearance-stripping analysis exposes this confound. These results distinguish historical fidelity from current-story correctness and show why retrieval relevance or final-video consistency alone does not establish memory utility.

AI.title_translation: 更多的记忆，更好的视频？长视频生成中视觉记忆的受控研究
AI.tldr: 长视频生成中的视觉记忆检索能提高实体召回率和与过去外观的相似性，但会降低准确性并可能强化过时外观，表明记忆的效用并非总是积极的。
AI.motivation: 长视频生成器越来越多地检索过去的视觉观察以防止身份漂移，但这种做法是否总是能改善生成的故事情节，即更多的历史访问是否能使未来的视频更具一致性，是本研究旨在探究的问题。
AI.method: 本研究通过VMem-Bench，一个双轨诊断研究进行。A轨在生成前且无生成器混淆的情况下，测量了从92部真实电影（16,548个片段）中选择的参考。B轨使用共享生成器，比较了四种检索策略与无记忆和黄金信息最后一次出现控制策略在30个因果生成故事（2,824个片段）上的表现。还进行了外观剥离分析以暴露混淆。
AI.result: 检索将实体召回率从0.559提高到0.628-0.693，并改善了与过去外观的相似性，但将准确率从0.977降低到0.915-0.938，禁止实体回避率从0.968降低到0.845-0.898。它还可能在故事改变外观后强化过时的外观。相反，当提示本身提供外观时，即使没有记忆也能实现高长间隔召回率；外观剥离分析揭示了这一混淆。
AI.conclusion: 本研究区分了历史保真度与当前故事的正确性，并表明单独的检索相关性或最终视频一致性并不能确立记忆的实用性。
AI.translation: 长视频生成器越来越多地检索过去的视觉观察以防止身份漂移。这种直觉引人注目：更多地访问历史应该使未来的视频更具一致性。但是，一张图像可能忠实于过去却与现在不符。视觉记忆总是能改善生成的故事情节吗？我们通过VMem-Bench，一个双轨诊断研究来调查这个问题。A轨在生成前且无生成器混淆的情况下，测量了从92部真实电影（16,548个片段）中选择的参考。B轨使用共享生成器，比较了四种检索策略与无记忆和黄金信息最后一次出现控制策略在30个因果生成故事（2,824个片段）上的表现。检索将实体召回率从0.559提高到0.628-0.693，并改善了与过去外观的相似性，但将准确率从0.977降低到0.915-0.938，禁止实体回避率从0.968降低到0.845-0.898。它还可能在故事改变外观后强化过时的外观。相反，当提示本身提供外观时，即使没有记忆也能实现高长间隔召回率；外观剥离分析揭示了这一混淆。这些结果区分了历史保真度与当前故事的正确性，并表明单独的检索相关性或最终视频一致性并不能确立记忆的实用性。
AI.summary: 本研究通过VMem-Bench诊断性研究，探讨了长视频生成中视觉记忆的效用。结果显示，虽然检索能提高实体召回率和与过去外观的相似性，但会降低生成内容的准确性和禁止实体回避能力，并可能导致强化过时外观的问题。研究强调，历史保真度不等于当前故事的正确性，单纯的检索相关性或视频一致性不足以证明记忆的实用性。
AI.keywords: 视频生成, 视觉记忆, 身份漂移, 检索策略, VMem-Bench
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地挑战了长视频生成中视觉记忆的直观假设，揭示了记忆检索在提高一致性的同时可能引入的负面影响，如降低准确性和强化过时外观。VMem-Bench作为一个诊断性基准，对于理解视觉记忆在复杂视频生成任务中的作用及其局限性具有重要意义，促使未来研究探索更精细的记忆管理策略。

title: DUET4D: Self-Corrective Coupled Guidance for Sparse-View 4D Reconstruction
summary: Sparse-view 4D reconstruction is highly under-constrained when only a few cameras are available. Generative priors can recover missing appearances, but video models are computationally impractical for iterative reconstruction, whereas single-view models produce temporally inconsistent pseudo-observations. Moreover, directly absorbing uncertain generative outputs into Gaussian optimization often creates redundant primitives and floating artifacts. To address these challenges, we propose DUET4D, a self-corrective coupled guidance framework for sparse-view 4D Gaussian splatting. The core of our approach is a self-corrective framework where the 4D representation guides generative prior for spatio-temporal consistent supervisions. We first construct sequential alignments from current Gaussian evidence to steer the latent restoration. Then we use Sequential Fidelity Resampling to lift generative supervisions into Gaussian space to selectively distinguish repeatedly supported primitives. The corrected representation then provides more reliable Gaussian evidence for the next restoration cycle. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUET4D significantly improves rendering quality and rendering efficiency.

AI.title_translation: DUET4D：用于稀疏视角4D重建的自校正耦合引导框架
AI.tldr: DUET4D通过构建4D高斯表征与生成先验的自校正双向耦合引导机制，显著提升了稀疏视角4D动态重建的渲染质量与效率。
AI.motivation: 在相机视角极少时，4D重建严重欠约束。视频生成先验在迭代重建中计算成本过高，单视角模型生成的外观又缺乏时序一致性，且直接将不确定的生成内容用于高斯优化容易产生冗余基元和悬浮伪影。
AI.method: 提出DUET4D自校正耦合引导框架：利用当前高斯证据构建序贯对齐以引导潜在特征恢复；采用序贯保真重采样（Sequential Fidelity Resampling）将生成监督投影到高斯空间，选择性区分得到重复支持的基元；再将校正后的表征反馈为下一恢复周期的更可靠高斯证据。
AI.result: 大量实验证明，DUET4D显著提高了渲染质量与渲染效率。
AI.conclusion: DUET4D通过结合4D表征引导生成先验与序贯保真重采样，构建了自校正的闭环机制，有效解决了稀疏视角4D动态重建中的欠约束与几何伪影问题，兼顾了重建质量与效率。
AI.translation: 当仅有少数相机可用时，稀疏视角4D重建处于高度欠约束状态。生成先验可以恢复缺失的外观信息，但在迭代重建过程中，视频模型的计算开销往往难以承受，而单视角模型又会产生时序不一致的伪观测。此外，直接将具有不确定性的生成结果融入高斯优化中，往往会产生冗余基元和悬浮伪影。为了解决这些挑战，我们提出了DUET4D——一种用于稀疏视角4D高斯溅射（4D Gaussian Splatting）的自校正耦合引导框架。我们方法的核心在于一个自校正框架，其中4D表征引导生成先验以提供具备时空一致性的监督信息。我们首先根据当前的高斯证据构建序贯对齐，以引导潜在空间的恢复；随后利用序贯保真重采样（Sequential Fidelity Resampling）将生成监督提升至高斯空间，选择性地区分受到重复支持的基元。校正后的表征随后为下一个恢复周期提供更加可靠的高斯证据。广泛的实验表明，DUET4D显著提升了渲染质量和渲染效率。
AI.summary: 针对极少视角下4D动态重建欠约束及生成先验利用效率低、伪影多的挑战，本文提出了DUET4D框架。该方法通过4D高斯表征与生成先验相互引导的自校正闭环，结合序贯对齐与序贯保真重采样，在抑制伪影的同时大幅提升了稀疏视角4D重建的渲染质量和效率。
AI.keywords: 稀疏视角4D重建, 4D高斯溅射, 生成先验, 自校正引导, 序贯保真重采样
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地在4D高斯表征与生成先验之间建立了闭环的自校正耦合机制，巧妙缓解了视频先验计算开销过大以及单视角生成先验时序不一致的固有矛盾。通过序贯保真重采样机制过滤不确定的伪观测，有效解决了传统先验引导容易引入悬浮伪影和冗余基元的问题，在稀疏视角动态重建领域具有显著的实用价值。

title: Follow the Regularized Leader Does Not Converge in Constrained Optimization
summary: Follow the regularized leader (FTRL) is a foundational algorithm in online learning whose regret properties have been extensively studied for decades. However, in stark contrast to mirror descent---and gradient descent in particular---the convergence of FTRL to first-order stationary points in constrained nonconvex optimization was not well understood. In this paper, we show that continuous-time FTRL can fail to converge even asymptotically in infinitely smooth constrained optimization problems: its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) gap can remain bounded away from zero indefinitely. This is especially surprising in light of the fact that continuous-time FTRL guarantees a monotonic improvement of the objective value. As a result, we establish that non-convergent behavior of no-regret dynamics---which besets general variational inequality problems---can occur even in potential systems. From a technical standpoint, our construction relies on an infinitely differentiable function where the gradient flow dynamics exhibit decelerating oscillations without ever converging pointwise, which we in turn embed into higher-dimensional FTRL dynamics that sustain a perpetually large KKT gap. We complement our negative result by showing that FTRL with Euclidean regularization does converge when the objective function is analytic. This shows that the analytic property plays a more fundamental role for FTRL than for gradient flow: it governs not only pointwise convergence, but convergence to first-order stationarity itself.

AI.title_translation: 正则化领导者跟踪算法在约束优化中不收敛
AI.tldr: 本文证明了在约束非凸优化中，连续时间FTRL算法即使在无限光滑问题中也可能不收敛到一阶驻点，其KKT间隙可以持续远离零。但当目标函数是解析的时，欧几里得正则化的FTRL可以收敛。
AI.motivation: 尽管FTRL在在线学习中的遗憾性质已被广泛研究，但其在约束非凸优化中收敛到一阶驻点的情况却不甚明了，这与镜像下降法（尤其是梯度下降法）形成了鲜明对比。
AI.method: 通过构建一个无限可微函数，其中梯度流动力学表现出减速振荡但不收敛，并将其嵌入到高维FTRL动力学中，以维持一个持续较大的KKT间隙。此外，通过证明当目标函数是解析时，带有欧几里得正则化的FTRL确实收敛，来补充了其负面结果。
AI.result: 连续时间FTRL在无限光滑的约束优化问题中可能无法收敛，即使渐近地，其KKT间隙也可以无限期地保持远离零。这表明无遗憾动力学的不收敛行为（困扰一般变分不等式问题）甚至可能发生在势系统中。然而，当目标函数是解析的，并且使用欧几里得正则化时，FTRL是收敛的。
AI.conclusion: 解析性质对于FTRL的重要性比对梯度流更为基础：它不仅决定了逐点收敛，还决定了向一阶驻点的收敛本身。
AI.translation: 正则化领导者跟踪（FTRL）是在线学习中的一种基础算法，其遗憾性质已被广泛研究数十年。然而，与镜像下降法——尤其是梯度下降法——形成鲜明对比的是，FTRL在约束非凸优化中收敛到一阶驻点的情况并未得到很好的理解。在本文中，我们证明了连续时间FTRL即使在无限光滑的约束优化问题中也可能无法收敛，甚至渐近地：其Karush-Kuhn-Tucker（KKT）间隙可以无限期地保持远离零。鉴于连续时间FTRL保证了目标值的单调改进，这一点尤其令人惊讶。因此，我们确立了无遗憾动力学的不收敛行为——困扰一般变分不等式问题——甚至可能发生在势系统中。从技术角度来看，我们的构建依赖于一个无限可微函数，其中梯度流动力学表现出减速振荡而从未逐点收敛，我们又将其嵌入到高维FTRL动力学中，以维持一个持续较大的KKT间隙。我们通过证明当目标函数是解析的，并且使用欧几里得正则化时，FTRL确实收敛，来补充了我们的负面结果。这表明解析性质对于FTRL的重要性比对梯度流更为基础：它不仅决定了逐点收敛，还决定了向一阶驻点的收敛本身。
AI.summary: 本文研究了在线学习算法FTRL在约束非凸优化中的收敛性。研究发现，在连续时间设置下，FTRL即使在无限光滑的问题中也可能不收敛到一阶驻点，其KKT间隙可能持续远离零，这揭示了无遗憾动力学在势系统中也可能出现不收敛行为。这一发现通过构造一个具有不收敛梯度流动力学的无限可微函数并将其嵌入FTRL动力学中得到证实。然而，研究也指出，当目标函数是解析的且采用欧几里得正则化时，FTRL能够收敛。这强调了解析性质对于FTRL收敛的重要性，甚至超越了其对梯度流的影响。
AI.keywords: FTRL, 约束优化, 不收敛, KKT间隙, 解析性质
AI.comments: 这项工作提出了一个重要的负面结果，挑战了对FTRL在约束优化中普遍收敛的假设，尤其是在无限光滑但非解析的函数上。这对于理解在线优化算法的局限性及其与传统优化方法的差异具有重要意义。同时，它也指出了解析性这一性质对于确保FTRL收敛的关键作用，为未来的算法设计和理论分析提供了新的方向。

title: Shifted Window Temporal Transformer for YOLO-Guided Phase Recognition in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Surgery
summary: Intelligent operating rooms require accurate awareness of surgical workflow for better intra-operative decisions, teamwork, and surgical documentation. Therefore, accurately recognizing surgical phase during surgery is crucial. However, previous artificial intelligence-based methods provide fluctuating predictions for the transitions, restricting their clinical use. To address this challenge, we propose a clinically meaningful framework that integrates a Swin Transformer and Temporal Transformer Encoder (TTE) for effective surgical phase recognition and a parallel YOLOv11s network for real-time surgical instrument localization. To avoid phase flickering and to produce stable workflow predictions, a causal temporal smoothing is applied. The proposed framework is tested on the Cholec80 dataset for the simultaneous recognition of the surgical phases and instruments. The overall phase recognition accuracy of this model was 92%, and the macro average F1-score was 0.86. This performance surpasses CNN based methods such as EndoNet (81.7%) and SV-RCNet (85.3%), as well as temporal convolutional and transformer-based approaches including TeCNO (88.6%), Trans-SVNet (90.9%), and LoViT (91.5%). Besides, the module of instrument detection achieved mAP@0.5 = 0.863. The reliability of the results is confirmed, obtaining a high recognition rate of the workflows, and a high accuracy of the localization of the instruments. The proposed framework can serve as a foundation for intelligent surgical assistance, enriching situation awareness, and potential robotic surgery applications. Code will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/ac005sheekar/LapChol-Surgery-Swin-Cholec80

AI.title_translation: 用于YOLO引导的腹腔镜胆囊切除手术阶段识别的滑动窗口时间Transformer
AI.tldr: 提出结合Swin Transformer、时间Transformer编码器与YOLOv11s的框架，通过因果时间平滑实现稳定高效的手术阶段识别与器械定位。
AI.motivation: 智能手术室需要精准感知手术工作流，但先前的AI方法在阶段过渡时常出现波动和闪烁预测，限制了其临床应用。
AI.method: 提出一个集成Swin Transformer和时间Transformer编码器（TTE）的手术阶段识别框架，并结合平行的YOLOv11s网络进行实时手术器械定位；同时应用因果时间平滑算法抑制阶段预测闪烁。
AI.result: 在Cholec80数据集上，手术阶段识别总体准确率达92%，宏平均F1分数为0.86，超越了EndoNet、SV-RCNet、TeCNO、Trans-SVNet和LoViT等现有方法；器械检测的mAP@0.5达到0.863。
AI.conclusion: 该框架实现了高准确率的手术工作流识别与器械定位，验证了其可靠性，可作为智能手术辅助、增强态势感知和机器人手术应用的基础。
AI.translation: 智能手术室需要准确感知手术工作流程，以优化术中决策、团队协作和手术记录。因此，在手术过程中准确识别手术阶段至关重要。然而，以往基于人工智能的方法在阶段过渡时预测易产生波动，限制了其临床应用。为了应对这一挑战，我们提出了一个具有临床意义的框架，该框架集成了用于有效识别手术阶段的Swin Transformer和时间Transformer编码器（TTE），以及用于实时手术器械定位的并行YOLOv11s网络。为了避免阶段预测闪烁并生成稳定的工作流预测，模型应用了因果时间平滑技术。所提出的框架在Cholec80数据集上针对手术阶段和器械的同步识别进行了测试。该模型的总体阶段识别准确率达到92%，宏平均F1分数为0.86。该性能超越了基于CNN的方法（如EndoNet为81.7%、SV-RCNet为85.3%），以及基于时间卷积和Transformer的方法（包括TeCNO的88.6%、Trans-SVNet的90.9%和LoViT的91.5%）。此外，器械检测模块的mAP@0.5达到了0.863。结果证实了该方法的可靠性，获得了高工作流识别率和高精度的器械定位。该框架可作为智能手术辅助的基础，增强态势感知，并具备应用于机器人手术的潜力。代码将公开发布在：https://github.com/ac005sheekar/LapChol-Surgery-Swin-Cholec80。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种结合Swin Transformer、时间Transformer编码器（TTE）和YOLOv11s的临床辅助框架，用于腹腔镜胆囊切除术的手术阶段识别与器械检测。通过引入因果时间平滑算法，有效解决了阶段预测闪烁问题，在Cholec80数据集上达到了92%的识别准确率和0.863的器械检测mAP@0.5，显著优于主流方法。
AI.keywords: 腹腔镜胆囊切除术, 手术阶段识别, Swin Transformer, YOLOv11s, 时间平滑
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地将Swin Transformer与时间Transformer编码器结合用于手术阶段识别，并引入YOLOv11s进行器械检测及因果时间平滑技术解决阶段跳变问题；在Cholec80上取得了优异性能，但摘要中未说明两分支间具体的引导融合机制细节，且评估主要局限于单一公开数据集。

title: When the Persona Contradicts the Line: Diagnosing Plan-to-Synthesis Failures in Chain-of-Thought TTS
summary: Chain-of-thought TTS systems rely on language-model planners to translate persona and context into vocal delivery, but it is unclear where this intent is lost when the requested affect conflicts with lexical sentiment. We introduce a bilingual Japanese--English persona--line conflict benchmark in which each item pairs one line with congruent and conflicting personas and pre-declares the expected acoustic direction. We probe this direction in the planner-generated delivery phrase, the planner-written emotion vector, the QwenEmotion-generated vector, and the rendered waveform. Planner outputs are usually direction-correct, while downstream agreement can be substantially lower. Bypassing QwenEmotion provides only modest gains over the full planner-controlled Base. Supervising QwenEmotion raises the direction rate to 75% in Japanese and 84% in English. A learned text-to-latent interface reaches the highest English rate of 89% and the highest Japanese arousal rate of 88%. These results show that learned repair of the plan-to-synthesis interface can recover counter-textual delivery, although its effect differs across languages and acoustic axes.

AI.title_translation: 当人设与台词矛盾时：诊断思维链文本转语音中从规划到合成的失效
AI.tldr: 研究诊断了CoT-TTS在人设与台词冲突时情感意图丢失的问题，发现瓶颈在下游接口，并通过可学习的接口修复显著恢复了反文本的声学表达。
AI.motivation: 思维链TTS依赖语言模型规划器将人设与语境转化为声音表达，但当要求的情感与台词字面情感冲突时，不清楚系统在哪个环节丢失了规划意图。
AI.method: 构建了一个日-英双语人设-台词冲突基准，将台词分别与一致和冲突的人设配对并预设声学方向；沿生成管线（规划短语、规划器情感向量、QwenEmotion向量及渲染波形）对意图方向进行层层探测诊断；并评估了绕过QwenEmotion、监督QwenEmotion以及采用可学习的文本到隐变量接口等修复策略。
AI.result: 规划器输出的声学方向通常是正确的，但下游模块的一致性大幅下降；绕过QwenEmotion增益有限；对QwenEmotion进行监督使日语方向正确率提升至75%，英语提升至84%；学习到的文本到隐变量接口达到了最高的英语正确率（89%）和最高的日语唤醒度正确率（88%）。
AI.conclusion: 通过可学习的接口修复“规划到合成”环节，可以有效恢复与文本语义相冲突的反向情感表达，但该修复在不同语言和声学轴向上的泛化效果存在差异。
AI.translation: 思维链（CoT）文本转语音系统依赖语言模型规划器将人设和语境转化为声音表达，但当要求的情感与台词词汇情绪发生冲突时，该意图在何处丢失尚不清楚。我们提出了一个日-英双语的人设-台词冲突基准，其中每个测试项将同一台词与一致和冲突的人设进行配对，并预先声明预期的声学方向。我们在规划器生成的表达短语、规划器编写的情感向量、QwenEmotion生成的向量以及渲染后的波形中探测了这一方向。规划器的输出通常方向正确，而下游的一致性可能明显更低。绕过QwenEmotion相比于完全由规划器控制的Base基线仅带来微弱的提升。对QwenEmotion进行监督可将方向正确率在日语中提高至75%，在英语中提高至84%。一个经过学习的文本到隐变量接口达到了最高的英语正确率（89%）和最高的日语唤醒度正确率（88%）。这些结果表明，通过学习修复“规划到合成”接口可以恢复反文本的语音表达，尽管其效果在不同语言和声学维度上存在差异。
AI.summary: 本文研究了思维链TTS在人设情感与台词情绪矛盾时意图传递失败的问题，提出了日-英双语冲突基准并定位了失效环节。结果表明失效主要发生在下游合成接口，而采用可学习的文本到隐变量接口修复方案能显著提升反向情感表达的正确率。
AI.keywords: 思维链文本转语音 (Chain-of-thought TTS), 人设与台词冲突 (Persona-line conflict), 规划到合成接口 (Plan-to-synthesis interface), 情感语音合成 (Emotional TTS)
AI.comments: 该研究的创新之处在于系统性地针对CoT-TTS中“人设情感与台词词义冲突”这一复杂场景建立了多语言评估基准，并层层诊断了意图在规划到合成各个阶段的丢失问题；其重要性在于揭示了生成失败的主因在下游接口而非规划端本身，并证明了接口修复的有效性；局限性在于效果在不同语言和声学特征轴上表现不均，且依赖于特定的模型组件。

title: JevVLA: Jev-Inspired Energy-Based Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can select among discrete candidates for pick-and-place manipulation or generate continuous action chunks for motion control. Improving both forms of decision making through a common mechanism while retaining the capabilities of a pretrained policy is an important adaptation problem. Inspired by Jev's structured, probabilistic decision interface, we propose JevVLA, a lightweight energy-based adaptation framework for VLA policies. JevVLA instantiates this inspiration by modeling the relative quality of action proposals: with the base policy frozen, it learns a differentiable scalar energy conditioned on observations, task context, and actions, using execution feedback, expert corrections, or demonstration-derived preferences. JevVLA uses this single learned action preference function in two ways: its values compare discrete candidates, while its action gradients correct continuous actions or guide their generation. Candidate selection and continuous control thus share one trainable decision core. Each benchmark uses independently trained weights and fixed input/output encodings, while retaining the same core network with approximately 80,000 trainable parameters. On the held-out test sets, JevVLA improves task success over the respective matched base-policy controls by 1.28, 2.31, 1.60, 1.52, and 1.28 percentage points on MetaWorld MT50, VIMA, LanguageTable, LIBERO Plus, and CLIPort, respectively. These results support the feasibility of a lightweight, Jev-inspired energy model for adapting both discrete action selection and continuous action guidance. The JevVLA implementation will be open-sourced at https://github.com/ZJU4EmbodiedAI/JevVLA.

AI.title_translation: JevVLA：受Jev启发的视觉-语言-动作策略能量基适配方法
AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为JevVLA的轻量级能量基适配框架，通过统一的动作偏好函数同时优化VLA策略的离散决策与连续控制，在多个机器人操作基准上实现了性能提升。
AI.motivation: 改善视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略中离散候选选择与连续动作生成两种决策形式，并在保留预训练策略能力的同时实现轻量级的高效适配。
AI.method: 提出JevVLA框架，在冻结基础策略的同时，利用执行反馈、专家修正或示范偏好学习一个条件化的可微标量能量函数，其值用于比较离散候选，其动作梯度用于修正或引导连续动作。
AI.result: 在MetaWorld MT50、VIMA、LanguageTable、LIBERO Plus和CLIPort等基准的测试集上，相比对应的基础策略控制，任务成功率分别提升了1.28、2.31、1.60、1.52和1.28个百分点。
AI.conclusion: JevVLA证明了基于轻量级、受Jev启发的能量模型来适配离散动作选择和连续动作引导的可行性与有效性。
AI.translation: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略既可以在抓取和放置操作中从离散候选集中进行选择，也可以为运动控制生成连续的动作块。通过统一的机制改进这两种决策形式，同时保留预训练策略的能力，是一个重要的适配问题。受Jev的结构化概率决策接口启发，我们提出了JevVLA，这是一个用于VLA策略的轻量级能量基适配框架。JevVLA通过对动作提案的相对质量进行建模来实现这一灵感：在冻结基础策略的同时，它利用执行反馈、专家修正或示范派生的偏好，学习一个以观测、任务上下文和动作为条件的可微分标量能量。JevVLA以两种方式使用这个单一的学习动作偏好函数：其值用于比较离散候选，而其动作梯度用于修正连续动作或引导其生成。因此，候选选择和连续控制共享一个可训练的决策核心。每个基准测试使用独立训练的权重和固定的输入/输出编码，同时保留具有约80,000个可训练参数的相同核心网络。在保留的测试集上，JevVLA在MetaWorld MT50、VIMA、LanguageTable、LIBERO Plus和CLIPort上将任务成功率分别比匹配的基础策略控制提高了1.28、2.31、1.60、1.52和1.28个百分点。这些结果支持了使用轻量级的、受Jev启发的能量模型来适配离散动作选择和连续动作引导的可行性。JevVLA的实现将在https://github.com/ZJU4EmbodiedAI/JevVLA开源。
AI.summary: 本文提出了JevVLA，一种受Jev启发的轻量级能量基适配框架，用于优化视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略。该框架通过学习一个统一的动作偏好函数，能够同时支持离散候选选择与连续动作引导，在多个基准测试中显著提升了任务成功率。
AI.keywords: Vision-Language-Action, Energy-Based Adaptation, Policy Adaptation, Embodied AI
AI.comments: 该论文受Jev结构化概率决策接口启发，创新性地提出了JevVLA框架，仅通过约8万个可训练参数即实现了对视觉-语言-动作策略的高效轻量级能量基适配，兼顾了离散候选选择与连续动作引导，在多个主流具身智能基准上取得了性能提升。

title: Critic's Eye: Review-Grounded Graph Reasoning for Long-Form Motif Discovery
summary: Deep narrative understanding requires distinguishing what happens from how it is presented, moving beyond the chronological fabula to decode the sjuzet, the discursive organization through which themes are staged. We study this through the recurrence of literary motifs (blood in Macbeth, for instance), where symbolic significance emerges not from local cues, but through repetition-with-variation across the whole work. We operationalize this setting as Computational Motif Discovery, a transductive task that predicts missing line-motif links using the full narrative structure of a play. We propose Critic's Eye, which models the work as a heterogeneous Narrative Topology Graph and performs discriminative inference over global structural evidence. Critic's Eye achieves 84.8% Hit@5 on our benchmark, nearly quadrupling state-of-the-art proprietary foundation models (Gemini-3-pro-preview, ~22.6%). Our analysis reveals that despite massive scaling, sequence-based models hit a "semantic ceiling", struggling to resolve dispersed dependencies. These findings suggest that explicit structural priors are a far more effective inductive bias than parameter scaling for decoding the complex architecture of long-form literature.

AI.title_translation: 评论之眼：长篇母题发现的评论驱动图推理
AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为 Critic's Eye 的图推理模型用于长篇文学母题发现，其性能接近当前最先进专有大模型的四倍，证明了图结构先验在长文本叙事理解中的巨大优势。
AI.motivation: 深入理解叙事需要区分故事的内容（fabula）和话语的组织（sjuzet），而文学母题的象征意义往往是通过全书的“变体重复”体现的。现有的序列基础模型在处理这种分散的长程依赖时面临“语义上限”，因此需要引入显式的图结构先验。
AI.method: 提出 Critic's Eye 模型，将文学作品建模为异构叙事拓扑图（Heterogeneous Narrative Topology Graph），并在全局结构证据上进行判别式推理。
AI.result: Critic's Eye 在自建基准上达到了 84.8% 的 Hit@5 准确率，几乎是当前最先进的专有基础模型（Gemini-3-pro-preview 的约 22.6%）的四倍。
AI.conclusion: 显式结构先验（如图推理）作为归纳偏置，在解码长篇文学复杂架构时，比单纯的参数规模扩展（Scaling）有效得多。
