With a recursive form for unfairness, we develop \emph{adaptive top-two sampling}, which combines sampling counts and empirical evidence of Pareto membership to define a gain for each arm and guide sampling without committing to an estimated Pareto set. When the Pareto set is stable under small perturbations, we establish an $O(\log T/T)$ and $O(T^{-1})$ bound on expected unfairness and variance, respectively. Information-theoretic lower bounds show that the $\log T/T$ rate can be unavoidable for uniformly fair policies on stable instances, matching our upper bound. More surprisingly, stability is indeed crucial, as the expected unfairness can be $ω(\log T/T)$ without it. Finally, we create a variant that encourages exploration of undersampled arms to reduce the risk of persistent underallocation. At sufficiently large horizons, it preserves the rate on the expected unfairness while admitting a sharper bound of $O(\log^2 T/T^2)$ on variance. Numerical studies support these findings and suggest practical insights.

title: Metric Scale for Insta360 Structure-from-Motion from the Camera's Embedded IMU
summary: Structure-from-motion (SfM) from the dual-fisheye video of a consumer 360-degree camera recovers geometry only up to a similarity transform; in the pipeline considered here, metric scale is obtained from smartphone ARKit or ARCore poses captured alongside the camera. This paper evaluates a self-contained alternative: the IMU embedded in the Insta360 X5 and X6, recorded at 1 kHz. The sensor is characterised (noise density, camera-IMU synchronisation, accelerometer scale factor, bias stability), the camera-IMU rotation and frame timing are estimated from the data, and the scale is recovered by a linear visual-inertial alignment over the SfM poses of a whole survey. The standard formulation, with gravity and accelerometer bias shared across the survey, overestimates the scale by 3.4% on average; estimating each contiguous segment independently and averaging removes the bias. On nine surveys with a co-mounted LiDAR scanner the inertial scale deviates from the LiDAR by 0.74% in mean absolute error, against 1.94% for the smartphone scale; on printed fiducial markers both agree within the 1% uncertainty of the target. On the reference trajectories of thirty sequences of a public benchmark, brought to scales of 1/40, 1 and 40, the estimator recovers the metric scale with a mean error of -0.07% and a standard deviation of 1.28%. On fifty production surveys where the smartphone is the only reference, the two scales agree to a standard deviation of 2.6%, the inertial scale being 0.9% lower on average; the difference does not depend on window construction, grows with the extent of the smartphone anchor, and cannot be attributed to either reference. An ablation over window construction and a comparison with monocular metric-depth networks complete the study.

title: LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers
summary: Looped Transformers increase computation per token by repeatedly applying a shared backbone, offering a way to improve language modeling and downstream task performance at a fixed backbone parameter count. However, each loop depends on the preceding loop, so increasing recurrent depth also increases decoding latency. Existing approaches include Parallel Loop Transformers, which reduce latency by overlapping loop computation across token positions, but yield rapidly diminishing marginal accuracy gains at larger depths. To address this challenge, we introduce LoopFold, which folds computation at multiple recurrent depths into parallel batches for the same token prefix. A lightweight predictor estimates inputs to later loops so they can start before earlier loops finish. A corrector then refines the outputs of these later loops using newly available results from earlier loops. All components are trained jointly using only the final next-token prediction loss. In experiments with 1.4B models, deeper LoopFold configurations achieve progressively higher average zero-shot accuracy across eight tasks, rising from 53.41% to 56.38%. Vanilla looped models and PLT show limited gains over the same depth range. Compared with a nine-loop vanilla model, LoopFold uses five sequential stages and additional parallel computation to reduce decoding latency by 46%.

title: EXCISE: Locating and Excising Distracting Sentences in Medical Question Answering
summary: Language models are increasingly considered for clinical decision support, where their answers should be grounded in clinical evidence and remain robust to irrelevant information. Prior work shows that a single irrelevant sentence can lower the accuracy of medical models, but not where inside the model its effect can be removed, or how to do so without knowing which sentence it is. We find that blocking attention to a known distractor restores the answer, whereas head masking can suppress correct answers. We also show that the model's hidden states mark the distractor as the sentence that least fits the case even when the model follows it. To remove a distractor's effect without knowing which sentence it is, we propose EXCISE, an inference-time method that blocks the sentence most influencing the answer, but only if the model's hidden states mark it as inconsistent with the case. On MedQA-TD (MedQA with Targeted Distractors), a benchmark we construct in which each distractor targets a specific wrong option, EXCISE gains 16.7-22.8 accuracy points at a 1.5-2.1-point cost on the same questions without distractors, outperforming prompting, rewriting, and steering baselines for all three models. Its gains extend to MedDistractQA and BiasMedQA, as well as chain-of-thought generation.

title: Multi-Fidelity Training Reshapes Uncertainty Decomposition in Atomistic Models
summary: Multi-fidelity training, which combines abundant low-fidelity data with scarce high-fidelity labels, is increasingly common in atomistic modeling, but its effect on predictive uncertainty remains largely unexplored. We investigate this question using deep ensembles of mean-variance MACE models trained on ANI-1x, contrasting high-fidelity training from scratch with low-fidelity pretraining followed by fine-tuning. We characterize aleatoric, epistemic, and total uncertainty throughout training and under two distribution shifts: unseen molecular systems and higher-energy configurations. We find that pretraining reduces prediction error and improves uncertainty-based ranking across all test sets, but does not yield well-calibrated predictive variances; calibration deteriorates more severely under energy extrapolation. Training-dynamics analysis localizes most of this calibration degradation to high-fidelity optimization, during which the learned aleatoric variance becomes overconfident on held-out data. Moreover, multi-fidelity fine-tuning produces a more effective uncertainty-based acquisition function than high-fidelity training from scratch. These findings show that uncertainty ranking and calibration capture distinct properties and must be assessed separately in multi-fidelity atomistic models, especially under extrapolation.

title: Beyond Being Accurate: Implications for Using Natural Language Descriptions for Accessible 3D Modeling with~Blind and Low Vision Makers
summary: People who are blind or have low vision (BLV) are largely excluded from 3D modeling tools that rely on visual representations of geometry. Natural language descriptions offer a potential path to accessibility, but it is unclear whether language alone can support the deep spatial understanding that editing, not just browsing, requires. Advances in generative AI offer the promise of automatic model description, yet descriptions suited to BLV modelers are structurally distinct from alt-text and from existing 3D model captioning datasets, and the domain-specific requirements for generating them are not well understood. We address this through two coordinated studies: an autoethnographic pilot in which the blind first author worked with 12 sighted participants to develop a taxonomy of descriptive strategies, and a Wizard-of-Oz main study that applied those strategies as idealized scripts with 10 BLV participants. We identify a systematic use-to-editing gap: descriptions that support accurate but incomplete mental models are insufficient for specifying modifications, because editing requires knowing the state of features the user did not know to ask about. We show that this gap produces four failure types (accuracy, completeness, expression, and navigation) that accuracy-focused evaluation frameworks cannot detect. We propose a two-phase evaluation framework that diagnoses the failure type a description system exhibits and guides developers toward targeted design interventions, thereby providing a methodological standard for assessing whether description-based systems genuinely support BLV modelers as creators.

title: High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable
comments: 58 pages, including 14 pages of main text and 44 pages of supplementary information. 5 main figures and 19 supplementary figures
summary: Experts can master fine hand-object manipulation skills, yet limited conscious perception of rapid tactile interactions hinders their ability to articulate the underlying control mechanisms. Badminton racket control requires rapid, fine hand-force coordination, providing a demanding testbed for uncovering these mechanisms. An 864-node tactile-inertial glove with synchronized 100-Hz acquisition recorded over 14,000 strokes from more than 70 participants across five skills. Inspired by sensorimotor control, our mechanics-grounded two-layer framework inferred object-driving and grip-stabilizing control from tactile history, while resolving their spatiotemporal force realization. We found that higher proficiency was associated with selective rather than extensive control: greater skill specificity, anticipatory regulation, focal distal modulation and lower geometric torque cancellation, while spatiotemporal coordination showed a non-monotonic acquire-refine pattern. We translated these mechanisms into personalized guidance targeting force control and force-motion coordination. In a randomized cohort, mechanism-guided learners gained 0.72 expert-rated skill levels versus 0.05 with level-only feedback, making control mechanisms actionable.
comment: 58 pages, including 14 pages of main text and 44 pages of supplementary information. 5 main figures and 19 supplementary figures

title: A Unified Queueing-Based Framework for Comparative Evaluation of Serverless Autoscaling Strategies under Bursty Workloads
summary: Serverless computing platforms must preserve quality of service (QoS) while adapting to highly bursty and unpredictable workloads. To cope with workload fluctuations while satisfying QoS requirements and service-level agreements (SLAs), these platforms rely on automatic resource scaling. Commercial function-as-a-service (FaaS) platforms employ different autoscaling strategies to dynamically adjust the number of active function instances and the available processing capacity. In this work, three representative autoscaling strategies are modeled and compared: scale-per-request (SPR), concurrencylevel scaling (CLS), and metric-based scaling (MBS). To enable systematic evaluation independent of proprietary platform-specific implementations, we develop a unified modeling framework that combines analytical queueing network (QN) modeling with queueing Petri nets (QPN) implemented in Java Modeling Tools (JMT) to evaluate autoscaling behavior under two-phase hyper-exponential (H2) arrivals. Evaluation is conducted using four system-level metrics: throughput, mean response time, system population, and system power. The framework captures dynamic function instance (FI) activation, concurrency constraints, and queue buildup under saturation. Comparative analysis reveals a clear trade-off between peak performance and stability: SPR provides the lowest delay under moderate load but becomes fragile near capacity limits; CLS is governed by concurrency tokens and is highly sensitive to configuration under bursty conditions; whereas MBS provides the most stable QoS across the workload range by keeping utilization below a critical region and preventing explosive queue growth under critical load.

title: Copying As Defense: Protecting Images from Editing By Eliciting Model Copying
summary: Image editors built on diffusion transformers (DiTs), such as Flux Kontext, make it possible to turn a single photograph into a convincing manipulated image, including harmful and non-consensual edits. Proactive defenses aim to prevent such manipulations by adding an imperceptible perturbation before an image is shared. Existing defenses for DiT-based in-context editors make the output attend less to the protected reference image. But this leaves the model free to follow the edit instruction using the text and its own generated tokens, often producing a new, weakly grounded image rather than preventing the edit. We find that the opposite strategy is more effective: instead of leading the model to ignore the reference, we encourage it to copy it. Through controlled attention interventions, we show that concentrating target-token attention on the reference image in only a few early blocks is sufficient to collapse the editing behavior, causing the model to reproduce its input, often as a lossy copy, rather than execute the requested transformation. Based on this insight, we introduce Copying-as-Defense (CaD), which maximizes per-token target-to-reference attention mass in early transformer blocks. Since attention rows are normalized, increasing reference attention suppresses the attention allocated to the text and generated canvas. Restricting the objective to early blocks also lets us truncate the backpropagation path, keeping optimization cheap. Across editors and benchmarks, CaD reduces average edit success from 81.4% on unprotected images to 24.0%, a 70.6% relative reduction, and by a further 44.3% relative to DeContext, the strongest baseline (43.0%). CaD is also roughly 1.8-2.0x faster per optimization step than comparable methods.

title: ExCal: Optimization-Free Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection via Excess Calibration
comments: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026), Special Session on Intelligent Data Mining. 10 pages, 3 figures, 9 tables
summary: We introduce ExCal, a normal-only multivariate time series anomaly detector that combines raw state retrieval, a signal/derivative subspace, and robust statistics across temporal scales. Each expert map receives a high normality floor from the training prefix. During scoring, positive excess is retained, attenuated for broadly firing maps, and combined with a small rank term. The method fits reference memories and projections without gradient optimization or anomaly labels. Prevalence and ranks depend on the complete scored sequence, making inference batch and transductive rather than online. On 180 series from 17 TSB-AD-M families, ExCal obtains AUC-PR $0.421\pm0.37$ and VUS-PR $0.452\pm0.37$ over three seeds, ranking second among 24 methods. Holm-adjusted paired tests detect no significant difference from AxonAD or StreamVAE, which are the two leading non-pretrained methods on TSB-AD-M, on either primary metric, while finding significant positive differences against the other 21 baselines. A separate single-run probe over three series measures median model-wrapper time of $0.0662$ s. Ablations associate the largest primary-metric changes with raw retrieval and excess-magnitude preservation. The evaluated score is decomposable by expert, but its diagnostic utility and online suitability remain untested.
comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026), Special Session on Intelligent Data Mining. 10 pages, 3 figures, 9 tables

title: Preemptive Instruction Following with Resumption
summary: Long-horizon embodied navigation may be interrupted by a higher-priority instruction before the current task sequence is complete. The agent must finish its current atomic task, execute the inserted task, and resume the remaining sequence from the updated environment state, where its viewpoint and available navigation candidates may have changed. To evaluate this capability, we introduce PIFR benchmark, a novel task for runtime task preemption and resumption in embodied navigation. PIFR includes single, repeated, and nested interruption settings,with stage-specific metrics for inserted-task completion, resumption of the original task, and completion of the full sequence. Evaluations show that recovery performance varies across interruption conditions, while aggregate success can obscure differences in interruption handling and resumption. We further propose a lightweight candidate-ranking baseline to improve target re-grounding after interruption. Together, PIFR and the baseline provide a systematic framework for studying interruption handling and task recovery in long-horizon embodied navigation.

title: Computing ${}_{q+1}{F}_q$ via rational conformal maps
summary: It is well-known that certain Möbius (linear fractional) transformations provide analytic continuation of the Gauss hypergeometric function. These transformations work by exchanging the roles of the three regular singular points and $0$, $1$, and $\infty$ of the Gauss hypergeometric differential equation. Not one of these transformations, however, brings the points $e^{\pm{\rm i}π/3}$ closer to the origin, and convergence in a neighbourhood of these is also troublesome. In this work, we produce a Maclaurin series in optimal complexity after rational conformal mapping that induces pointwise convergence to any ${}_{q+1}F_q$ throughout the cut complex plane $\mathbb{C}\setminus[1,\infty)$. We show that for the optimal parameter values this series converges faster than an approximate mapped Chebyshev series obtained by the ultraspherical spectral method.

title: Infinity Machine: a self-improving AI agent for research
summary: We present the Infinity Machine, a self-improving AI agent that we use for research on problems whose answers aprogram or data can check. Each candidate solution is produced by a full tool-using agent that works for up to an hour in a fresh sandbox; proposers see only a public score, and a private split decides what counts. The harness itself(prompts, tools, skills, playbook, meta agent) is an editable genome, changed only through a kernel-enforced gate with held-out and cost checks. An autonomous mode goes from a plain-text goal to a verified report with no human step: an agent picks an open problem and writes its verifier, the kernel calibrates it, an adversarial agent audits it, and an agent that never sees the verifier re-checks the result. Across fourteen problems in six days, for about $180 of model usage, the system produced four results beyond the published state of the art on catalogued open problems in quantum information: a certified depolarizing-channel threshold point p = 0.064966, a qutrit positivity frontier of 0.2910672, a 44-gate depth-6 Golay state preparation, and a stabilizer-rank bound chi(T^7) <= 10. It also cut SABRE qubit-routing overhead from 68,559 to 12,087 added gates. In hardware, it cut the energy per MAC of an open 8x8 INT8 systolic tile by 77.7% through a full open RTL-to-GDS flow, bit-exact. Three fully autonomous runs ended in honestties with public records; one audit caught a stale record, and one agent-written score pointing the wrong way went unnoticed. We report the failures as carefully: the one self-derived harness generation was rejected on cost, proposers gamed lenient scorers four times, and operator changes were decisive for several results.

title: Hyperspectral Unmixing using a Structured Linear Mixing Model with Additive Spectral Variability
summary: Linear hyperspectral unmixing aims at retrieving pure material spectra present in an observed scene and their associated abundance fractions in each pixel. In most practical situations, hyperspectral images are affected by spectral variability (SV) also known as intra-class variability, which is caused by different physical phenomena including atmospheric effects, intrinsic variability of the pure materials and illumination or topographic changes. Nevertheless, the standard hyperspectral unmixing methods that rely on the Linear Mixing Model (LMM) do not consider these phenomena. Thus, neglecting them will spread errors throughout the linear hyperspectral unmixing process. To avoid this problem, this paper proposes two hyperspectral unmixing algorithms dedicated to a parametric model called Structured Additive Variability LMM (SAV-LMM). This mixing model handles SV in an additive manner by incorporating two terms into the standard LMM. Moreover, the designed algorithms are based on Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) and optimize a cost function which integrates additional penalization accounting for SV. Furthermore, a novel improved initialization scheme, which takes SV into account, is proposed. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for linearly unmixing hyperspectral images with SV compared to the tested state-of-the-art methods.

title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
comments: Submitted to Robotics and Autonomous Systems
summary: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics. As the swarm grows denser, collision avoidance becomes the limiting factor, and the number of safely coexisting robots depends on the formulation of the inter-robot safety constraint. We present a distributed predictive flocking controller in which each robot solves its own nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) problem, optimizing swarm cohesion and alignment costs, inter-robot and obstacle safety, and a task objective, while exchanging only predicted trajectories with local neighbors. Within this generalized controller architecture, solved in real time, we compare six barrier and control-barrier-function (CBF) safety formulations on a digital twin of an open-source vibration-driven bristlebot in a $0.64\,\mathrm{m^2}$ arena. A look-ahead discrete-time CBF performs best overall, with the fewest collisions and the widest inter-robot margins across nearly every swarm size tested. We deploy it on phototaxis, phototactic orbiting, and cohesion without a stimulus tasks, using swarm sizes starting from ten robots and up to the geometric packing limit. The swarm holds well: collisions stay low in small swarms, rising steeply as the packing limit approaches, while coordination and cohesion degrade gently rather than collapsing. The swarm is found not to trade safety for order, keeping both across the confined arena, with local alignment high at every swarm size.
comment: Submitted to Robotics and Autonomous Systems

title: Linear Probes Transfer from Base to Distilled Language Models despite Rotation
summary: Linear probes, classifiers that read a language model's internal activations, are widely used to detect harmful requests. They are cheap to train and run, and an auditor who has trained one would like to reuse it when the model is replaced by a successor rather than retrain it for every release. We test how well probes can be reused. For four base models (Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B) we train a probe on the base model with the XSTest prompt set and apply it, unchanged, to two successors of that base: the DeepSeek-R1 distilled reasoning model and the developer's instruction-tuned chat model. We find that the successors rotate the direction separating unsafe from safe prompts by 17$^\circ$ to 35$^\circ$, yet on XSTest the transferred probe's AUC changes by only $-0.011$ to $+0.027$, and on an independent OR-Bench evaluation, never used for training, by $-0.015$ to $+0.053$. On XSTest, whose safe prompts deliberately contain alarming words, the probes beat a classifier that sees only the prompt text by 0.15 to 0.20 AUC. On the OR-Bench prompts that margin shrinks to 0.03 to 0.20, and the probes flag 29\% to 42\% of prompts that sound harmful but are benign, so part of what they read is the appearance of harm rather than harm itself. A probe trained on a base model can thus be reused, in these families, after distillation and after instruction tuning; how much it reads beyond textual cues depends on the test set.

title: Making the Telemetry Pipeline Measurable: An Edge IoT Testbed and Dataset for End-to-End Latency, Provenance, and Energy-Aware Benchmarking
summary: Edge-centric IoT systems are increasingly evaluated through sensor values or platform features, yet the telemetry pipeline itself, the sequence of sensing, serialization, message mediation, ingestion, and persistence, is rarely released as a measurable object. This limits reproducible benchmarking of timeliness, provenance, and operational cost, especially in early-stage IoT design where real deployments and high-quality open data are often unavailable. I present a measurement-first edge IoT testbed and dataset that elevate timeliness, provenance, and energy to first-class telemetry dimensions. The testbed operationalizes a role-based event-driven architecture with explicit Source-Broker-Aggregator responsibilities and a schema-governed TelemetryMessage envelope (Avro) that embeds correlation identifiers and a uniform, cross-role vocabulary of stage-level timestamps. To trace mediation effects, I extend an MQTT broker (Eclipse Mosquitto) with a plugin that annotates messages with high-precision ingress/egress timestamps. I release the dataset in a dual representation: (i) replayable raw events as compressed Avro streams and (ii) analysis-ready long-format Parquet tables partitioned for efficient query and benchmarking, generated by a deterministic raw-to-tabular transformation pipeline. The contribution is an integrated engineering artifact and dataset built from established components. The demonstration describes one deployment through latency summaries, measurement-context distributions, and energy aggregates; it does not establish a new attribution method or a controlled performance benchmark. By co-releasing heterogeneous telemetry with pipeline timing and energy signals in both replayable and queryable forms, the artifact provides a basis for reproducible exploratory analysis and subsequent benchmarking studies.

title: GEAR: Feature-Based Configuration and Code Generation for Agentic Systems
summary: Engineering multi-agent systems (MAS) requires choosing agents, orchestration strategies, communication mechanisms, reasoning approaches, and memory configurations. These choices depend on framework-specific capabilities and abstractions, requiring developers to learn different APIs when exploring alternative implementations. We present GEAR, an open-source tool for configuring MAS and generating framework-specific implementations from a common specification. GEAR uses a feature-based representation to make configuration options and their constraints explicit, enabling users to validate specifications before code generation. Through connectors for ten agentic frameworks, users generate projects from the same specification and can then inspect reports describing framework-specific adaptations. A preliminary assessment of mapping feasibility identifies translation strategies for 271 of 320 evaluated feature-framework pairs (84.69%). GEAR supports developers prototyping agentic systems and researchers exploring MAS configurations across frameworks. GEAR is available as open-source software at https://github.com/brellsanwouo/gear-framework and a video demo is available at https://youtu.be/iwNi-oC2tCw.

title: SAP-ViT: A Self-Attributing Patch Vision Transformer for Medical Image Classification
summary: Vision Transformer (ViT) classifiers commonly rely on a global classification (CLS) token for image-level prediction, which is poorly aligned with local interpretability requirements in medical imaging. We propose SAP-ViT, a Self-Attributing Patch Vision Transformer that replaces CLS-based classification with direct aggregation of last-layer patch embeddings. This design makes class predictions decomposable into patch-level contributions as part of the forward pass. To encourage concise and readable evidence, SAP-ViT applies sparsity regularization to the patch-weight distribution. Since self-attention mixes information across patch tokens, we further introduce an input-space back-mapping mechanism to estimate which input patches contribute to influential output patch embeddings. We evaluate SAP-ViT qualitatively and quantitatively on multiple medical image classification datasets spanning different imaging modalities. The results show that SAP-ViT maintains strong classification performance while providing consistent and interpretable patch-level explanations across datasets. Ablation results further show that both sparsity regularization and the alignment component of input-space back-mapping contribute to the final explanation quality. Overall, SAP-ViT provides a favorable trade-off between predictive accuracy and interpretability for ViT-based medical image classification.

title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Self-Supervised Representation Forcing for Few-Step Video Generation
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://sotamak1r.github.io/SF2-web/
summary: Few-step distillation is essential for deploying modern video diffusion models. Among existing approaches, Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) has emerged as a highly promising paradigm by achieving strong output-space fidelity without adversarial training, while remaining flexible across various student architectures. We observe, however, that DMD fundamentally relies on an output-space objective, lacking explicit regularization on the model's internal representations. As the distillation step count aggressively shrinks, this output-only supervision becomes insufficient, causing the distilled student to degrade in both fine-grained spatial structures and coherent temporal dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce Self Flow Forcing (SF$^2$), which incorporates a predictive representation loss into the DMD framework without altering its output objective. By providing the student and an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) teacher with heterogeneous noise levels, we establish an information asymmetry. This formulation forces the student to predict the teacher's internal representations from a more corrupted input, effectively integrating self-supervised representation alignment into distribution matching. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SF$^2$ effectively mitigates temporal flickering and consistently improves both spatial fidelity and motion quality. Furthermore, the proposed mechanism is architecture-agnostic - seamlessly supporting both bidirectional and causal models - and requires no external feature extractors, introducing minimal computational overhead.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://sotamak1r.github.io/SF2-web/

title: Agentic Algorithm Design: LLMs that Propose, Formalise, and Prove Runtime Bounds for Evolutionary Algorithms in Lean
comments: A github repository with source code will be published later
summary: LLMs now prove hard theorems in Lean. Can they also design algorithms and prove their correctness and efficiency? LLM-guided design of optimisation heuristics (such as AlphaEvolve) is purely empirical. Automated theorem provers with LLMs prove given statements. So far, there has been little evidence that LLMs can do both: design an algorithm and guarantee its efficiency by a mathematical proof. We present a staged pipeline modelled after research methodology in design and analysis of evolutionary algorithms. The agent proposes black-box optimisation algorithms, and Lean guards filter out flawed designs. The agent then defines a potential function and proves drift bounds that guarantee an expected runtime improvement over the baseline algorithm. At no point in the pipeline are the algorithms compared empirically. The agent generates a black-box optimisation algorithm with expected runtime $O(n^2)$ on a CycleUncover problem, where the classical (1+1) EA needs runtime $e^{Ω(n)}$. The pipeline also designs and analyses a black-box optimisation algorithm for integer-valued submodular minimisation with expected runtime $O(n^{2+2c})$, and it matches the optimal order $O(n^2)$ on LeadingOnes. Across 8 problem classes, 12 of 15 runs with frontier models complete the pipeline with a machine-checked expected-runtime bound. An ablation study shows that removing the staging and asking the agent to zero-shot an algorithmic design with a runtime guarantee leads to a copy of the seeded baseline algorithm (random search) or to incomplete proofs. Our study suggests that machine-checked specifications in Lean can replace empirical evaluation in open-ended algorithm discovery. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of an automated pipeline that designs efficient black-box optimisation algorithms with machine-checked runtime bounds in Lean.

title: Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
summary: Knowledge graphs (KGs) provide reliable external knowledge for multi-hop factual reasoning with large language models (LLMs), yet most KGs in real-world domains such as finance and industry lack question--answer (QA) annotations. Without such annotations, existing methods struggle to improve LLM graph reasoning: training-free agents cannot improve their exploration through interaction; reinforcement learning (RL) agents depend on QA data annotated by humans or synthesized by closed-source models; and training data is typically built offline, so its topology mix is fixed and cannot follow the agent's ability. We propose Evolve on Graph (EoG), a framework that lets an LLM self-evolve its graph reasoning without any QA annotations. Through Graph Self-Play, a single LLM alternates between a Proposer that poses questions and a Solver that answers them. To make questions verifiable, Symbolically Verifiable Topology Synthesis (SVTS) samples reasoning topologies on the KG and executes the corresponding first-order logic queries, yielding topology skeletons with correct and complete answer sets; guided by a skeleton, the Proposer explores the graph to pose a multi-hop question. To let task topologies follow the Solver, a Boundary-Aware Graph Curriculum rewards the Proposer by the Solver's score variance, keeping questions at the Solver's capability boundary so that complex topologies enter training as the Solver improves. On six benchmarks over Freebase, Wikidata, and an industrial KG, EoG consistently outperforms prompting-, retrieval-, and agent-based methods, showing that LLM graph reasoning can improve through self-play without QA annotations. Our code is available at https://github.com/Szy5/EoG

title: Whole-Route Planning of a Memory Bus Between Two BGAs: An Exact Model of Crossings and Layer Changes, Negotiated to DRC-Clean Copper
summary: Routing the bus between a processor and its DRAM remains largely manual in printed circuit board (PCB) design, and published algorithms optimize proxies such as crossing or layer counts. We present a router that plans every lane of a two-layer BGA-to-BGA bus before any copper is laid, and carries the plan to design-rule-clean copper. Its core is an exact constraint-programming model that chooses, for all lanes at once, where each necessary crossing occurs, in what order -- by a rule over every triple of lanes -- and where each lane changes layer, with via room; for the ends it is given, it proves its plan optimal within the model. The model reads naturally as physics: worldlines, frustrated Ising spins and contact forces. A linear program places the lanes in millimeters; the constraints it must violate return to the model as cuts, and audit findings as negotiated congestion prices, until the plan passes an audit against the production router's rules or lays clean. The escapes are chosen by an estimate of the same objective, and differential pairs carry their polarity, with an automatic via crossover where the ends disagree. On an Allwinner H3 and a Zynq-7020, each to a DDR3 device, the router completes every rung of two ladders, of up to 51 nets on the H3 (its whole bus) and 43 on the Zynq, connected and DRC-clean, never with more vias than the human designer (80 against 88 and 62 against 100 at the top rungs) and always with less copper, where the toolkit's production router leaves nets open on four of the ten rungs and Freerouting completes none. On the Zynq board itself it completes 45 of the bus's nets with 70 vias to the designer's 105. On generated buses of three, four and six routing layers every run completes, and every one with a known optimum attains it.

title: RoboDoctor: Training-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Robot Policies
summary: Generalist robot policies and language-model agents provide complementary capabilities, but completing a task also requires adapting their use to the consequences of physical interaction. We study execution as a locus of adaptation: feedback guides the current action and supplies evidence for revising subsequent decisions under fixed model weights. We introduce RoboDoctor, a training-free framework that connects diagnosis, grounded action, and persistent experience across three revision targets. The harness allocates control between policy and agent; intervention determines when to assist while preserving useful policy behavior; and operation refines physical methods through observed effects. Linked experience records retain the reason for a decision, the attempted method, its outcome, and conditions for reuse. On a curated archive of 54 RoboDojo-Sim task entries, RoboDoctor achieves a five-dimension mean score of 57.10, with a native success rate of 49.44%. Recorded interactions illustrate strategy changes, selective correction, and grasp revision. These findings characterize execution-time adaptation in the evaluated system; controlled trials remain necessary to isolate the contribution of cross-episode experience.

title: ArchiveLens: A Generative Spatial Knowledge Framework for Semantic Reconstruction of Historical Maps
summary: Historical maps contain dense morphological and semantic information about past urban environments, but many digitization workflows focus primarily on extracting geometry, and do not capture cartographic semantics such as building use and construction materials. This study introduces ArchiveLens, a generative spatial knowledge framework that operationalizes historical maps as entity-centric, machine-queryable geospatial databases. The pipeline decouples morphological and semantic reconstruction through three stages: tiled YOLOv11-seg instance segmentation for building footprint extraction; deterministic material classification via hue, saturation, and value (HSV)-based color thresholds; and localized attribute parsing using a quantized vision-language model constrained by domain-specific prompts. Extracted entities are integrated into a hybrid Spatial-Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (ST-RAG) architecture that combines dense semantic retrieval with symbolic spatio-temporal filtering and mandatory provenance grounding. Applied to 445 georeferenced Sanborn map sheets of Chicago (1918-1950), the framework achieves high geometric and semantic accuracy. Beyond performance, ArchiveLens advances GIScience by formalizing historical cartography as structured spatial knowledge representation, allowing researchers to query building attributes and compare spatial patterns across map sheets and years.

title: VaLoP: Value Gradient Lookahead and Pullback for Reward-Guided Diffusion
summary: Reward guidance steers a pretrained diffusion or flow model toward images or actions that a reward model prefers, at sampling time and without retraining the model for each reward. It follows the gradient of a value function, the expected reward given the noisy state. The two common estimates of this gradient, gradients through a one-step denoised estimate and learned value models, are least accurate at high noise, where the coarse structure of the sample is decided. Interestingly, we find that both errors are posterior covariances, which grow with the uncertainty about the clean sample, and hence at higher noise. To reduce them, we evaluate the value at a less noisy state, one sampler step ahead, where this uncertainty is smaller, and pull its gradient back to the current state. This lookahead places both estimators at the two ends of one family and reveals that an intermediate lookahead requires one additional term, a correction through the generator. We therefore propose Value Gradient Lookahead and Pullback (VaLoP), which computes this correction with one vector-Jacobian product, and VaLoP-Fast, which amortizes it with a small head that, for text-to-image models, is trained with a single reward and reused for the others. Across various models, rewards, and benchmark datasets, both robustly outperform existing value-gradient guidance on the target reward, VaLoP-Fast at about the cost of learned-value guidance. Both extend to critic-guided robot policies, where VaLoP-Fast attains the highest success rates on LIBERO and RoboCasa.

title: Making Reasoning Visible: Configuration-Aware Diagnostic Modeling for Adaptive Scaffolding in Structured Reasoning Tasks
summary: Modeling the latent, multi-step reasoning processes of learners is a core challenge for adaptive tutoring systems, which often rely on simple right/wrong answers rather than understanding how students think. Instantiated here for grammatical reasoning, this study introduces a diagnostic framework that makes students' step-by-step problem-solving visible by analyzing their action sequences in an interactive learning game. The framework computes five interpretable strategy dimensions (e.g., systematic error correction, random guessing), estimates coordination demand from task structure and behavioral patterns, and classifies reasoning into four distinct states. Analyzing 36,234 interactions from 234 students working on 42 morphosyntactic exercises, we found that reasoning strategies vary primarily by context rather than stable traits (intraclass correlation = 0.14), and students show high persistence in unproductive states; specifically, 74.6% of failures driven by high coordination demand (rather than simple knowledge gaps) are followed by another failure without intervention. Our early warning model predicts validation success with strong accuracy (AUC = 0.826 using strategy patterns alone; 0.902 with additional sequential context) while avoiding circular reliance on current error counts. These findings demonstrate that making latent reasoning processes visible enables earlier, more targeted scaffolding that responds to how students are thinking rather than simply whether they succeed. While demonstrated in language learning, the framework provides a generalizable, interpretable architecture for diagnosing complex, structured reasoning in any domain.

title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models
summary: Expressive robot motion positively impacts human-robot interaction by improving user engagement, likability, or task performance. We present a novel approach to automatically generate and modulate complex, expressive full-body gesture sequences from a multimodal (text, audio, video) context description. Based on a unified mathematical implementation of the Principles of Animation using Dynamic Movement Primitives, we use multimodal foundation models to generate such sequences along with parametric motion variations that are highly context-aware. This method extends the state of the art in terms of flexibility and generality by being interpretable, composable, and working across different robot morphologies. Moreover, we integrate the system into a continuous control framework and leverage knowledge distillation to learn a much smaller model, significantly improving token efficiency and system latency. Results from a user study with a human-like platform indicate that participants judged our system's motions to be better aligned with the interaction context than motions produced under a non-modulated or API-level condition. We also demonstrate how the system generates expressive motion for robots with different kinematics, showcasing its versatility. Paper webpage: https://gen-mod-expressive-motion-behavior.github.io/.

title: Hierarchical Skill Evolution for Coding Agent
summary: Skills provide agents with reusable experience to guide future decisions without modifying the underlying model. However, coding trajectories are often entangled with task- and repository-specific contexts, making it challenging to distill procedural skills that generalize across diverse coding environments. To address this challenge, we present Hierarchical Skill Evolution (HSE), which progressively distills procedural knowledge from coding trajectories through hierarchical evidence aggregation. HSE first extracts task-level evidence from individual trajectories, then aggregates recurring evidence within the same repository to form repository-specific skill candidates, and finally consolidates consistent patterns across repositories into transferable skills across repositories. The evolution is driven by an external writer-evaluator loop that generates and assesses skills while keeping the underlying coding model frozen. The loop externally updates the writer and evaluator policies to improve subsequent skill generation and assessment. This hierarchy progressively filters task-specific details while preserving procedures that generalize across diverse coding environments. Successful trajectories yield reusable guidance for future tasks, while failed trajectories reveal recurring failure modes that guide avoidance and recovery. We evaluate HSE on SWE-bench Verified and DeepSWE, using GLM-5.2 across Pi and Claude Code harnesses and GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8 with Pi. Across both benchmarks, 10 skills evolved solely from SWE-Gym improve coding performance across all evaluated settings, demonstrating transfer across benchmarks, coding models, and agent harnesses. We further evolve the skill library from target-benchmark trajectories without verifier feedback, relying solely on the learned evaluator for candidate assessment and achieving additional gains through benchmark-tailored skills.

AI.title_translation: 面向代码智能体的分层技能演化
AI.tldr: 提出分层技能演化框架（HSE），通过层次化聚合代码轨迹证据提炼通用技能，在无需修改底层模型的情况下实现跨模型与跨环境的性能提升。
AI.motivation: 代码轨迹通常与特定的任务和代码仓库上下文深度耦合，导致难以从中提炼出能够在多样化编程环境中泛化的通用程序性技能。
AI.method: 提出分层技能演化（HSE）方法：首先从单个轨迹中提取任务级证据；然后在同一仓库内聚合重复证据形成仓库级候选技能；最终整合跨仓库的一致模式生成可迁移技能。该过程通过外部编写器-评估器循环驱动，冻结底层代码模型，同时利用成功轨迹提炼正向指导并从失败轨迹中总结避错恢复策略，支持在无需验证器反馈的情况下仅依赖学习到的评估器进一步演化技能库。
AI.result: 在SWE-bench Verified和DeepSWE基准上，仅从SWE-Gym演化出的10个技能在GLM-5.2、GPT-5.5和Opus 4.8等多种模型及Pi、Claude Code不同框架下均提升了编程性能，展现出跨基准、模型和框架的迁移能力；在无验证器反馈下仅靠评估器演化目标基准技能还带来了额外性能提升。
AI.conclusion: HSE通过分层证据聚合有效过滤了任务特定细节，提炼出具有跨环境、跨模型和跨框架泛化能力的程序性技能，显著提升了代码智能体的表现。
AI.translation: 技能为智能体提供了可复用的经验以指导未来的决策，而无需修改底层模型。然而，代码轨迹往往与具体的任务和代码仓库上下文纠缠在一起，使得提炼能在多样化编程环境中泛化的程序性技能极具挑战。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了分层技能演化（HSE），通过分层证据聚合逐步从代码轨迹中提炼程序性知识。HSE首先从单个轨迹中提取任务级证据，然后聚合同一代码仓库内的重复证据以形成仓库特定的候选技能，最后将跨仓库的一致模式整合为跨仓库的可迁移技能。这种演化由外部的编写器-评估器循环驱动，在保持底层代码模型冻结的同时生成并评估技能。该循环通过外部更新编写器和评估器策略来改进后续的技能生成与评估。这一层次结构逐步过滤了特定任务的细节，同时保留了可在不同编程环境中泛化的流程。成功的轨迹为未来的任务提供了可复用的指导，而失败的轨迹则揭示了重复出现的失败模式以指导规避和恢复。我们在SWE-bench Verified和DeepSWE上评估了HSE，在Pi和Claude Code框架下使用了GLM-5.2，并在Pi框架下使用了GPT-5.5和Opus 4.8。在这两个基准测试中，仅从SWE-Gym演化出的10个技能就在所有评估设置下提升了代码性能，展现了跨基准测试、代码模型和智能体框架的迁移能力。我们进一步在没有验证器反馈的情况下，仅依靠学习到的评估器从目标基准轨迹中演化技能库进行候选评估，并通过针对基准定制的技能获得了额外的性能提升。
AI.summary: 本文提出了分层技能演化（HSE）框架，旨在从与特定上下文纠缠的代码轨迹中提炼通用的程序性技能。HSE通过任务级、仓库级到跨仓库级的分层证据聚合与外部编写器-评估器循环，在冻结底层模型的前提下逐步演化出通用指导与避错技能。实验表明，该方法演化出的少量技能可在多种大模型、智能体框架及评测基准上实现通用迁移并持续提升代码解决能力。
AI.keywords: Coding Agent, Hierarchical Skill Evolution, Procedural Skills, SWE-bench, Transferable Skills
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地提出了自底向上的分层聚合机制（任务级-仓库级-跨仓库级），有效解决了代码智能体轨迹与特定上下文高度耦合、难以提炼通用技能的难题。此外，通过外部编写器-评估器循环实现技能演化且无需微调底层基座模型，具有极高的实用性和跨模型/跨框架的迁移泛化能力。

title: Distilling neural networks into equations to predict planetary instability
comments: 32 pages, 15 figures, 3 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/simonalford42/planet_eqs
summary: The problem of predicting when a multi-planet system will become dynamically unstable has defied analytical progress over the past three hundred years. Recent machine learning advances achieve high predictive performance of instability dynamics, but as black-box systems cannot be interpreted to connect to existing scientific understanding. Here we show analytic equations that predict when a multi-planet system will undergo instability. We discover these equations by first training a neural network on a dataset of N-body simulations, and then distilling its latent knowledge into closed-form algebraic expressions. Our two-stage pipeline first learns an interpretable variable basis, then searches for equations using symbolic regression. The resulting equations outperform existing analytic estimates of instability and apply across wide ranges of mass ratios, spacing, and orbital eccentricities. They capture structure in the prediction landscape with a small number of variables amenable to dynamical interpretation. These results demonstrate how symbolic learning can be combined with neural networks to extract scientific insight from complex dynamical systems.

AI.title_translation: 将神经网络提炼成方程以预测行星不稳定性
AI.tldr: 利用神经网络和符号回归将复杂行星系统不稳定性预测模型提炼为可解释的解析方程，并优于现有分析方法。
AI.motivation: 过去三百年预测多行星系统动态不稳定性的问题缺乏分析进展，现有机器学习方法虽预测性能高但缺乏可解释性，无法与现有科学理解联系。
AI.method: 采用两阶段管道：首先在N体模拟数据集上训练神经网络，然后通过符号回归将神经网络的潜在知识提炼成封闭形式的代数表达式，以发现预测行星系统不稳定性的解析方程。
AI.result: 得到的解析方程在广泛的质量比、间距和轨道偏心率范围内优于现有不稳定性分析估计，并用少量变量捕获预测景观的结构，这些变量易于动态解释。
AI.conclusion: 结果表明符号学习可以与神经网络结合，从复杂动力系统中提取科学见解。
AI.translation: 预测多行星系统何时会变得动态不稳定，这个问题在过去三百年中一直未能取得分析进展。最近的机器学习进展在不稳定性动力学预测方面取得了很高的性能，但作为黑箱系统无法被解释以与现有科学理解联系起来。在这里，我们展示了预测多行星系统何时会发生不稳定性的解析方程。我们通过首先在N体模拟数据集上训练神经网络，然后将其潜在知识提炼成封闭形式的代数表达式来发现这些方程。我们的两阶段管道首先学习一个可解释的变量基础，然后使用符号回归搜索方程。由此产生的方程优于现有的不稳定性分析估计，并适用于广泛的质量比、间距和轨道偏心率。它们用少量易于动态解释的变量捕获了预测景观中的结构。这些结果表明，符号学习如何与神经网络结合，从复杂动力系统中提取科学见解。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种将神经网络知识提炼为解析方程的两阶段方法，用于预测多行星系统的动态不稳定性。该方法首先训练神经网络，然后通过符号回归提取可解释的代数表达式。所得方程在预测性能上优于现有分析方法，且具有良好的可解释性，展示了结合符号学习与神经网络提取科学洞察的潜力。
AI.keywords: 行星不稳定性, 神经网络, 符号回归, 解析方程, 动力系统
AI.comments: 这项工作创新性地结合了神经网络的强大预测能力和符号回归的可解释性，解决了行星不稳定性预测长期以来的挑战。其重要性在于将黑箱模型转化为可理解的科学定律，为物理学等领域提供了新的研究范式。

title: Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark: A mechanically annotated dataset for evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction
comments: 34 pages, including 5 pages of Supplementary Methods; 10 main-text figures and 1 supplementary figure
summary: Evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction requires ground truth linking camera motion, surface deformation, material correspondence and image appearance. We introduce the Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark, generated with LumenMorph, an open-source toolkit for creating, annotating and evaluating tubular scenes. The release contains 5,580 RGB images. Its baseline crosses three surface-motion conditions with moving and stationary cameras in six scene families; matched appearance variants cover only moving-camera finite-element actions in four families. Documented public and evaluation interfaces expose camera poses, geometry, depth, deformation fields, persistent material correspondences and discrete finite-element records. Persistent triangle identities and material weights let users track the same surface location across frames and query its three-dimensional trajectory. Separately implemented geometric and mechanical checks assess annotation consistency with the generating models. Structure-from-motion, optical-flow and supplied-geometry displacement-interpolation studies demonstrate how the resource distinguishes registration coverage from geometric accuracy, exposes camera- and surface-motion effects, and tests the benefits and mismatch of mechanical priors. Public readers, evaluation contracts and the configurable generator support reuse and extension. Data integrity, fixed-environment repeatability and retained-prediction score replay have distinct verification scopes. The benchmark provides a controlled synthetic reference without claiming anatomical or clinical realism.
comment: 34 pages, including 5 pages of Supplementary Methods; 10 main-text figures and 1 supplementary figure

AI.title_translation: 合成可变形管状基准：用于评估可变形3D重建的机械标注数据集
AI.tldr: 提出首个针对可变形3D重建的、带有丰富机械标注的合成基准数据集，用于全面评估算法的几何与运动重建性能。
AI.motivation: 评估可变形3D重建算法需要包含相机运动、表面变形、材料对应关系和图像外观的准确真值，但目前缺乏同时具备这些丰富机械标注的高质量基准。
AI.method: 利用开源工具LumenMorph生成包含5,580张RGB图像的Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark，提供相机位姿、几何、深度、变形场、材料对应关系和离散有限元记录等全面标注，并进行了运动、光流和位移插值等基准研究。
AI.result: 基准研究成功展示了该资源如何区分注册覆盖范围与几何准确性、揭示相机与表面运动的影响，并测试机械先验的好处与不匹配性。
AI.conclusion: 论文提出的Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark提供了一个受控的合成参考数据集，包含详细的几何、相机运动和机械标注，能够有效评估可变形3D重建算法的性能。
AI.translation: 评估可变形3D重建需要将相机运动、表面变形、材料对应关系和图像外观联系起来的真实基础。我们推出了合成可变形管状基准（Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark），该基准由LumenMorph生成，这是一个用于创建、标注和评估管状场景的开源工具包。该版本包含5,580张RGB图像。其基线跨越了三种表面运动条件，在六个场景系列中包含运动和静止相机；匹配的外观变体仅涵盖四个系列中移动相机的有限元动作。文档化的公共和评估接口公开了相机位姿、几何形状、深度、变形场、持久材料对应关系和离散有限元记录。持久的三角形标识和材料权重使用户能够跨帧跟踪相同的表面位置并查询其三维轨迹。分别实现的几何和机械检查评估了注释与生成模型的一致性。运动结构恢复、光流和提供的几何位移插值研究展示了该资源如何区分配准覆盖范围与几何精度、暴露相机和表面运动效应，以及测试机械先验的好处和不匹配。公共读取器、评估契约和可配置生成器支持重用和扩展。数据完整性、固定环境可重复性和保留预测分数重放具有不同的验证范围。该基准提供了一个受控的合成参考，而不声称具有解剖学或临床真实感。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark，这是一个通过开源工具LumenMorph生成的机械标注合成数据集，旨在为可变形3D重建算法的评估提供包含精确相机位姿、几何变形和材料对应关系的受控参考基准。
AI.keywords: 可变形3D重建, 合成基准, 机械标注, 表面变形, 3D追踪
AI.comments: 该论文填补了可变形3D重建领域缺少机械标注基准的空白，通过开源工具生成包含丰富物理与几何真值的合成数据集，对于评估和测试算法在处理复杂表面变形时的性能具有重要意义。不过它也明确指出不追求解剖或临床真实感。

title: Adversary Brains: Hypothesis-Based Logical Signatures for Threat Actor Detection with LLMs
summary:
An adversary brain is an LLM-based model of a threat actor's behavior, held as an evolving logical signature: a hypothesis with enough structure that data can test it continuously, without a person re-interpreting it each time. Rather than any single observation, such as an IoC (Indicator of Compromise), it is the arrangement that becomes a detection, or intelligence, mechanism. Where YARA matches a file and Sigma matches a log line, an adversary brain matches the activity pattern of a campaign or threat actor. This is based on an intelligence analysis technique called Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH), which the design lifts from the limitation of a few hypotheses at a time, to thousands, and then also operationalizes it for continuous detection purposes. Language models make the concept, and scale, practical: they turn prose reports into brains, judge matches, and drive the loop that keeps brains current. A partial pattern in a brain can also match a new value, such as a fresh C2 (command and control) domain name, assisting with the discovery of new indicators, and turning unknown unknowns into known unknowns, and potentially into knowns.
  The author would like to thank Ryan Moon for the collaboration, and Sounil Yu, Chris Inglis, Thomas Roccia, Marius Benthin, Israel Grimberg, Michal Kamensky, Justin Borland, Brandon Levene, John Hultquist, and John Bambenek for their feedback and assistance.

AI.title_translation: 对抗者大脑：基于假设的逻辑签名用于使用大型语言模型检测威胁行为者
AI.tldr: “对抗者大脑”是一种基于大型语言模型（LLM）的威胁行为者行为模型，它以不断演变的逻辑签名（即假设）的形式存在，旨在实现威胁行为的持续、自动化检测，并能发现新的攻击指标。
AI.motivation: 传统的检测方法（如IoC、YARA、Sigma）侧重于匹配单一观察或日志行，无法有效识别威胁活动或威胁行为者的复杂活动模式。本研究旨在解决如何实现对威胁行为者行为模式的持续、自动化检测，并克服现有技术在处理大量假设和发现未知威胁方面的局限性。
AI.method: 本研究提出了“对抗者大脑”的概念，它是一个基于大型语言模型（LLM）的威胁行为者行为模型，以不断演变的逻辑签名（即假设）形式存在。这些假设可以被数据持续测试，无需人工每次重新解释。该设计借鉴了“竞争假设分析”（ACH）的情报分析技术，并将其从一次处理少数假设扩展到数千个，并使其可操作化以用于持续检测。LLM负责将散文报告转化为大脑，判断匹配项，并驱动保持大脑更新的循环。
AI.result: 对抗者大脑能够匹配整个攻击活动或威胁行为者的活动模式，而非单一的观察结果。它能协助发现新的指标，例如新的C2（命令和控制）域名，将“未知未知”转化为“已知未知”，并有可能转化为“已知”。
AI.conclusion: 通过利用大型语言模型，“对抗者大脑”提供了一种可扩展且持续的方法，用于通过建模不断演变的逻辑签名来检测复杂的威胁行为者行为，并主动发现新的攻击指标。
AI.translation:
对抗者大脑是一种基于大型语言模型（LLM）的威胁行为者行为模型，它以不断演变的逻辑签名（即假设）的形式存在：一个具有足够结构的假设，数据可以持续测试它，而无需人工每次重新解释。它不是任何单一的观察结果（例如妥协指标IoC），而是这种排列组合成为一种检测或情报机制。YARA匹配文件，Sigma匹配日志行，而对抗者大脑匹配攻击活动或威胁行为者的活动模式。这基于一种名为“竞争假设分析”（ACH）的情报分析技术，该设计将其从一次少数几个假设的限制提升到数千个，并将其操作化以用于持续检测目的。语言模型使这一概念和规模变得实用：它们将散文报告转化为大脑，判断匹配项，并驱动保持大脑更新的循环。大脑中的部分模式也可以匹配新值，例如一个新的C2（命令和控制）域名，从而协助发现新指标，并将未知未知转化为已知未知，并有可能转化为已知。
作者要感谢Ryan Moon的合作，以及Sounil Yu、Chris Inglis、Thomas Roccia、Marius Benthin、Israel Grimberg、Michal Kamensky、Justin Borland、Brandon Levene、John Hultquist和John Bambenek的反馈和协助。
AI.summary: 本论文引入了“对抗者大脑”的概念，这是一个基于大型语言模型（LLM）的威胁行为者行为模型。它将威胁行为建模为不断演变的逻辑签名（即假设），这些假设可以被数据持续测试，从而实现对威胁活动或威胁行为者活动模式的持续、自动化检测。该方法通过扩展和操作化“竞争假设分析”（ACH）技术，克服了传统方法（如IoC、YARA、Sigma）的局限性，能够识别复杂的活动模式，并协助发现新的攻击指标，将未知威胁转化为可操作的情报。
AI.keywords: 对抗者大脑, 大型语言模型, 威胁检测, 逻辑签名, 竞争假设分析
AI.comments: 本文提出了一种创新的威胁检测方法，通过从静态指标转向由大型语言模型驱动的动态、基于假设的模型，显著提升了威胁识别能力。其核心优势在于能够持续适应和检测复杂、不断演变的威胁行为者模式，并具有自动发现新指标的潜力。将竞争假设分析（ACH）技术大规模应用于持续检测，是该方法的亮点之一。

title: Robot-Aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Precise Reaching with Wrist-Camera VLA Policies
summary: Efficient robotic data collection remains a major bottleneck for vision-language-action (VLA) policy learning, especially for tasks requiring accurate end-effector positioning and camera-action alignment. This challenge is particularly severe in electronic-waste disassembly, where robots operate in cluttered assemblies of densely packed, visually similar components. Full digital-twin simulation is difficult because many parts are thin, reflective, or mechanically complex, making accurate object-level meshes and contact models difficult to obtain. In this work, we focus on pre-contact reaching and propose a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based data generation pipeline for wrist-camera VLA adaptation. Our method reconstructs the real workspace with 3DGS and renders diverse wrist-camera observations from robot-aligned poses. These observations are paired with smooth, structured reaching trajectories to provide robot-aligned visual-action supervision for VLA fine-tuning. We further augment the VLA policy with an instruction-conditioned reach verifier that estimates target proximity and provides reliable termination before physical interaction. Experiments in motherboard disassembly demonstrate precise VLA-based reaching using wrist-camera observations alone, without an external side-view camera. With $π$0.5, 1,500 generated trajectories achieve 80.0\% precise-reaching success across three targets, compared with 58.7\% using 150 teleoperated demonstrations, while requiring less than 10 minutes of active human capture. Project website: https://001-wang.github.io/PrecisionReach-GS/

AI.title_translation: 机器人对齐的3D高斯泼溅用于腕部摄像头VLA策略的精确到达
AI.tldr: 本文提出一种基于3D高斯泼溅的数据生成管道，用于腕部摄像头VLA策略的精确到达，解决了机器人数据收集的瓶颈，并在电子垃圾拆卸任务中取得了高成功率和数据效率。
AI.motivation: 机器人数据收集是VLA策略学习的主要瓶颈，尤其对于需要精确末端执行器定位和摄像头-动作对齐的任务。在电子垃圾拆卸等复杂环境中，准确的数字孪生模拟难以实现，因为零件薄、反光或机械复杂。
AI.method: 提出一个基于3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）的数据生成管道，用于腕部摄像头VLA适应。该方法通过3DGS重建真实工作空间，并从机器人对齐的姿态渲染多样化的腕部摄像头观察。这些观察与平滑、结构化的到达轨迹配对，为VLA微调提供机器人对齐的视觉-动作监督。此外，VLA策略通过一个指令条件到达验证器进行增强，该验证器估计目标接近度并在物理交互前提供可靠的终止。
AI.result: 在主板拆卸实验中，仅使用腕部摄像头观察（无需外部侧视摄像头）实现了精确的VLA-based到达。使用1500条生成轨迹，在三个目标上实现了80.0%的精确到达成功率，而使用150次遥操作演示的成功率为58.7%，且所需主动人工捕获时间少于10分钟。
AI.conclusion: 本文提出的方法能够通过生成数据实现精确的VLA-based到达，尤其适用于腕部摄像头设置，显著提高了数据效率和任务成功率，克服了机器人数据收集的挑战。
AI.translation: 机器人数据收集仍然是视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略学习的主要瓶颈，特别是对于需要精确末端执行器定位和摄像头-动作对齐的任务。这一挑战在电子垃圾拆卸中尤为严峻，机器人在此类环境中操作于密集堆积、视觉相似组件的杂乱装配体中。完整的数字孪生模拟难以实现，因为许多零件薄、反光或机械复杂，使得难以获得精确的物体级网格和接触模型。在这项工作中，我们专注于预接触到达，并提出了一种基于3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）的数据生成管道，用于腕部摄像头VLA适应。我们的方法使用3DGS重建真实工作空间，并从机器人对齐的姿态渲染多样化的腕部摄像头观察。这些观察与平滑、结构化的到达轨迹配对，以提供机器人对齐的视觉-动作监督，用于VLA微调。我们通过一个指令条件到达验证器进一步增强了VLA策略，该验证器估计目标接近度并在物理交互前提供可靠的终止。在主板拆卸中的实验表明，仅使用腕部摄像头观察即可实现精确的VLA-based到达，无需外部侧视摄像头。使用1500条生成轨迹，在三个目标上实现了80.0%的精确到达成功率，相比之下，使用150次遥操作演示的成功率为58.7%，同时所需主动人工捕获时间少于10分钟。项目网站：https://001-wang.github.io/PrecisionReach-GS/
AI.summary: 本文针对VLA策略学习中机器人数据收集的瓶颈，特别是在电子垃圾拆卸等复杂场景下，提出了一种基于3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）的数据生成管道。该方法通过3DGS重建真实工作空间并渲染机器人对齐的腕部摄像头观察，结合结构化到达轨迹，为VLA策略提供高效的视觉-动作监督。此外，引入指令条件到达验证器提高精确性。实验证明，该方法在主板拆卸任务中，仅凭腕部摄像头实现了高成功率的精确到达，且显著减少了对人工示教数据的依赖。
AI.keywords: 3D Gaussian Splatting, 机器人抓取, VLA策略, 数据生成, 腕部摄像头
AI.comments: 这项工作通过创新的3D Gaussian Splatting技术生成高质量、机器人对齐的合成数据，有效解决了机器人VLA策略学习中数据收集的痛点，特别是在复杂和对精度要求高的任务（如电子垃圾拆卸）中具有重要意义。其引入的指令条件到达验证器进一步提升了策略的鲁棒性和安全性。这种数据生成范式对于降低机器人学习的门槛和提高效率具有广阔的应用前景。

title: Investigating Forecasting Capabilities of Narrative Networks on Emerging Stories
summary: Networks have been used to model the interactions among the elements that underlie a narrative. In this paper, we investigate whether the structure of these networks can predict which links will emerge as a storyline evolves. We construct these networks from news articles using a Semantic Edge Parser (SEP) built on a Large Language Model (LLM), and evaluate the networks on three disparate real-world storylines, the 2022 Canadian Freedom Convoy, Hurricane Melissa (2025), and the 2025-26 Iranian protests. To test the narrative network's predictive capability, we construct a rolling window of the narrative and predict the emergent links between existing narrative elements on the day following the rolling window period. We identify candidate links with seven standard link predictors, including the Adamic-Adar index, Common Neighbors, and Preferential Attachment. Forecasting next-day links across the three storylines, we find Preferential Attachment to be the strongest standard link predictor, achieving a mean ROC-AUC of 0.76-0.79. It exceeds EdgeBank, a memorization baseline, by 11.3-14.5 points on every event. To summarize, narrative-network structure ranks next-day emergent relations above chance, though this advantage is concentrated among the most frequently mentioned, highly connected entities.

AI.title_translation: 调查叙事网络对新兴故事的预测能力
AI.tldr: 该论文利用大语言模型构建叙事网络，证明了网络结构（特别是通过优先连接方法）能够有效预测新闻事件中次日涌现的关系。
AI.motivation: 探究基于网络建模的叙事结构是否能够预测随着故事情节发展哪些新的链接会涌现出来。
AI.method: 使用基于大语言模型的语义边缘解析器（SEP）从新闻文章中构建叙事网络，利用滑动窗口并在次日应用七种标准链接预测器（如Adamic-Adar、共同邻居、优先连接）以及EdgeBank记忆基线来预测涌现链接。
AI.result: 优先连接（Preferential Attachment）是最强的标准链接预测器，平均ROC-AUC达到0.76-0.79，在每个事件上比EdgeBank基线高出11.3-14.5个百分点；不过这种预测优势主要集中在被提及最频繁、高度连接的实体上。
AI.conclusion: 叙事网络结构能够以显著高于随机水平的准确率预测次日涌现的叙事关系，其中优先连接（Preferential Attachment）表现最好，且明显优于记忆基线。
AI.translation: 网络已被用于建模叙事底层元素之间的交互。在本文中，我们调查了这些网络的结构是否能够预测随着故事情节演化哪些链接会涌现。我们使用构建在大语言模型（LLM）之上的语义边缘解析器（SEP）从新闻文章中构建这些网络，并在三个不同的真实世界故事情节上评估这些网络：2022年加拿大自由车队、梅丽莎飓风（2025年）以及2025-26年伊朗抗议活动。为了测试叙事网络的预测能力，我们构建了叙事的滚动窗口，并预测滚动窗口期后一天现有叙事元素之间涌现的链接。我们用七种标准链接预测器（包括Adamic-Adar指数、共同邻居和优先连接）识别候选链接。通过跨三个故事情节预测次日链接，我们发现优先连接是最强的标准链接预测器，其平均ROC-AUC达到0.76-0.79。它在每个事件上比记忆基线EdgeBank高出11.3-14.5个百分点。综上所述，叙事网络结构将次日涌现的关系排在随机水平之上，尽管这种优势集中在提及最频繁、高度连接的实体之中。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了叙事网络结构在预测新兴新闻故事发展中的能力。通过利用大语言模型从新闻中构建叙事网络，并采用标准链接预测器（如优先连接）在三个真实世界的故事数据集上进行测试，结果表明叙事网络能有效预测次日涌现的叙事关系，且表现优于记忆基线。
AI.keywords: 叙事网络, 链接预测, 大语言模型, 新闻文章, 事件演化
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将大语言模型与网络科学相结合，用于预测叙事（新闻故事）的发展趋势，展示了图结构在社会事件演化预测中的潜力，但预测能力主要集中在高频实体上。

title: From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes
summary: This work explores a multimodal approach to the alignment of the behavior of open-ended learning autonomous robots with human purposes through the use of large language models as cultural enablers. While autonomous robots can generate their own skills and goals through interaction with the environment, they often lack mechanisms to ensure that these remain relevant and aligned to those of human users. The proposed approach makes use of the general and cultural knowledge contained in LLMs and VLMs to establish a multimodal interactive alignment process in which human purposes, expressed in natural language, are transformed into motivational components of a robot architecture in the form of robot missions and drives that guide the behavior of the robot. The system is structured into three layers for semantic alignment, mission generation, and drive modeling. This design enables a bidirectional interaction loop: human inputs define high-level purposes, robots expand them into executable missions making use of multimodal information relayed by LLMs and VLMs, and feedback maintains alignment with human intent. Experiments in simulation and with a physical robot demonstrate that the process produces valid missions and behaviors, supporting effective human-agent alignment in interactive scenarios with autonomous robots.

AI.title_translation: 从语言到驱动：一个多模态框架，用于使自主机器人与人类目的对齐
AI.tldr: 该工作提出了一个多模态框架，利用大型语言模型（LLMs）和视觉语言模型（VLMs）将人类目的（通过自然语言表达）转化为自主机器人的任务和驱动，从而实现机器人行为与人类意图的对齐。
AI.motivation: 自主机器人在与环境互动中可以生成自身的技能和目标，但它们往往缺乏机制来确保这些技能和目标与人类用户的需求保持相关和对齐。
AI.method: 该方法利用LLMs和VLMs中包含的通用和文化知识，建立一个多模态交互对齐过程。人类目的（以自然语言表达）被转化为机器人架构中的激励性组件，即机器人任务和驱动，以指导机器人的行为。该系统分为三个层：语义对齐、任务生成和驱动建模，并支持双向交互循环和反馈机制。
AI.result: 在模拟和物理机器人上的实验表明，该过程产生了有效的任务和行为，支持了自主机器人在交互场景中与人类智能体的有效对齐。
AI.conclusion: 该多模态框架能够有效地将自主机器人的行为与人类目的对齐，通过将自然语言表达的人类意图转化为机器人的任务和驱动，实现了有效的人机对齐。
AI.translation: 这项工作探索了一种多模态方法，通过使用大型语言模型作为文化促成者，使开放式学习自主机器人的行为与人类目的对齐。虽然自主机器人可以通过与环境的互动生成自己的技能和目标，但它们往往缺乏机制来确保这些技能和目标与人类用户的需求保持相关和对齐。所提出的方法利用LLMs和VLMs中包含的通用和文化知识，建立一个多模态交互对齐过程，其中以自然语言表达的人类目的被转化为机器人架构中的激励性组件，即指导机器人行为的机器人任务和驱动。该系统分为语义对齐、任务生成和驱动建模三个层。这种设计实现了双向交互循环：人类输入定义高层目的，机器人利用LLMs和VLMs传递的多模态信息将其扩展为可执行的任务，并通过反馈维持与人类意图的对齐。在模拟和物理机器人上的实验表明，该过程产生了有效的任务和行为，支持了自主机器人在交互场景中与人类智能体的有效对齐。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了一个多模态框架，旨在解决自主机器人行为与人类目的对齐的问题。它利用大型语言模型（LLMs）和视觉语言模型（VLMs）的通用和文化知识，将自然语言表达的人类意图转化为机器人的任务和驱动。该系统采用三层架构，包括语义对齐、任务生成和驱动建模，并设计了双向交互循环以确保持续对齐。实验结果验证了该方法能够生成有效的任务和行为，从而在交互场景中实现人机之间的有效对齐。
AI.keywords: 自主机器人, 人机对齐, 大型语言模型, 多模态框架, 机器人驱动
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于利用大型语言模型和视觉语言模型作为“文化促成者”，将人类抽象的语言目的转化为机器人可执行的具体任务和内在驱动，从而解决了开放式学习机器人与人类意图对齐的关键挑战。其多模态和分层设计提供了一个全面且具有前瞻性的解决方案。

title: Revisiting Direct Control: A Field Evaluation of Sensor Fusion Efficacy in Teleoperating Full-Scale Autonomous Vehicles via Bird's Eye View
comments: Accepted at 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
summary: In autonomous driving, robot teleoperation serves as a critical safety fallback mechanism, requiring operators to assume direct control in the event of system failure. While recent research has pivoted toward high-level supervisory control or simulation-based studies, these approaches often fail to capture the physical dynamics and sensory demands of driving a full-scale vehicle. To address this gap, we evaluated the impact of spatial data representation on operator performance using a real car-sized vehicle in a field experiment with $N = 18$ participants. We compared three visualization interfaces: (i) a standard camera feed baseline, with two bird's-eye views (BEV) from (ii) a raw LiDAR point cloud, and (iii) a sensor fusion of LiDAR and camera data streams. Contrary to prior passive observation studies suggesting that sensor-fusion BEV may hinder awareness, our active-control results demonstrate that such representation significantly outperforms the standard LiDAR BEV in perceived usability ($p \leq 0.0001$) and cognitive task load ($p = 0.01$, NASA-TLX score: 34.58/100) while also being significantly better than the Camera-only view ($p = 0.043$). The fused interface also led to statistically significant reductions in task completion time ($p = 0.0461$) and superior usability (SUS: 77.9/100) compared to those of the Camera-only and LiDAR-only views. By synthesizing objective performance data with comprehensive subjective assessments, we demonstrate that BEV fusion maximizes safety margins while minimizing the operator's mental demand. These findings challenge existing teleoperation conventions and provide an empirically validated approach for designing robust remote piloting systems.
comment: Accepted at 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

AI.title_translation: 重新审视直接控制：通过鸟瞰图远程操作全尺寸自动驾驶汽车的传感器融合效果的现场评估
AI.tldr: 在真实的自动驾驶汽车远程操作场景中，结合了LiDAR和摄像头数据的鸟瞰图（BEV）融合界面，在提高操作员感知可用性、降低认知负荷、缩短任务完成时间和提升整体可用性方面，显著优于仅使用摄像头或仅使用LiDAR的界面。
AI.motivation: 现有研究侧重于高级监督控制或模拟，未能充分考虑全尺寸车辆的物理动态和感官需求，而远程操作是自动驾驶汽车的关键安全后备机制。
AI.method: 在真实的车辆上进行了现场实验，有18名参与者，比较了三种可视化界面：纯摄像头、LiDAR点云鸟瞰图以及LiDAR和摄像头数据融合的鸟瞰图，并评估了操作员的表现。
AI.result: 与仅使用摄像头或仅使用LiDAR的视图相比，传感器融合的鸟瞰图界面在感知可用性、认知任务负荷、任务完成时间和整体可用性方面均表现出显著优势。
AI.conclusion: 鸟瞰图传感器融合能够最大化安全裕度并最小化操作员的精神负荷，这挑战了现有的远程操作惯例，并为设计稳健的远程驾驶系统提供了一种经验证的方法。
AI.translation: 在自动驾驶领域，机器人远程操作作为一种关键的安全后备机制，要求在系统故障时操作员能够直接接管控制。尽管最近的研究已转向高级监督控制或基于仿真的研究，但这些方法往往无法捕捉全尺寸车辆的物理动态和感官需求。为了解决这一差距，我们在一次现场实验中，使用了一辆真实的汽车大小的车辆，对空间数据表示对操作员性能的影响进行了评估，共有 N = 18 名参与者。我们比较了三种可视化界面：(i) 标准摄像头馈送基线，以及两种鸟瞰图 (BEV)，分别来自 (ii) 原始 LiDAR 点云，和 (iii) LiDAR 与摄像头数据流的传感器融合。与先前表明传感器融合 BEV 可能阻碍意识的被动观察研究相反，我们的主动控制结果表明，这种表示方式在感知可用性（p ≤ 0.0001）和认知任务负荷（p = 0.01，NASA-TLX 得分：34.58/100）方面显著优于标准的 LiDAR BEV，并且也显著优于仅摄像头的视图（p = 0.043）。与仅摄像头和仅 LiDAR 视图相比，融合界面在任务完成时间（p = 0.0461）方面也实现了统计学上的显著减少，并在可用性（SUS：77.9/100）方面表现更佳。通过综合客观绩效数据和全面的主观评估，我们证明了 BEV 融合能够最大化安全裕度，同时最小化操作员的精神需求。这些发现挑战了现有的远程操作惯例，并为设计稳健的远程驾驶系统提供了一种经验证的方法。
AI.summary: 这项研究评估了在全尺寸自动驾驶汽车的远程操作中，不同传感器数据可视化方式对操作员性能的影响。通过在真实车辆上的现场实验，研究发现结合了LiDAR和摄像头数据的鸟瞰图（BEV）融合界面，相比纯摄像头或纯LiDAR的视图，能够显著提升操作员的感知可用性、降低认知负荷、缩短任务完成时间，并提供更好的整体可用性。这表明传感器融合的BEV界面是设计更安全、更高效的远程驾驶系统的有效途径。
AI.keywords: 传感器融合, 鸟瞰图, 远程操作, 自动驾驶汽车, 操作员性能
AI.comments: 这项研究通过在真实车辆上进行的现场实验，有力地挑战了仅依赖模拟或被动观察的现有研究范式，为自动驾驶汽车的远程操作提供了重要的实践指导。研究结果强调了传感器融合在鸟瞰图界面中的关键作用，这对于提升操作员在紧急情况下的决策效率和安全性具有重要意义。然而，研究可以进一步探讨不同融合算法、不同传感器配置以及在更复杂交通场景下的表现。

title: Cheap AI-Assisted Reverse Engineering and What It Will Do
summary: Generative AI is putting the law of reverse engineering (RE) under severe strain. Existing IP and technology laws assume that RE is expensive and time-consuming, and that it requires specialized expertise. They generally allow it, but they rely on its difficulty as a filter to separate (permissible) RE from (impermissible) copying and theft. Generative AI is changing this equation by making \RE much faster, cheaper, and easier. AI systems can identify hardware components, extract firmware, decompile object code, and clone entire apps. The resulting struggle between technology vendors and reverse engineers will challenge a wide range of laws, including trade secret, copyright, anti-circumvention, computer misuse, and contract. In this article, we describe the ways in which AI is changing \RE, map these new practices onto existing laws, and sketch ways that the legal system could respond and their associated trade-offs.

AI.title_translation: 廉价的人工智能辅助逆向工程及其影响
AI.tldr: 生成式人工智能正在使逆向工程（RE）变得更快、更便宜、更容易，这对现有的知识产权和技术法律构成了严峻挑战，这些法律通常假设RE是昂贵且耗时的。
AI.motivation: 现有的知识产权和技术法律假设逆向工程（RE）是昂贵且耗时的，并依赖其难度来区分合法的RE和非法的复制与盗窃。然而，生成式人工智能正在改变这一现状，使得RE变得更快、更便宜、更容易，从而对现有法律体系构成挑战。
AI.method: 文章描述了人工智能如何改变RE，将这些新的实践与现有法律进行对比，并概述了法律体系可能的回应及其权衡。
AI.result: 生成式人工智能能够识别硬件组件、提取固件、反编译目标代码和克隆整个应用程序，这使得RE的成本和难度大大降低。
AI.conclusion: 生成式人工智能对逆向工程的改变将挑战包括商业秘密、版权、反规避、计算机滥用和合同在内的广泛法律，需要法律体系做出相应的调整和回应。
AI.translation: 生成式人工智能正使逆向工程（RE）面临严峻挑战。现有的知识产权和技术法律假设RE是昂贵且耗时的，并且需要专门的专业知识。它们通常允许RE，但依赖其难度作为区分（允许的）RE和（不允许的）复制与盗窃的过滤器。生成式AI正在改变这一等式，使e变得更快、更便宜、更容易。AI系统能够识别硬件组件、提取固件、反编译目标代码并克隆整个应用程序。由此产生的技术供应商和逆向工程师之间的斗争将挑战广泛的法律，包括商业秘密、版权、反规避、计算机滥用和合同。在本文中，我们描述了AI改变e的方式，将这些新的实践映射到现有法律上，并勾勒出法律体系可能的回应及其相关的权衡。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了生成式人工智能（AI）如何通过降低成本和复杂性来颠覆传统的逆向工程（RE）实践。文章分析了AI在识别硬件、提取固件、代码反编译和应用程序克隆等方面的能力，并阐述了这些新能力如何挑战现有的知识产权和技术法律框架，这些法律通常基于RE的昂贵和耗时假设。作者进一步将AI驱动的RE实践与商业秘密、版权、反规避、计算机滥用和合同法等领域联系起来，并提出了法律体系可能的回应及其潜在的权衡。
AI.keywords: 生成式AI, 逆向工程, 知识产权法, 法律挑战, 技术发展
AI.comments: 该论文强调了生成式AI对传统逆向工程实践及其法律框架的颠覆性影响。它准确地指出了现有法律在面对AI驱动的低成本、高效率RE时可能面临的挑战。文章的分析框架——描述AI如何改变RE，映射到现有法律，并提出法律回应——是一个清晰且有条理的方法。然而，文章可能可以更深入地探讨具体的法律案例或提出更具体的立法建议，以增强其现实指导意义。总的来说，这是一篇具有前瞻性和重要性的论文，为理解AI时代下的法律挑战提供了有价值的见解。

title: Offline Language-Based Support System for Tactical Decision-Making in Air Combat Operations
comments: Accepted at the LatinX in AI Workshop @ NeurIPS 2025. 7 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables
summary: An offline language-based support tool is presented to assist pilot training and tactical decision-making in air combat operations. The system, named MATE (Mission Assistant for Training and Evaluation), applies retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to answer natural language questions using content extracted from doctrinal and tactical manuals. Built entirely with open-source components, it performs text preprocessing, embedding generation, semantic search, and language generation locally, ensuring full offline functionality. The tool was evaluated by three Brazilian Air Force fighter pilots, who rated the answers produced with three open-weight language models (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 14B, and Mistral NeMo 12B) to five tactical questions derived from a publicly available air combat manual. Average ratings ranged from 4.00 to 4.40 on a five-point scale, with Mistral NeMo 12B obtaining the highest score, and the pilots rated the response time of the tool as fully adequate compared to manual search. The relevance of the retrieved content was identified as the main point for improvement. Potential applications are discussed in onboard mission systems, flight simulators, and training environments.

AI.title_translation: 空战行动中战术决策的离线语言支持系统

title: Adapt for Planning, Not just Prediction: Optimistic Test-Time World Model Adaptation
comments: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Pretrain to Adapt
summary: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this degradation by updating the model during deployment. Unlike pre-training on fixed data, TTA for planning is closed-loop: the planner uses model rollouts to select actions, and the resulting transitions drive the next update. This raises the question: which objective should guide TTA for planning? Under a prediction-only objective, the model is fit only to the outcomes of its own actions, so it can remain wrong about the actions that would reach the goal, and low prediction error need not translate into better planning. Inspired by reward-biased maximum likelihood from adaptive control, we introduce Optimistic Test-Time Adaptation (OpTTA). Its objective has two terms, the prediction loss on observed transitions and the planner's goal-reaching cost on its candidate rollouts, both minimized over the model parameters. The planning term biases adaptation toward models that are optimistic about reaching the goal, without any additional environment interaction. Across visual and environment shifts on manipulation, reaching and navigation tasks, OpTTA raises final planning success over the frozen model by 13.5 percentage points on average, compared with 6.9 for the prediction-only objective (AdaJEPA), when only the predictor is adapted. When the encoder is adapted as well, the gains are 13.5 and 7.5 points. These experiments span three JEPA world models with different encoders and training objectives and, for temporal straightening, both CEM and gradient-based planners. Our results suggest that test-time adaptation of world models for planning benefits from an optimistic, task-aware term in addition to the prediction loss.
comment: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Pretrain to Adapt

AI.title_translation: 为规划而适应，而非仅仅预测：乐观的测试时世界模型适应
AI.tldr: 预训练的潜在世界模型在分布偏移下规划性能下降。本文提出乐观测试时适应（OpTTA），通过引入任务感知和乐观的目标函数，显著提升了测试时的规划成功率。
AI.motivation: 预训练的潜在世界模型在测试时面临分布偏移，导致规划性能下降。传统的测试时适应（TTA）方法，如果只关注预测精度，可能无法有效改善规划，因为低预测误差不一定能转化为更好的目标达成行动。因此，本研究的动机是寻找一个更适合规划的TTA目标函数。
AI.method: 本文引入了乐观测试时适应（OpTTA）方法。其目标函数包含两个项，均在模型参数上进行最小化：1）对观测到的转换的预测损失；2）规划器在其候选推演上的目标达成成本。这个规划项使适应偏向于对达成目标持乐观态度的模型，且无需额外的环境交互。该方法在JEPA世界模型上，结合CEM和基于梯度的规划器进行了实验验证。
AI.result: OpTTA相对于冻结模型，平均将最终规划成功率提高了13.5个百分点，而仅采用预测目标（AdaJEPA）时，提高幅度为6.9个百分点（仅适应预测器）。当编码器也进行适应时，OpTTA的增益为13.5个百分点，而AdaJEPA为7.5个百分点。这些实验结果在视觉和环境偏移、操作、到达和导航任务上，以及三种具有不同编码器和训练目标的JEPA世界模型上均保持一致。
AI.conclusion: 世界模型在规划时的测试时适应，除了预测损失之外，从一个乐观的、任务感知的项中受益匪浅。
AI.translation: 潜在世界模型通常离线预训练并在测试时保持冻结，因此使用它们进行规划在分布偏移下可能会退化。测试时适应（TTA）可以通过在部署期间更新模型来缓解这种退化。与在固定数据上预训练不同，用于规划的TTA是闭环的：规划器使用模型推演来选择行动，由此产生的转换驱动下一次更新。这就提出了一个问题：哪个目标应该指导用于规划的TTA？在仅预测的目标下，模型仅适应其自身行动的结果，因此它可能对能够达到目标的行动保持错误认知，并且低的预测误差不一定能转化为更好的规划。受自适应控制中奖励偏置最大似然的启发，我们引入了乐观测试时适应（OpTTA）。其目标函数包含两项，即观测转换上的预测损失和规划器在其候选推演上的目标达成成本，两者都在模型参数上进行最小化。规划项使适应偏向于对达成目标持乐观态度的模型，而无需任何额外的环境交互。在操作、到达和导航任务的视觉和环境偏移中，OpTTA将最终规划成功率相对于冻结模型平均提高了13.5个百分点，而仅采用预测目标（AdaJEPA）时，提高幅度为6.9个百分点（仅适应预测器）。当编码器也进行适应时，增益分别为13.5和7.5个百分点。这些实验涵盖了三种具有不同编码器和训练目标的JEPA世界模型，以及用于时间校正的CEM和基于梯度的规划器。我们的结果表明，用于规划的世界模型的测试时适应，除了预测损失之外，从一个乐观的、任务感知的项中受益。
AI.summary: 本文旨在解决潜在世界模型在分布偏移下规划性能下降的问题。作者提出了乐观测试时适应（OpTTA）方法，其核心在于结合了预测损失与一个任务感知的规划项，从而使模型在适应过程中偏向于对达成目标持乐观态度。实验结果表明，OpTTA在多种任务和模型架构上，显著优于仅依赖预测损失的适应方法，有效提高了规划成功率。
AI.keywords: 世界模型, 测试时适应, 规划, 乐观适应, 分布偏移
AI.comments: OpTTA的创新之处在于其为测试时适应引入了新颖的目标函数，明确地融入了以规划为中心的乐观偏差。这至关重要，因为仅仅提高预测准确性并不总是能转化为更好的规划结果。通过直接优化达成目标的乐观性，OpTTA提供了一种在部署中更有效地适应世界模型的方法，尤其是在动态或不断变化的环境中。其重要性通过其在性能上显著超越仅预测方法的表现得到强调，突出了适应策略中“预测”与“规划”之间的关键区别。潜在的局限性可能是闭环设置下优化双项目标的计算成本，尽管论文声称无需额外的环境交互。

title: SeeRF: Learning to See Beyond Fields of View via Generative Image Registration and Fusion
summary: Due to the inherent discrepancies in imaging viewpoints and field-of-view mismatches among multi-modal sensors, existing fusion methods have long struggled to achieve complete scene-level information integration beyond the limitation in sensor fields of view. Consequently, the generated fusion results often contain modality-specific regions and fusion artifacts, limiting the comprehensive representation of scene structures and semantic information. To address this challenge, we propose a generative registration-fusion framework, termed SeeRF. Specifically, it first introduces a deformation generation strategy based on the diffeomorphic stationary velocity field, combined with visual foundation model-guided feature extraction and a coarse-to-fine progressive multi-modal image registration module, to achieve accurate cross-modal flow estimation and generate valid field-of-view masks. Subsequently, the registration module is tightly coupled with the generative diffusion module for multi-modal completion and fusion, where the cross-modal control encoding module and the control residual feature encoder-decoder mechanism provide effective guidance. By leveraging the powerful prior modeling capability of generative diffusion models, the proposed framework overcomes the limitations imposed by shared fields of view and enables effective completion and natural fusion of non-overlapping field-of-view regions. Extensive experiments on multiple public datasets and real-world scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance, validating its effectiveness, superiority, and robustness. The code will be available at https://github.com/XunpengYi/SeeRF.

AI.title_translation: SeeRF：通过生成式图像配准与融合实现超越视野的感知
AI.tldr: SeeRF是一个生成式配准-融合框架，通过变形生成、视觉基础模型引导的特征提取和多模态配准，结合生成扩散模型进行多模态补全和融合，以克服多模态传感器视野不匹配的问题，实现超越共享视野的完整场景信息整合。
AI.motivation: 现有融合方法因成像视点差异和多模态传感器视野不匹配，难以实现超越传感器视野限制的完整场景级信息整合，导致融合结果包含特定模态区域和融合伪影，限制了场景结构和语义信息的全面表示。
AI.method: 提出SeeRF，一个生成式配准-融合框架。它首先引入基于微分同胚平稳速度场的变形生成策略，结合视觉基础模型引导的特征提取和从粗到精的渐进式多模态图像配准模块，实现精确的跨模态流估计和有效视野掩码生成。随后，配准模块与生成扩散模块紧密耦合进行多模态补全和融合，其中跨模态控制编码模块和控制残差特征编解码器机制提供有效指导。
AI.result: 在多个公共数据集和真实世界场景上的广泛实验表明，所提出的方法取得了卓越的性能，验证了其有效性、优越性和鲁棒性。
AI.conclusion: 通过利用生成扩散模型强大的先验建模能力，SeeRF框架克服了共享视野的限制，实现了对非重叠视野区域的有效补全和自然融合。
