AI.title_translation: 紧凑型基础模型用于洪水期间地表水映射的准确性与效率
AI.tldr: 紧凑型预训练地球观测基础模型在洪水映射中无法持续超越传统U-Net模型的准确性，但在计算效率上表现更佳。
AI.motivation: 评估预训练地球观测模型（如Prithvi-EO-2.0-Tiny）在洪水地表水映射中的实际价值，明确其相比于传统模型（如U-Net和光谱指数阈值）在准确性和效率上的优劣。
AI.method: 使用Sen1Floods11数据集中的446个手动标注Sentinel-2影像块，对比了微调模型、冻结编码器模型、随机初始化架构、同尺寸U-Net、较大Prithvi模型以及光谱指数阈值，通过改变训练样本数量、事件排除实验来评估预测准确性、计算成本和预测可靠性。
AI.result: 使用252个训练影像块时，U-Net的水体IoU为0.856，而微调后的Prithvi-Tiny为0.833；在事件排除评估中，微调Prithvi-Tiny的平均IoU为0.768，U-Net为0.777。然而，Prithvi-Tiny的计算效率更高（GPU上处理512x512影像块耗时16.1毫秒，CPU耗时258毫秒，优于U-Net）。预训练相比随机初始化有性能提升，但未能超越U-Net排名。
AI.conclusion: 紧凑型预训练基础模型（如Prithvi-Tiny）无法在洪水映射中实现对传统U-Net的持续超越，但它们在保持竞争力的准确性的同时，提供了更低的计算需求。
AI.translation: 预训练的地球观测模型可能会减少映射地表水所需的工作量，但它们的价值取决于与其进行比较的替代方案。我们使用Sen1Floods11中来自11次洪水事件的446个手动标注的Sentinel-2影像块，对Prithvi-EO-2.0-Tiny进行了评估。将微调模型、冻结编码器模型和相同的随机初始化架构与同等大小的U-Net、更大的Prithvi模型以及光谱指数阈值进行了比较。实验改变了训练影像块的数量，从模型拟合中排除了部分事件，并测量了计算成本和预测可靠性。在有252个训练影像块的情况下，U-Net在官方测试集上实现了0.856的水体交并比（IoU），而微调后的Prithvi-Tiny为0.833。在有25个训练影像块时，预训练使微调的微型Transformer比随机初始化提高了0.046的IoU，在252个影像块时提高了0.023，但并未扭转U-Net的排名。在11次事件排除评估中，微调后的Prithvi-Tiny的平均IoU为0.768，U-Net为0.777；配对区间包含零。微调后的Prithvi-Tiny在GPU上处理512x512像素影像块耗时16.1毫秒，在笔记本电脑CPU上耗时258毫秒，而U-Net分别为30.6毫秒和665毫秒。误差主要集中在水体边界附近，高预测熵识别出了许多（但不是全部）错误像素。这些结果支持了紧凑型预训练模型的特定角色：更低的计算需求和具有竞争力的准确性，而非持续的优越性。事件相关性能、共享超参数选择以及观测水体与新淹没土地之间的区别限定了这些结论。
AI.summary: 该论文评估了紧凑型地球观测基础模型（Prithvi-EO-2.0-Tiny）在洪水地表水映射中的准确性与计算效率。研究表明，尽管预训练紧凑模型展现出更低的计算需求，但其精度并未持续优于同尺寸的传统U-Net模型，主要在计算效率上具有优势。
AI.keywords: 基础模型, 洪水映射, 地球观测, U-Net, 精度与效率
AI.comments: 该论文对紧凑型基础模型（Prithvi-EO-2.0-Tiny）在洪水地表水映射中的准确性和效率进行了严谨的基准测试。其创新之处在于跳出了“基础模型必然优于传统模型”的思维定势，通过与传统U-Net和光谱指数阈值的全面对比，客观指出预训练紧凑模型在精度上并未显著超越精心训练的同尺寸U-Net，但展现出更低的计算需求。这为资源受限场景下地球观测基础模型的落地应用提供了重要的实证参考。

title: Explicit Globally Asymptotically Stable Attitude Control with Reaction Wheel Angular Momentum and Torque Constraints
comments: Preprint accepted in CDC 2026 for presentation
summary: We present an explicit Lyapunov attitude controller for rigid spacecraft actuated by three orthogonally mounted reaction wheels, parameterized using Modified Rodrigues Parameters (MRPs), which enforces hard bounds on wheel angular momentum and applied torque at every instant without solving any online optimization. A barrier-inspired momentum feedback prevents wheel saturation; a continuous positive scalar uniformly scales the feedback whenever a torque limit would otherwise be breached, preserving Lyapunov convergence. For the regulation problem, global asymptotic stability (GAS) is established via LaSalle's invariance principle, and constraint satisfaction is proved analytically for arbitrary symmetric positive-definite inertia matrices. Replacing the barrier by an error-state counterpart extends the design to tracking, with asymptotic (though no longer global) stability and the same safety guarantees under explicit feasibility conditions on the reference. Simulations confirm convergence and constraint satisfaction, and compare performance against other controllers.
comment: Preprint accepted in CDC 2026 for presentation

AI.title_translation: 带有反应轮角动量和力矩约束的显式全局渐近稳定姿态控制
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种无需在线优化、能严格满足反应轮角动量和力矩硬约束的显式姿态控制器，并证明了其全局渐近稳定性。
AI.motivation: 为了解决刚性航天器在反应轮角动量和施加力矩存在硬约束的情况下的显式姿态控制问题，避免复杂的在线优化计算。
AI.method: 采用修正罗德里格斯参数（MRPs）参数化，利用基于势垒的动量反馈防止饱和，并通过连续正标量在接近力矩极限时均匀缩放反馈，结合LaSalle不变性原理证明稳定性。
AI.result: 对于调节问题，建立了全局渐近稳定性（GAS），并在任意对称正定惯性矩阵下证明了约束满足性；通过引入误差状态对应项，设计扩展到了跟踪问题，在显式可行性条件下保持了渐近稳定性和安全性。
AI.conclusion: 本文成功开发了一种满足力矩和动量约束的显式姿态控制器，不仅实现了调节问题的全局渐近稳定性，还通过修改设计扩展到了轨迹跟踪问题。
AI.translation: 我们提出了一种用于由三个正交安装的反应轮驱动的刚性航天器的显式Lyapunov姿态控制器，该控制器使用修正罗德里格斯参数（MRPs）进行参数化，在每个瞬间强制对轮角动量和施加力矩施加硬界限，而无需求解任何在线优化问题。受势垒启发的动量反馈防止了轮饱和；每当力矩极限将被违反时，连续的正标量均匀缩放反馈，从而保持Lyapunov收敛性。对于调节问题，通过LaSalle不变性原理建立了全局渐近稳定性（GAS），并对任意对称正定惯性矩阵解析证明了约束满足性。用误差状态对应项代替势垒，将设计扩展到跟踪，在对参考的显式可行性条件下具有渐近（虽然不再是全局）稳定性和相同的安全保证。仿真验证了收敛性和约束满足性，并与其他控制器进行了性能比较。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了一种针对刚性航天器的显式Lyapunov姿态控制器，利用修正罗德里格斯参数（MRPs），在无需在线优化的情况下，实现了对反应轮角动量和力矩硬约束的严格满足。对于调节问题，证明了全局渐近稳定性，并通过修改设计将其扩展到了满足安全保证的参考轨迹跟踪问题。
AI.keywords: 姿态控制, 反应轮, 全局渐近稳定性, 约束满足, 修正罗德里格斯参数
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地提出了一种显式的Lyapunov姿态控制器，能够在不进行在线优化的情况下，严格满足反应轮的角动量和力矩硬约束，同时保证全局渐近稳定性，对航天器姿态控制具有较高的理论和工程应用价值。

title: Reinforcement learning for constrained stochastic linear--quadratic control in continuous time
summary: We study continuous-time stochastic linear--quadratic control with a scalar state and nonnegative control constraints. With quadratic running costs, randomized exploration can change the optimal mean feedback. We introduce an auxiliary problem without entropy in which the conditional policy mean is nonnegative and the covariance is prescribed in proportion to the squared state. Moment reduction and state separation yield two regional Riccati equations and characterize the finite-horizon value function and optimal conditional mean. We give a sufficient control--cost compatibility condition under which this mean coincides with the optimal feedback of the original constrained problem. For time-invariant coefficients, we characterize the undiscounted infinite-horizon optimum and establish mean square asymptotic stability under the stated assumptions. For unknown dynamics, we develop model-free actor--critic schemes for finite and infinite horizons. Numerical experiments compare the learned policies with their analytical targets and examine the effect of exploration on the optimal mean.

AI.title_translation: 连续时间约束随机线性二次控制的强化学习
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一个解决连续时间随机线性二次控制问题的强化学习方法，该问题具有非负控制约束。通过引入一个辅助问题并利用矩量归约和状态分离，推导出了区域Riccati方程，并表征了有限时间范围内的价值函数和最优条件均值。在满足一定的控制-成本兼容性条件下，该均值与原始约束问题的最优反馈一致。对于未知动力学，研究开发了模型无关的Actor-Critic算法。数值实验验证了所学策略的有效性。
AI.motivation: 研究连续时间随机线性二次控制问题，特别是包含非负控制约束的情况，并探索随机探索对最优均值反馈的影响。
AI.method: 引入一个无熵的辅助问题，其中条件策略均值非负且协方差与状态平方成比例。利用矩量归约和状态分离推导出两个区域Riccati方程，并表征有限时间范围内的价值函数和最优条件均值。推导了控制-成本兼容性条件，以确保辅助问题的最优均值等于原始约束问题的最优反馈。对于未知动力学，开发了模型无关的Actor-Critic算法。
AI.result: 推导出了两个区域Riccati方程，并表征了有限时间范围内的价值函数和最优条件均值。在满足特定条件下，得出了原始约束问题的最优反馈。对于时间不变系数，表征了无折扣无限时间范围的最优解，并证明了在给定假设下的均方渐近稳定性。模型无关的Actor-Critic算法在数值实验中得到了验证，并与分析目标进行了比较。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的方法能够有效地解决连续时间随机线性二次控制问题，即使在存在非负控制约束的情况下。通过引入辅助问题和利用特定的数学技术，可以找到最优的条件均值反馈。对于未知动力学，模型无关的Actor-Critic算法也表现出潜力。
AI.translation: 我们研究了具有标量状态和非负控制约束的连续时间随机线性二次控制。对于二次运行成本，随机探索可以改变最优均值反馈。我们引入了一个没有熵的辅助问题，其中条件策略均值非负，协方差与状态平方成比例。矩量归约和状态分离产生了两个区域Riccati方程，并表征了有限时间范围内的价值函数和最优条件均值。我们给出了一个充分的控制-成本兼容性条件，在该条件下，该均值与原始约束问题的最优反馈一致。对于时间不变系数，我们表征了无折扣无限时间范围的最优解，并在给定假设下建立了均方渐近稳定性。对于未知动力学，我们开发了有限和无限时间范围的模型无关Actor-Critic方案。数值实验比较了学习到的策略与其分析目标，并考察了探索对最优均值的影响。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种用于解决连续时间随机线性二次控制问题的强化学习方法，该问题具有非负控制约束。通过引入一个辅助问题，并利用矩量归约和状态分离技术，推导出了区域Riccati方程，从而表征了有限时间范围内的价值函数和最优条件均值。在满足一定的控制-成本兼容性条件下，该方法得到的最优均值反馈与原始约束问题的最优反馈一致。此外，研究还为未知动力学开发了模型无关的Actor-Critic算法，并通过数值实验验证了该方法的有效性。
AI.keywords: 随机线性二次控制, 强化学习, 非负控制约束, Actor-Critic, 区域Riccati方程
AI.comments: 该研究在理论和实践上都具有重要意义。理论上，它为解决具有约束的随机控制问题提供了一种新的视角和方法。实践上，模型无关的Actor-Critic算法为处理现实世界中动力学未知的问题提供了解决方案。然而，算法的计算复杂度和收敛性仍需进一步研究。

title: Inverse heat source problem from terminal data on a set of low Hausdorff dimension
summary: We study the recovery of a spatial source in the heat equation from terminal observations on a compact interior set $E$ with positive $β$ dimensional Hausdorff content for some $β>d-1$. The prescribed temporal forcing vanishes on a nontrivial interval immediately preceding the observation time. Under a spectral Sobolev prior and a quantitative noncancellation condition on the terminal spectral multipliers, we establish conditional logarithmic stability. For scattered observations on such sets, we derive a sampling inequality under a quasi uniformity assumption. Under explicit sampling and independent noise assumptions, we prove a logarithmic convergence rate in probability for the corresponding Tikhonov reconstructions with a data driven parameter choice. Two numerical experiments using a finite candidate approximation of a fixed Hausdorff set assess discrete spectral sampling stability and illustrate the effects of the waiting interval and measurement noise on reconstruction.

AI.title_translation: 从具有低Hausdorff维数的集合上的终端数据反演热源问题
AI.tldr: 该研究解决了从终端观测数据中恢复热方程空间源的问题，特别关注具有低Hausdorff维数的观测集。研究人员提出了条件对数稳定性，并推导了采样不等式和概率收敛速率，验证了Tikhonov重建方法的有效性，并通过数值实验进行了评估。
AI.motivation: 从终端观测数据中恢复热方程中的空间源，特别是在具有低Hausdorff维数的观测集上的情况。
AI.method: 研究人员提出了条件对数稳定性，并推导了采样不等式和概率收敛速率。他们使用了谱Sobolev先验和定量非取消条件，并对Tikhonov重建方法进行了数据驱动的参数选择。通过有限候选近似和固定Hausdorff集进行了两次数值实验。
AI.result: 建立了条件对数稳定性，并证明了在特定假设下，Tikhonov重建方法的对数收敛速率（以概率论）。数值实验评估了离散谱采样稳定性的影响，并说明了等待时间和测量噪声对重建的影响。
AI.conclusion: 该研究为从低Hausdorff维数观测集恢复热源问题提供了理论基础和数值验证，表明所提出的方法在处理这类具有挑战性的逆问题时是有效的。
AI.translation: 我们研究了从具有正β维Hausdorff内容的紧凑内部集合E上的终端观测来恢复热方程中的空间源，其中β>d-1。规定的时间强迫在观测时间之前的非平凡区间上消失。在谱Sobolev先验和终端谱乘子的定量非取消条件下，我们建立了条件对数稳定性。对于这类集合上的分散观测，我们在准均匀性假设下推导了采样不等式。在明确的采样和独立噪声假设下，我们证明了相应Tikhonov重建方法在数据驱动参数选择下的概率对数收敛速率。使用固定Hausdorff集的有限候选近似进行的两次数值实验评估了离散谱采样稳定性的影响，并说明了等待区间和测量噪声对重建的影响。
AI.summary: 本研究探讨了如何从具有特定Hausdorff维数（β>d-1）的紧凑内部集合E上的终端观测数据中恢复热方程的空间源。研究人员在谱Sobolev先验和定量非取消条件下，建立了条件对数稳定性。此外，他们还推导了在准均匀性假设下针对分散观测的采样不等式，并证明了在明确采样和独立噪声假设下，数据驱动参数选择的Tikhonov重建方法具有概率对数收敛速率。最后，通过数值实验评估了该方法的稳定性和噪声、等待时间等因素的影响。
AI.keywords: 逆热源问题, 终端数据, 低Hausdorff维数, 条件对数稳定性, Tikhonov重建
AI.comments: 该研究在处理具有低Hausdorff维数观测集的逆问题方面取得了重要进展，为实际应用提供了理论支持。然而，实际应用中Hausdorff维数的确定以及噪声模型的选择仍是挑战。

title: From Single Spins to Ensembles: A Calibrated Symbolic Regression Pipeline for NV Spectroscopy
summary: Characterizing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensembles requires connecting their collective spectra to individual centers that experience different local environments. We develop a symbolic-regression pipeline that carries single-center spin structure into a calibrated ensemble model by generating individual spectral responses and combining them with explicit weights. A constrained search selects Hermitian operator terms from single-center optically detected magnetic resonance spectra, fits their coefficients, and retains the selected expressions as source models for the ensemble. Ensemble calibration then accounts for resonance shifts, local disorder, orientation, and optical response while keeping the individual spectral contributions accessible. On public single-center and ensemble data, the zero-field ensemble held-frequency root-mean-square error decreases from 0.008835 to 0.003872 in normalized photoluminescence, a 56.2% improvement over matched uncorrected composition. In controlled QuTiP ensembles of 128 sites spanning four NV orientations, models calibrated at 0 and 3 mT predict an independently held-out 5.17 mT spectrum with errors of 0.000207-0.000228 across three random seeds, comparable to the 0.000200 noise standard deviation. Resolving the simulated response into its individual-center contributions shows how local spectral diversity combines into the ensemble line shape. By retaining the source Hamiltonians while calibrating sample-dependent spectral differences, the pipeline connects local spin physics to collective optical readout and makes the contributions to an ensemble line shape available for physical interpretation.

AI.title_translation: 从单自旋到系综：用于NV光谱的校准符号回归管道
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种符号回归管道，将单中心自旋结构校准到系综模型中，通过生成个体光谱响应并结合权重来连接集体光谱与个体中心，实现了系综模型性能的大幅提升，并能解析个体中心对系综线形状的贡献。
AI.motivation: 连接氮-空位（NV）系综的集体光谱与其经历不同局部环境的个体中心。
AI.method: 开发了一个符号回归管道，该管道将单中心自旋结构映射到校准的系综模型中。它通过生成个体光谱响应并明确地结合权重来工作。通过约束搜索从单中心光学检测的磁共振光谱中选择厄米算符项，拟合其系数，并将所选表达式作为系综的源模型。系综校准考虑了共振位移、局部无序、方向和光学响应，同时保持个体光谱贡献的可及性。
AI.result: 在公开的单中心和系综数据上，零场系综持有频率的均方根误差从0.008835降低到0.003872（归一化光致发光），比匹配的未校正组合提高了56.2%。在控制的QuTiP系综（128个位点，跨越4个NV方向）中，在0和3 mT下校准的模型，能够以0.000207-0.000228的误差预测一个独立保持的5.17 mT光谱，这与0.000200的噪声标准差相当。将模拟响应分解为个体中心贡献，显示了局部的光谱多样性如何组合成系综线形状。
AI.conclusion: 通过在校准样本依赖的光谱差异的同时保留源哈密顿量，该管道能够将局域自旋物理学与集体光学读数联系起来，并使系综线形状的贡献可用于物理解释。
AI.translation: 连接氮-空位（NV）系综的集体光谱与其经历不同局部环境的个体中心。我们开发了一个符号回归管道，该管道通过生成个体光谱响应并结合明确的权重，将单中心自旋结构映射到校准的系综模型中。约束搜索从单中心光学检测的磁共振光谱中选择厄米算符项，拟合它们的系数，并将所选表达式作为系综的源模型。系综校准随后考虑共振位移、局部无序、方向和光学响应，同时保持个体光谱贡献的可及性。在公开的单中心和系综数据上，零场系综持有频率的均方根误差从0.008835降低到0.003872（归一化光致发光），比匹配的未校正组合提高了56.2%。在控制的QuTiP系综（128个位点，跨越4个NV方向）中，在0和3 mT下校准的模型，能够以0.000207-0.000228的误差预测一个独立保持的5.17 mT光谱，这与0.000200的噪声标准差相当。将模拟响应分解为个体中心贡献，显示了局部的光谱多样性如何组合成系综线形状。通过在校准样本依赖的光谱差异的同时保留源哈密顿量，该管道能够将局域自旋物理学与集体光学读数联系起来，并使系综线形状的贡献可用于物理解释。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种新的符号回归管道，用于校准氮-空位（NV）系综的光谱模型。该方法能够将单中心的自旋结构信息映射到系综模型中，通过生成个体光谱响应并结合权重来解释系综的光谱特性。实验结果表明，该管道显著提高了系综模型的预测精度，并能解析个体中心对系综线形状的贡献，为理解和应用NV系综提供了新的途径。
AI.keywords: NV系综,符号回归,光谱校准,自旋物理学,集体光学读数
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种创新的符号回归管道，用于解决NV系综光谱表征中的关键挑战，即连接集体光谱与个体中心。其方法通过结合单中心物理和系综校准，实现了显著的性能提升，并提供了对个体贡献的可解释性。该方法在实际数据和模拟数据上都得到了验证，显示了其潜力和通用性。然而，对于不同类型的NV系综或更复杂的环境条件下的性能仍需进一步研究。

title: Macro Mondrian Conformal Risk Control
summary: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) extends conformal prediction beyond the coverage setting to the control of general monotone loss functions, in a distribution-free and modelagnostic fashion. This makes it well-suited to problems with high-dimensional targets, such as the semantic segmentation task addressed in this work. However, CRC guarantees only marginal control, meaning that the risk is controlled on average over the data distribution. Under imbalanced distributions, the risk on inputs that contain rare objects may therefore remain uncontrolled, even when the marginal guarantee holds. We propose a new method that controls the risk on average over user-defined groups of the domain, drawing on Mondrian conformal prediction and macro-coverage algorithms. The method relies on a taxonomy, that is, a function that assigns a group to each data point, and reweights each point's risk by a coefficient that depends on its group probability, so that rare points contribute more than common ones. We illustrate the approach on two semantic segmentation datasets.

AI.title_translation: 宏观蒙德里安共形风险控制
AI.tldr: 共形风险控制（CRC）在处理高维目标（如语义分割）时存在分布不均的问题，可能导致罕见类别风险失控。本文提出了一种基于蒙德里安共形预测和宏观覆盖算法的新方法，通过用户定义的类别和基于类别概率的权重调整，实现对特定子集（如罕见类别）风险的控制，并在两个语义分割数据集上进行了验证。
AI.motivation: 现有的共形风险控制（CRC）方法在分布不均的情况下，对罕见类别的风险控制效果不佳，即使满足了整体的保证。
AI.method: 提出了一种新的方法，结合了蒙德里安共形预测和宏观覆盖算法。该方法通过定义一个分类函数将数据点分配到不同的组，并根据数据点所属组的概率为其风险分配权重，使得罕见数据点的风险贡献更大，从而实现对用户定义的特定数据组的风险控制。
AI.result: 该方法在两个语义分割数据集上进行了说明和验证。
AI.conclusion: 通过引入基于宏观覆盖和蒙德里安共形预测的方法，可以实现对特定数据组（尤其是罕见类别）的风险控制，解决了标准CRC在分布不均情况下的局限性。
AI.translation: 共形风险控制（CRC）将共形预测扩展到覆盖范围之外，用于控制一般单调损失函数，并且不依赖于分布和模型。这使其非常适合处理高维目标问题，例如本工作中解决的语义分割任务。然而，CRC仅能提供边际控制，意味着风险是在数据分布的平均意义上进行控制的。在分布不均的情况下，即使边际保证成立，包含稀有对象的输入的风险也可能保持不受控制。我们提出了一种新方法，该方法借鉴了蒙德里安共形预测和宏观覆盖算法，能够控制数据域的用户定义组的平均风险。该方法依赖于一种分类法，即一个将组分配给每个数据点的函数，并根据每个数据点的组概率对其风险进行加权，使得稀有数据点的贡献比常见数据点更大。我们在两个语义分割数据集上说明了该方法。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种改进的共形风险控制（CRC）方法，称为宏观蒙德里安共形风险控制（Macro Mondrian Conformal Risk Control）。针对标准CRC在处理分布不均数据（如语义分割中的罕见对象）时可能无法有效控制风险的问题，该新方法结合了蒙德里安共形预测和宏观覆盖算法。通过引入数据分类和基于组概率的风险加权，使得罕见数据点对风险的贡献被放大，从而实现了对用户定义数据组（特别是罕见类别）的风险控制。该方法在两个语义分割数据集上的应用得到了说明。
AI.keywords: 共形风险控制, 蒙德里安共形预测, 宏观覆盖, 风险控制, 语义分割
AI.comments: 该研究解决了共形风险控制在处理不均衡数据分布时的重要挑战，通过结合蒙德里安共形预测和宏观覆盖算法，提出了一种有效的风险控制新机制。该方法在理论上具有吸引力，并且通过在语义分割任务上的应用进行了验证，显示了其实际潜力。未来的工作可以进一步探索该方法在其他高维、不均衡数据场景下的适用性，并对其理论保证进行更深入的分析。

title: Revisiting entropy and entropy-related magnitudes of a symbolic sequence and their estimation
summary: This article revisits entropy and related magnitudes (entropy density, effective measure complexity, and informational distance) for the analysis of sequential data. We present their mathematical foundations within information theory and ergodic theory, establishing connections between probabilistic Shannon entropy and algorithmic Kolmogorov complexity. A central result, Zivs theorem, demonstrates the asymptotic equivalence between the normalised number of distinct words and entropy density, providing the theoretical basis for estimation via Lempel-Ziv factorisation. We examine the convergence properties of these magnitudes and introduce estimation procedures for finite sequences, including a method for the effective measure complexity and the transfer entropy rate. An open-source software library implementing parallel algorithms for efficient Lempel-Ziv factorisation is presented. The practical utility of the framework is illustrated through three case studies: functional brain connectivity analysis from fMRI data, characterisation of spatiotemporal dynamics in coupled nonlinear oscillators, and electrocardiogram-based classification of atrial fibrillation, demonstrating how entropic measures capture meaningful structural and dynamical properties across diverse domains.

AI.title_translation: 符号序列的熵和熵相关量及其估计的再访
AI.tldr: 该论文重新审视了用于分析序列数据的熵及其相关量（熵密度、有效测度复杂度和信息距离），建立了概率香农熵与算法柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂性之间的联系，并提出了基于Ziv定理的估计方法。论文还介绍了用于有限序列的估计程序、一种用于有效测度复杂度和传递熵率的方法，并提供了一个开源软件库。最后，通过三个案例研究（fMRI数据的功能性大脑连接分析、耦合非线性振子的时空动力学表征以及基于心电图的心房颤动分类）展示了该框架的实用性。
AI.motivation: 对序列数据进行分析，重新审视熵及其相关量（熵密度、有效测度复杂度和信息距离）的数学基础，并建立概率香农熵与算法柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂性之间的联系。
AI.method: 利用信息论和遍历论的数学基础，通过Ziv定理证明了不同单词的归一化数量与熵密度之间的渐近等价性，从而为基于Lempel-Ziv分解的估计提供了理论基础。提出了有限序列的估计程序，包括有效测度复杂度和传递熵率的估计方法。实现了一个用于高效Lempel-Ziv分解的并行算法的开源软件库。
AI.result: Ziv定理证明了归一化的不同单词数量与熵密度之间的渐近等价性。提出了有限序列的估计程序，包括有效测度复杂度和传递熵率的估计方法。通过三个案例研究（功能性大脑连接分析、耦合非线性振子的时空动力学表征、心房颤动分类）证明了熵测量可以捕捉不同领域中有意义的结构和动力学特性。
AI.conclusion: 该框架通过熵及其相关量的估计，能够捕捉不同领域（如大脑连接、非线性振子和心电图分类）中有意义的结构和动力学特性，并提供了一个包含并行算法的开源软件库以支持其实际应用。
AI.translation: 本文重新审视了用于分析序列数据的熵及其相关量（熵密度、有效测度复杂度和信息距离）。我们将其数学基础置于信息论和遍历论的背景下，建立了概率香农熵与算法柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂性之间的联系。一个核心结果，即Ziv定理，证明了不同单词的归一化数量与熵密度之间的渐近等价性，为通过Lempel-Ziv分解进行估计提供了理论基础。我们研究了这些量的收敛性质，并提出了有限序列的估计程序，包括有效测度复杂度和传递熵率的估计方法。本文还介绍了一个实现并行算法以进行高效Lempel-Ziv分解的开源软件库。该框架的实际效用通过三个案例研究得到说明：来自fMRI数据的功能性大脑连接分析、耦合非线性振子的时空动力学表征以及基于心电图的心房颤动分类，展示了熵测量如何在不同领域捕捉有意义的结构和动力学特性。
AI.summary: 本研究旨在分析序列数据，重新审视熵及其相关量（熵密度、有效测度复杂度和信息距离）的理论基础，并建立概率香农熵与算法柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂性之间的联系。通过Ziv定理，论文提出了一种基于Lempel-Ziv分解的估计方法，并开发了用于有限序列的估计程序和开源软件库。最后，通过脑连接分析、非线性振子和心电图分类等案例研究，验证了该框架在不同领域的实用性。
AI.keywords: 熵, 熵密度, Lempel-Ziv分解, 序列数据分析, 信息论
AI.comments: 该论文在信息论和遍历论的框架下，深入探讨了熵及其相关量在序列数据分析中的应用。通过Ziv定理和Lempel-Ziv分解，为熵的估计提供了坚实的理论基础和实用的计算方法。开源软件库的提供进一步增强了该研究的可及性和应用潜力。三个案例研究的成功应用，充分展示了该框架在不同跨学科领域的强大生命力。

title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
summary: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. Its multiscale dynamics, intermittency, extreme events, rough velocity fields and intrinsically stochastic transport make visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectral agreement insufficient measures of physical fidelity. We examine where generative AI provide novel capabilities with emphasis on diffusion models, score-based methods, and related probability-transport formulations. We discuss their use in unconditional generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, temporal evolution, and mesh-free representations. We argue that validation must address turbulence properties: energy transfer, structure functions, anomalous scaling, pdf tails, coherent structures, conservation laws, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity and generalization. Finally, we discuss potential limitations in validation, baseline, data availability and reproducibility, and the need for a benchmark ecosystem combining open data, standardized challenges, hidden tests, physics-aware metrics, and documented failures. This paper serves as a bridge between two communities. For AI practitioners, we provide a fair and accessible introduction to turbulence, essential for appreciating the challenges posed by the field and for assessing the physical relevance of generative models. For turbulent practitioners, we provide an introduction to the key technological aspects of Generative AI, clarifying what these tools actually do, and where their potential and current limitations lie.

AI.title_translation: 生成式人工智能在湍流中的应用：基础、应用、验证与基准
AI.tldr: 生成式AI为湍流问题提供了新方法，尤其在扩散模型方面，但湍流的复杂性（多尺度动力学、间歇性、极端事件等）使得视觉真实性不足以衡量物理保真度。验证应关注湍流特性，并需要一个结合开放数据、标准化挑战、隐藏测试、物理感知指标和已记录的失败案例的基准生态系统。
AI.motivation: 湍流问题通常面临观测不完整或自由度未解析的情况，导致存在多个物理上合理的解。生成式AI为解决这些问题提供了新途径，包括随机闭合、超分辨率、数据同化、不确定性量化以及欧拉和拉格朗日流集合的生成。
AI.method: 本文重点介绍了生成式AI在湍流中的应用，特别是扩散模型、基于分数的模型和相关的概率传输方法。讨论了它们在无条件生成、概率重建、降阶建模、时间演化和无网格表示等方面的应用。
AI.conclusion: 验证生成式AI在湍流中的应用需要关注物理特性，如能量传递、结构函数、异常标度、概率密度函数尾部、相干结构、守恒定律、时间一致性和集合多样性。此外，还需要解决验证、基线、数据可用性和可重复性方面的局限性，并建立一个包含开放数据、标准化挑战、隐藏测试、物理感知指标和已记录的失败案例的基准生态系统。
AI.translation: 生成式人工智能为湍流问题提供了新的方法，这些问题由于观测不完整或未解析的自由度而可能存在多个物理上合理的解。潜在应用包括随机闭合、超分辨率、数据同化、不确定性量化以及欧拉和拉格朗日流集合的生成。然而，湍流并非一个常规的图像生成问题。其多尺度动力学、间歇性、极端事件、粗糙的速度场和内在的随机输运使得视觉真实性、点误差和低阶谱一致性不足以衡量物理保真度。我们研究了生成式AI提供新能力的地方，重点关注扩散模型、基于分数的方法以及相关的概率传输公式。我们讨论了它们在无条件生成、概率重建、降阶建模、时间演化和无网格表示方面的应用。我们认为，验证必须解决湍流的特性：能量传递、结构函数、异常标度、概率密度函数尾部、相干结构、守恒定律、时间一致性、集合多样性和泛化能力。最后，我们讨论了验证、基线、数据可用性和可重复性方面的潜在局限性，以及对结合开放数据、标准化挑战、隐藏测试、物理感知指标和已记录的失败案例的基准生态系统的需求。本文旨在成为两个社区之间的桥梁。对于AI从业者，我们提供了对湍流的公平且易于理解的介绍，这对于欣赏该领域带来的挑战以及评估生成模型在物理上的相关性至关重要。对于湍流从业者，我们提供了对生成式AI关键技术方面的介绍，阐明了这些工具的实际功能，以及它们的潜力和当前的局限性。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了生成式人工智能（Generative AI）在湍流研究中的应用潜力。文章指出，生成式AI能够为湍流问题提供新的解决方案，尤其是在处理观测不完整或自由度未解析的情况时，可以生成多个物理上合理的解。文章重点介绍了扩散模型、基于分数的方法等生成式AI技术，并讨论了它们在随机闭合、超分辨率、数据同化、不确定性量化、流集合生成等方面的应用。然而，作者强调湍流的复杂性（如多尺度动力学、间歇性、极端事件等）使得传统的图像生成评估指标（如视觉真实性、点误差、低阶谱一致性）不足以衡量物理保真度。因此，文章呼吁在验证生成式AI模型时，必须关注湍流特有的物理属性，如能量传递、结构函数、异常标度、概率密度函数尾部、相干结构、守恒定律、时间一致性、集合多样性和泛化能力。最后，文章指出了在验证、基线设定、数据可用性和可重复性方面存在的挑战，并提出需要构建一个包含开放数据、标准化挑战、隐藏测试、物理感知指标和已记录失败案例的基准生态系统。本文旨在促进AI和湍流研究社区之间的交流，为AI从业者介绍湍流的挑战，为湍流从业者介绍生成式AI的技术和局限性。
AI.keywords: 生成式AI, 湍流, 扩散模型, 物理保真度, 验证基准
AI.comments: 该论文为理解生成式AI在湍流研究中的应用提供了一个全面的概述。它不仅强调了生成式AI的潜力，还深刻地指出了其在物理保真度评估和验证方面面临的挑战。文章对湍流特性的关注以及对建立基准生态系统的呼吁，为该领域未来的研究指明了方向。

title: Sharp Bounds for Graph-Codes Avoiding Complete Bipartite Differences
summary:
Let $d_{K_{s,t}}(n)$ be the largest fraction of all graphs on $[n]$ in a family containing no two distinct members whose symmetric difference is a copy of $K_{s,t}$. We determine this maximum density for every fixed pair of positive integers $s,t$. If both part sizes are odd, it is known that the density is exactly $1/2$. Otherwise, let $2h$ be the largest even part size. We prove $$ d_{K_{s,t}}(n)=Θ_{s,t}(n^{-h}). $$ For $h>1$, this improves the general $O_{s,t}(1/n)$ upper bound obtained from Alon's two-copy gluing theorem~\cite{Alon2024}. The sharp bounds for even stars were already proved by Alon and are recovered as special cases.
  The upper bound uses the Frankl--Füredi forbidden-intersection theorem. For the lower bound, we construct binary linear codes using BCH codes. When exactly one part size is even, we assign to each edge the sum of the binary vectors assigned to its endpoints. When both part sizes are even, we identify these vectors with elements of a finite field and assign to each edge the product of its endpoint elements. In both cases, every copy of $K_{s,t}$ has a nonzero syndrome.

title: Realizing Low-Precision Storage and Sparse Execution in a Folded FPGA Speech Enhancer
comments: 5 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISCAS 2027
summary: Hardware-aware training often optimizes FPGA resources, latency, or bit operations, but folding changes what compression saves: shared arithmetic decouples precision, weight storage, and scheduled work. We derive training objectives from the measured costs of a folded streaming speech-enhancement accelerator. Mixed-precision weights reduce on-chip storage; structured channel sparsity removes entire operations from the engine schedule. We deploy a bit-exact implementation on the Kria KV260. The best sparse model eliminates 47.3% of convolution MACs, cutting frame time by 45% (1.86 to 1.03 ms) and dynamic energy by 60% (83 to 33 $μ$J/frame) against a storage-priced model measured in the same session, with higher speech quality. Relative to the most efficient dense build measured separately, frame time falls by 42% and energy by 48%. Reducing weight width from 8 to 6 bits lowers dynamic power by 27% but changes frame time by less than 5%. Plain channel group-lasso removes more work than cycle-cost-weighted lasso. Thus, folded-accelerator training should price storage and removable work separately, rather than rely on a single bit-operation metric.
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISCAS 2027

title: Sequential versus fully conditional specification for tree-based synthesis of health data
summary: Disseminating synthetic data in place of original ones is a promising way to enforce privacy while complying with open science principles, especially in the healthcare domain. To keep pace with the rate at which researchers collect such data, there is a need for fast and flexible synthesis procedures. A popular class of such procedures is based on models of conditional distributions induced by decision trees. Such models can be combined into a synthetic distribution following two main approaches: sequential specification and fully conditional specification. However, there is currently no recommendation on which specification to use to optimize the risk-utility tradeoffs. In this work, we use both specifications to synthesize medical datasets by combining tree-based models of conditional distributions. We compare the quality of the resulting synthetic data using several metrics of risk and utility. Our results indicate no general superiority of either specification over the other. Sequential synthesis seems sensitive to the ordering of the variables, while the fully conditional specification involves more hyperparameters and incurs higher computational costs, which may limit its suitability for off-the-shelf synthesis procedures.

title: Global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ Convergence of Multilevel Gradient-Regularized Newton Methods
summary: We develop and analyze multilevel gradient-regularized Newton methods for unconstrained convex optimization with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. To establish this rate for multilevel methods, we introduce a class of row-nested restriction operators that ensures monotonicity of the reduced-gradient norms across levels. Numerical experiments with row-nested operators demonstrate convergence behavior comparable to full-space gradient-regularized Newton, while offering substantial computational savings on large-scale instances.

title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
comments: 24 pages, 9 figures. Dataset and accompanying resources available on Hugging Face under the HelmholtzAI-FZJ organization
summary: Learning molecular models of RNA requires simulation data that capture conformational variability and provide consistent physical training signals. Here, we introduce mdRNAcat, a curated dataset of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 48 RNA systems selected to promote sequence diversity. Each system is simulated using replica-exchange with solute scaling (REST2), with 32 Hamiltonian states and production lengths of 200-300 ns per state. The dataset provides atomic coordinates, instantaneous forces, and forces reevaluated under the unscaled reference Hamiltonian, together with structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata. Coordinates and forces are available at 1 ps intervals for the reference state and 100 ps intervals across all states in a standardized HDF5 format. We characterize conformational sampling, exchange behavior, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions to document the properties of the simulated ensembles. mdRNAcat provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating data-driven RNA models, including coarse-grained force fields.
comment: 24 pages, 9 figures. Dataset and accompanying resources available on Hugging Face under the HelmholtzAI-FZJ organization

title: A PDE-Based Model of Runner Flow in Mass Participation Events
comments: 6 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to the 2026 Modeling, Estimation and Control Conference (MECC)
summary: This paper presents a macroscopic approach for modeling pedestrian movement. A convection-diffusion partial differential equation (PDE) is described and used to model the flow of runners along a marathon course. A marathon is a good modeling case study for human movement because the location of runners is only known in sparse locations, so an accurate model is needed to know where people are at all times. As well, marathons offer many safety and logistical problems that can be solved by modeling human movement. Data is obtained from the 2023 Columbus Marathon, and model improvements are made to include a temporally varying convection term. Results show an increase in model accuracy which can allow for better resource allocation and safety measures.
comment: 6 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to the 2026 Modeling, Estimation and Control Conference (MECC)

title: Towards Exact Multidimensional Fluxes: A Structure-Preserving Data-Informed Framework for Riemann Solvers
summary:
Finite-volume and discontinuous Galerkin methods update cells using the space-time flux integral over their faces, which typically depends on the solutions to local Riemann problems. In the multidimensional Riemann problem setting, this integral is difficult to evaluate exactly because of complex wave interactions. In this work, we show that the exact space-time flux integral is a polynomial in the time step and face dimensions. This motivates a learning-based approach, as only the mapping from the initial states to the polynomial coefficients needs to be learned. We propose a structure-preserving, data-informed Riemann solver framework that uses a neural network trained on high-resolution simulation data to learn this mapping. Key structural properties, including consistency and symmetry, are enforced by construction. Provided that the high-resolution simulations converge to the exact flux integrals and the network accurately predicts the coefficients, this framework yields near-exact flux integrals for use in numerical simulations.
  We demonstrate the framework using classical implosion and explosion problems for the two-dimensional Euler equations. In an unsplit MUSCL-Hancock scheme, the learned Riemann solver remains stable at a CFL number of 0.9, whereas the same scheme using the exact one-dimensional Riemann solver fails. Compared with the latter scheme at CFL=0.45, the learned scheme is slightly more accurate and requires approximately 30% less computational time.

title: Identities, Not Pairs: Distribution-Free False-Accept Control for Embedding-Based Verification
summary: Embedding-based verification often calibrates a false-accept threshold from all impostor pairs among $m$ identities, although these pairs share identities. We characterize a worst-case limit: when hub identities score highly against a fraction $ρ$ of the population, a calibration-only threshold with marginal false-accept rate (FAR) at most $α$ under every identity-exchangeable law reaches the hub score on hub-free calibration sets with probability at most $(m+2)α/(2ρ)$. Uniformly accepting near that score at levels well below $ρ/m$ therefore requires trial information. We propose COVE, which ranks the trial pair among all $N=\binom{m+2}{2}$ pairs formed by augmenting the calibration units with the probe and reference. Under identity exchangeability, its marginal FAR is at most $\lfloorαN\rfloor/N$, with first possible acceptance at $1/N=O(1/m^2)$. The rule also retains this guarantee with a fixed symmetric cohort-normalized score using an independent cohort. On 6 benchmarks and 8 frozen encoders, realised FAR was consistent with the exact bound. Where both valid calibration-only baselines accepted nothing, COVE retained a median $100\%$ of the sampled oracle's true-accept rate over reliable comparisons. In contrast, an empirical quantile over dependent pairs reached 2.87$\,α$ FAR, and a binomial upper confidence bound over pairs missed its nominal 95\% conditional-FAR target in up to 55\% of calibration draws. Symmetric CSLS raised COVE's true-accept rate by up to 4.3-fold in the tested settings. The code is available in https://github.com/salimkhazem/Cove.git

title: A theoretically exact filtered back-propagationformula for single-time wave inversion
summary: We consider single-time wave inversion, that is, recovering the initial pressure $f$ from the wave field $\mathcal{W}_T f = u(\cdot,T)$ at a single time $T$, where $u$ solves the wave equation with sound speed $c$ and initial data $(f,0)$. In two dimensions this is the main reconstruction step of full-field photoacoustic projection imaging, where each camera image is a two-dimensional wave field at a single time instant. An efficient direct method is back-propagation by the Fourier multiplier $2\cos(cT|ξ|)$. It yields exact inversion in odd dimensions but not in two. We give its error in closed form, with bounds, and derive an exact explicit filtered back-propagation $f = 2\mathcal{W}_T \mathcal{M}_K \mathcal{W}_T f$ in analogy to filtered backprojection for the Radon transform.

title: Temporal-Difference Calibration of Black-Box Simulators
summary: We develop a derivative-free temporal-difference (TD) framework for calibrating black-box simulators using one-step transitions from a target system and noisy simulator-generated continuation values. The calibration parameter is defined through Bellman orthogonality, recovering the physical parameter under correct simulator specification and yielding a near-optimal $L_2$ approximation of the policy value under misspecification. We propose three TD algorithms based on random-direction finite differences, distinguished by their query costs and reuse of noisy simulator evaluations. We establish almost-sure convergence, last-iterate mean-square error bounds, and central limit theorems for Polyak-Ruppert averages across four query-noise regimes. Our analysis reveals a specification-dependent bias phenomenon: for two algorithms, the finite-difference bias of the TD estimating equation vanishes at the calibration target under correct specification, even when the gradient surrogate remains biased. This permits a fixed perturbation radius and rate exponents approaching $1/2$ in the simulator rollout budget, whereas misspecification generally recovers the classical Kiefer-Wolfowitz rates. We also develop a few-replicate online bootstrap that yields Student-$t$ calibrated confidence intervals under negligible query noise, and identify a covariance mismatch that can invalidate conventional multiplier inference along Markov trajectories. Finally, a second-stage TD recursion corrects the remaining value discrepancy without additional simulator queries.

title: Beyond Wasserstein Proximity: Finding Better Transfer Sources
summary: Source selection often favors similar data, yet marginal proximity need not identify the most useful pretraining source. We motivate a conditional alternative through domain-adaptation theory and a regression example in which broader source variation improves estimation despite increasing Wasserstein distance. We examine five-day cryptocurrency volatility using ten Binance spot assets, six forecaster families, three seeds, and shared temporal cutoffs. Selecting the three farthest rather than nearest Gaussian-Wasserstein sources improves mean persistence-relative skill by 12.52 percentage points for MLP and 20.90 for Transformer, with positive post-hoc paired date-block intervals. Forward pilot selection improves mean skill over random transfer in all six families. Compact recurrent models achieve the lowest absolute mean errors, separating selection utility from forecasting quality. Retrospective five-candidate screening shows additional gains from farthest-first geometry before pilot ranking for MLP and Transformer. We distinguish across-target associations from within-target decisions and evaluate target heterogeneity, training seeds, and temporal-block sensitivity. Findings are exploratory for a fixed historical panel; the screening analysis measures no runtime saving.

title: Measurement-dependent reduction of open dynamics in the quantum phase estimation algorithm: the visible subspace and the damped Fejér kernel
summary: For the quantum phase estimation (QPE) algorithm we study the minimal space of observables that is sufficient to predict the entire output distribution under open dynamics of the counting register. Building on the general Krylov theory of reduction, we compute the structure of this space explicitly for the full Fourier measurement. The outcome probabilities are determined by cyclic sums of the state matrix. If the adjoint generator is diagonal on the matrix units, the spectral classes inside the residue classes of the index difference modulo the register dimension $M$ give a constructive basis, an exact dimension formula, and attainable bounds: the dimension of the visible space lies between $M$ and $M^2-M+1$. The class includes independent qubit dephasing, and an analytically solvable reference model of Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) type yields a damped Fejér kernel; two random-unitary channels with the same Ramsey contrast show that higher harmonics are distinguishable in the QPE distribution. For approximate reduction we use a finite-time Gramian and an a posteriori residual estimate, with a quadratic error order for a reducing unperturbed subspace and a compatible initial state. Numerical calculations check the consistency of the representations and the behaviour of the error under non-Toeplitz perturbations.

title: A Unified Framework for Assortment Optimization and Matching under MNL Choice
summary: We develop a unified framework for assortment optimization and matching under multinomial logit (MNL) choice, yielding simple algorithms and analyses across a broad class of problems. The framework centers on a single-customer assortment problem in which the firm commits to eligible products before their independent availabilities are revealed. A simple threshold policy achieves a tight $1/2$ guarantee against a benchmark that selects its assortment after observing availability and may control dependence subject to the same marginal probability bounds. This guarantee accommodates cardinality constraints and adversarial removal of excess available products. Combined with problem-specific linear programming relaxations, the framework yields $1/2$ guarantees for standard two-sided assortment optimization, customization under mixtures of MNL models, ride-hailing notifications, multi-round broadcast matching, and MNL prophet inequalities, and a $1/4$ guarantee for fully static two-sided assortment optimization. Across these applications, we improve approximation factors, extend guarantees to more general revenues and cardinality constraints, and retain existing factors against stronger benchmarks.

title: Autonomous Structural Discovery Of Bioprocess Dynamics And Kinetics Via LLM-Driven Agents
summary: High-fidelity digital twins in continuous biomanufacturing are often bottlenecked by incomplete kinetic models, while standard data-driven algorithms (e.g., SINDy, PINNs) lack interpretability or impose rigid physical assumptions. This paper introduces a hybrid closed-loop architecture for autonomous kinetic state-space discovery driven by a Large Language Model (LLM) agent. The framework employs a sequential "isolation-peeling" methodology across orthogonal operational regimes. This algorithmic peeling mathematically decouples entangled multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (catalytic) biological rate law. Grounded in a Two-Level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) library, the framework utilizes Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) and logarithmic decomposition to decouple complex cell growth kinetics into orthogonal multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (regulatory) residual channels. When statistical degeneracy occurs an Active Design of Experiments (DoE) controller dynamically triggers targeted perturbations to decorrelate competing model hypotheses. Evaluated on a continuous stirred-tank reactor exhibiting unmodeled Haldane inhibition, Luong product toxicity, and secondary metabolite autocatalysis, the framework autonomously expanded the state space and recovered ground-truth parameters with under 6% error without a priori kinetic knowledge.

title: Quantitative approximation theorem of neural operators for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
summary: In this paper, we study neural operators for the Dirichet-to-Neumann map (DN map), which is encountered in the famous Calderón's problem. In many numerical methods used for reconstructing the unknown conductivity from the knowledge of the DN map need to evaluate the corresponding DN map at a given conductivity function, which involves solving the boundary value problem for the conductivity equation and taking the Neumann data. Such procedure is time consuming and not effective. Hence, it is a favorable strategy to construct a surrogate to replace the forward map mapping conductivity functions to corresponding DN maps. The main theme of this paper is to derive quantitative bounds on the parametric complexity of these neural operators. In particular, under suitable assumptions, their depth grows at most logarithmically with $\varepsilon^{-1}$, while the relevant spectral and projection ranks grow algebraically. It should be noted that general neural operators suffer from "the curse of parametric dimensionality". This work demonstrates the construction of neural operators for the DN map that does not suffer from such curse.

title: A knowledge-driven nonconvex square-root regularization framework for joint group sparsity and structured smoothness
summary: Structured sparse learning is a leading paradigm for high-dimensional data modeling, as it enables rigorous integration of domain-validated structural priors into the learning process. Among these priors, pre-defined grouped structure and piecewise smoothness are ubiquitous in real-world applications. However, most existing structured regularization methods are built on squared loss and convex penalties, rarely jointly model these two complementary structural priors, and suffer from two key limitations. Their optimal tuning parameters are sensitive to the unknown noise level $σ$ due to the squared loss. Meanwhile, convex penalties induce inherent estimation bias and severe over-shrinkage of large magnitudes. To address these issues, we propose a knowledge-driven Nonconvex Structured Smooth Adjustment for Square-Root Regularization (NS$^3$R), which unifies the $σ$-free square-root loss with a joint nonconvex $\ell_{2,q}$ penalty ($0 < q < 1$) to simultaneously encode group sparsity and structured smoothness priors. Theoretically, we establish rigorous non-asymptotic error bounds for the NS$^3$R estimator under a mild $(2,q)$-group restricted compatibility condition. Computationally, we develop an efficient double-screened IRLS with thresholding (DS-IRLS-th) algorithm, which adopts a nested double-screening strategy to reduce computational cost and improve numerical stability, with provable global convergence for the resulting nonconvex optimization problem. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate that NS$^3$R consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in finite-sample settings.

title: Movable Antenna Enabled Anti-Jamming: From Local Optimality Guaranteed Design to a Unified Antenna Position Optimization Framework
summary: Anti-jamming capability is of paramount importance in modern wireless communications, yet conventional receivers are severely constrained by their fixed array geometries, which limit the available spatial degrees of freedom and leave performance highly susceptible to strong interference. By contrast, movable antennas (MAs) provide additional spatial degrees of freedom through antenna-position optimization. This paper investigates MA-enabled anti-jamming by jointly optimizing the antenna-position vector (APV) and receive beamformer to maximize the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). For the canonical setting with a single jammer and a single line-of-sight (LoS) propagation path on the legitimate link, we develop a damped projected-gradient descent (DPGD) algorithm with low computational complexity, which scales linearly with the number of receive MAs. We establish a generic active strict-saddle landscape for the resulting steering-coherence minimization problem and prove that DPGD converges almost surely to a local minimizer rather than merely to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point. For the general setting with multiple channel paths on the legitimate link and/or multiple jammers, we derive an equivalent ridge least-squares formulation and develop a low-complexity soft-active projected-gradient (SAPG) algorithm, which also scales linearly with the number of receive MAs. We further show that the proposed antenna position optimization framework applies to both minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) and zero-forcing (ZF) reception. Numerical results validate the proposed algorithms, demonstrating substantial gains in both anti-jamming performance and computational efficiency.

title: Formation of international environmental agreements and payoff allocation
summary: Dealing with climate change requires that all countries engage in costly efforts to reduce their emissions. Reaching this objective has so far been elusive because it is in the best interest of each country to let the others do the effort and benefit itself from a better environment. The presence of negative externalities and strategic behavior have made game theory a natural paradigm to design an international environmental agreement (IEA) that codifies what countries should do. Considering that countries are sovereign and no supranational entity can impose an agreement, a stream of literature adopted a noncooperative mode of play to the formation of an environmental coalition. On the other hand, as joint optimization of all countries' payoff leads to the best outcome, cooperative games approach has also been proposed to share the cost of climate change. Both approaches have their pros and cons.

title: XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
summary: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel. Such approaches aim to offload large portions of the computation onto the channel itself, which is often controlled by reconfigurable MetaSurfaces (MSs). Typical MS-parametrized systems, however, enable only limited computation offloading in the wave domain, usually corresponding to a single neural network layer, due to adverse channel fading effects and the almost linear operation of the channel and conventional MS models. In this paper, we demonstrate that an eXtremely Large (XL) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system equipped with Stacked Intelligent MSs (SIM) at the RX side, together with a single antenna and its accompanying radio-frequency chain, may act as a two-layer neural network operating exclusively over the air. The first (uncontrollable) network layer corresponds to the transformations offered by wireless fading, while the second (controllable) layer is implemented via SIM operations. In particular, only the first, front-end MS layer needs to exhibit nonlinear response to serve as an activation function. Leveraging the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) framework, the proposed XL MIMO system architecture is shown to be a universal approximator, and the optimal linear-SIM-based combining is derived in closed form, allowing for fast training even and partial signal observability. Numerical evaluations across diverse datasets showcase that the proposed XL-MIMO-ELM framework achieves classification accuracy comparable to idealized digital models, thereby, proving the viability of low complexity, wave-domain neural computations.

title: Minimax Rates for Conditional Generative Learning under Wasserstein Loss
summary: We study minimax rates for conditional generative learning under integrated Wasserstein loss, with Hölder continuous conditional laws and an unrestricted covariate distribution. We evaluate unrestricted generators through their conditional output distributions. For expected Wasserstein loss, the minimax rate agrees with the rate under uniform covariates and follows from balancing localization bias against unconditional distribution estimation error. Higher moments of the loss can instead be dominated by unobserved covariate regions, which force an additional risk contribution of order $n^{-1}$, where $n$ is the sample size. An adaptive localization argument gives matching upper bounds. The results cover unrestricted response laws and possibly vanishing Besov densities for $W_1$, and extend to higher Wasserstein orders under uniform response density bounds and integrability conditions. A multiscale lower bound closes the logarithmic gap in unconditional $W_1$ minimax rates in dimension two for both unrestricted distributions and Besov density classes. We also establish minimax rates for conditional Brenier maps under density, integrability, and uniform curvature conditions.

title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
summary: Constraint learning is an emerging paradigm of modeling optimization problems with the help of machine learning. In this paradigm, trained machine learning models are embedded into the optimization model. For example, we can learn constraints empirically from available data, or we can avoid using a nonlinear objective function by learning a simpler approximation for it. Neural networks become a compelling option if the machine learning models must capture more elaborate and nuanced relationships. However, optimization models embedding neural networks may become too large or too slow to solve. In this tutorial, we present practical considerations for an effective and efficient use of constraint learning with neural networks and validate it with a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks.

title: Depth Improves Training-Time Scaling for Difficult Tasks in Deep Linear Networks
summary: Neural scaling laws describe the predictable power-law dependence of model performance on training time, dataset size, and model scale, with the exponents quantifying how performance changes with resources. Recent theory has shown how scaling exponents are shaped by the data distribution and the structure of the learning task, but whether network depth can improve training-time scaling has remained unsettled. Through a refined analysis of deep linear networks, we clarify that the task spectrum determines when increasing network depth improves training-time scaling. For spectrally difficult tasks, increasing depth improves the asymptotic training-time scaling exponent, whereas for easy tasks, the exponent remains independent of depth, with depth affecting only a logarithmic correction at the boundary between these regimes. Remarkably, we find that a reparameterization of time governed by the predictor norm provides a unified description of the dynamics across task difficulties. Under this reparameterization, the loss follows a common scaling law whose exponent is independent of depth. Numerical experiments on a task derived from benchmark image data and with nonlinear networks exhibit qualitatively consistent task-dependent effects of depth on training-time scaling. Our findings advance the theoretical understanding of how task structure shapes the effects of network architecture on learning and offer a basis for studying scaling behavior across broader classes of neural networks.

title: Explainable Prediction of High-Speed Solar Wind Streams driven by Coronal Holes via Topological Data Analysis
summary: High-speed solar wind streams (HSSs) originating from coronal holes (CHs) are an important driver of recurrent geomagnetic activity. Since HSSs are associated to coronal structures visible in extreme-ultraviolet observations, this provides a natural basis for forecasting several days in advance. In this work, we investigate whether the topology of coronal structures observed in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) images contains predictive information on the subsequent occurrence of CH-driven HSSs at Earth. To this end, we consider Topological Data Analysis (TDA), and in particular persistent homology, to classify EUV solar images according to the occurrence of HSSs at Earth four days later. The target is a binary classification of HSS occurrence at a four-day lead time, defined using an HSS interval catalog and solar wind speed thresholds. Several combinations of topological representations and classifiers are evaluated under a common cross-validation framework. The results indicate that the topology of EUV coronal structures alone contains predictive information on subsequent CH-driven HSS occurrence, despite the absence of explicit CH geometric descriptors in the model input. To investigate the origin of this predictive information, we develop a model-level explainability framework based on cross-validation-aggregated feature weights and spatial evidence maps. A fully traced example connects persistence diagrams and persistence-image features to the classifier output and to their spatial localization in the original EUV observation. The proposed framework provides a transparent and computationally lightweight approach for investigating the relationship between coronal topology and subsequent high-speed solar wind streams.

title: ADACT: PDE-Constrained Thermal Hardware/Software Co-Design Adjoint-Driven Optimal Control via Finite Difference Discretization
summary: By virtue of the sheer compute demands of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC), modern multi-core microprocessors suffer from severe power density limits and thermal throttling, entailing an urgent need for principled methods for predictive, physics-informed dynamical thermal management (DTM). Here, we introduce a hardware/software co-design physics-informed PDE-constrained DTM throttling optimal control algorithm, ADACT (Adjoint-Driven Adaptive Co-Design Thermal Control), that minimizes thermal risk and cooling energy overhead while maximizing core execution throughput. The underlying physical temperature field is governed by a two-dimensional nonhomogeneous parabolic reaction-diffusion equation with spatially localized, time-varying power source terms and variable convective cooling subject to nonhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We employ a discretization of the continuous state PDE via a Crank-Nicolson finite difference scheme with a 5-point discrete Laplacian operator on a uniform spatial mesh, which preserves unconditional numerical stability and $O(Δx^2 + Δy^2 + Δt^2)$ second-order temporal and spatial accuracy. To efficiently compute exact gradients, we construct and implement a continuous backward-in-time adjoint state method with L-BFGS as our optimization algorithm of choice. The accuracy and second-order convergence rates of both forward state and backward adjoint solvers are quantitatively verified via the Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS), and gradient accuracy is validated using directional derivative Taylor tests. Numerical experiments demonstrate that ADACT dynamically throttles software power workloads and modulates hardware cooling efforts to strictly uphold physical thermal thresholds while maintaining operational throughput.

title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
summary: A full-duplex spoken dialogue model must yield when the user cuts in and hold when the user merely backchannels. Sequence-level RL with a timing reward (GRPO) is the usual recipe; we test its whole-rollout form on four open models and find two failures. A binary window reward gives zero advantage on exactly the windows that most need learning (a zero-gradient trap), and the one score per rollout is spread over listening-state decisions the reward is not written in terms of (credit leakage), so the model talks into silence or stops answering. Both come from sampling a reward that is a known function of a few binary control decisions. We propose \emph{window likelihood} (\WL): sample a continuation per window, but integrate in closed form over the stop decisions it visits and maximise the log-probability of acting correctly---a noisy-OR for yielding, a survival product for holding. On HumDial-FDBench, \WL\ gives the best yield/hold F1 on all six structurally different open models we post-train, exceeds Kyutai's released GRPO checkpoints (trained on different data), and adds no re-opening of the floor on any model.

title: KAPPA: Checking the Proofs in Statistics Papers with Lean 4 and Language Model Agents
summary: Papers in statistical theory rest on long proofs that few readers check line by line. We present KAPPA (Kit of Agents for Proof-checking Papers with a proof Assistant), open-source software that organizes language model agents, run by Claude Code, to translate the proofs of a LaTeX paper into the proof assistant Lean 4 with its library Mathlib and check them there, result by result. Each numbered result receives one of four verdicts: verified unconditionally; verified conditionally, with every cited or unproved input stated as a named hypothesis; issue recorded, with its place in the paper and the side at fault; or unfinished, with the reason. The kit follows the paper's own proof step by step, rather than finding a new one. Separate agents write and review, each statement is compared with the paper before it is proved and fingerprinted afterwards, and every verdict rests on evidence that can be rerun without a language model. The kit runs unattended for hours, waits out usage limits, re-checks only what a revision changed and reports its cost by role, model and result. We describe the design, walk through a complete run, and apply the kit to four example papers with answer keys and to three published statistical papers, checked blind in their versions from before public corrections. In all three, the kit found the published error at the step that the correction names, together with further problems that we confirmed by hand. Given the same papers directly, the same language model working with Lean classified fewer results correctly on the longest paper and reported some statements narrower than the paper's as proved; no verdict of the kit claimed more than its Lean evidence showed.

title: Graph-Convolutional Reinforcement Learning for Finite-Time Stabilization of a Chaotic Chua Circuit via Unified Flexible Terminal Sliding-Mode Control
summary: This paper introduces a graph convolutional reinforcement learning framework for the finite-time stabilization of chaotic dynamics in a physical Chua circuit. The circuit is modeled directly in terms of capacitor voltages, inductor current, and physical component parameters. This preserves the connection between the mathematical model and the underlying electrical system. A unified, flexible terminal sliding-mode controller is developed to achieve stabilization within a finite time in the presence of uncertainties in the lumped model, external disturbances, and bounded control inputs. The controller incorporates state-dependent nonlinear exponents to provide flexible convergence characteristics while avoiding singular terms near equilibrium. To minimize dependence on manual controller tuning, the admissible controller parameters are optimized using an actor-critic reinforcement learning scheme with a graph convolutional network that leverages the circuit dynamics' coupling structure. The learned parameters are constrained to the ranges required by the theoretical stability conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the rapid suppression of chaotic oscillations and the finite-time convergence of the state and sliding variables while respecting the prescribed input-saturation limits. Compared to a reference control method, the proposed approach reduces the IAE, ISE, ITAE, and ITSE by 56.27\,\%, 56.40\,\%, 61.69\,\%, and 64.70\,\%, respectively. These results suggest that graph-based reinforcement learning can effectively tune parameters while retaining the robustness and analytical structure of the underlying sliding-mode controller.

title: Efficient ADMM for Soft-Constrained Quadratic Programs via Generalized Slack Projections
summary: Quadratic programs (QPs) are a core building block in many applications. In practice, constraints are often softened with slack variables to guarantee feasibility. The standard approach tackles this by introducing additional decision variables, growing the resulting optimization problem. In this paper, we propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) scheme for a broad class of convex slack penalty functions, including all $\ell_k$-norms, without increasing the problem size. The only change to the ADMM scheme is a modified slack projection function, while the remaining algorithm stays the same. We demonstrate our approach on numerical examples, showing significant speedups, and show its flexibility on an energy optimization problem.

title: Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning
summary: Standard reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms based on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) are vulnerable to sim-to-real gaps. To address this issue, distributionally robust RL algorithms based on robust MDPs (RMDPs) have been proposed, for ensuring that agents can perform reliably to unpredictable conditions in real-world environments. Despite of the rich literature, \revision{an efficient model-free method is still lacking} for robust RL, particularly for Markovian data, which is more relevant in practical applications. In this work, we take a step towards settling this problem by proposing a sample efficient (asynchronous Q-learning) algorithm for robust RL. In particular, consider a $γ$-discounted infinite-horizon RMDP with state space $\mathcal{S}$ and action space $\mathcal{A}$, where the uncertainty set is specified by the total variation (TV) distance with uncertainty level $σ$. Assuming access to a single trajectory of Markovian samples induced by a behavior policy and the nominal transition kernel, the sample complexity of the proposed Q-learning algorithm --- to achieve an entrywise $\varepsilon$-approximation of the optimal Q-function --- is bounded by $$ \frac{1}{μ_{\mathsf{min}}\varepsilon^2(1-γ)^3\max\{1-γ,σ\}} + \frac{t_{\mathsf{mix}}}{μ_{\mathsf{min}}(1-γ)} $$ up to logarithmic factors. Here, $t_{\mathsf{mix}}$ and $μ_{\mathsf{min}}$ denote the mixing time and the minimum state-action occupancy probability of the sample trajectory, respectively. This result is nearly minimax optimal, with an additional factor of $\frac{1}{1-γ}$. Moreover, it achieves a significant improvement over existing bounds.

title: Fuji: The Shape, Composition, and Spread of Demand Bursts on Robinhood Chain
summary: Demand on blockchain-based marketplaces arrives in bursts and at a high rate. On these platforms the data are completely visible, which makes it feasible to compare the bursty demand against the usual load. The congestion manifests as an increased demand for gas, the primary resource a blockchain sells. Existing studies consider how to price the gas. The demand itself, and what it is made of during bursts, has not been measured. We measure it on Robinhood Chain, a layer-2 blockchain that quickly became a venue for trading tokenized equities and memecoins. We collected the data from every block of its first three active months and more than 50 million Uniswap swaps that occurred during bursty periods. We find that a burst trades about as many pools as a quiet period, mostly different ones, and trades them harder, on top of elevated demand that accumulated for hours. With the bursts aligned on their peaks, the median peak is 2.5 times the usual load. Both the rise and the fall of the demand are described by the sum of two exponential functions with different timescales, a slow one of hours and a fast one of minutes. Against a matched quiet period, a burst has 1.05 times the pools, 1.40 times the trades, and 1.21 times the senders. We use two models to explain the arrival of bursts: externally triggered cascades and self-excitation. The former fits the data relatively better. Inside a burst, the entry of each trader into a pool is followed for about 24 seconds by more entries than the existing traders predict. Whether this is because of imitation or because of a shared signal is left open.

title: Model Selection for Off-Policy Evaluation via Pairwise Bellman Validation
summary: Model selection and hyperparameter tuning pose a central challenge in off-policy evaluation (OPE) because errors of fitted Q-functions and occupancy-ratio estimates cannot be directly evaluated from held-out transitions. Bellman-residual and minimax validation methods often require auxiliary regressions or optimization over separate critic classes, adding computational and tuning costs. We introduce pairwise Bellman validation (PBV), a tuning-free minimax procedure for selecting among finite classes of fitted Q-functions and occupancy-ratio estimators using held-out transitions. PBV constructs critics from pairwise candidate differences, requiring only finitely many empirical moment calculations without auxiliary validation models or separate critic optimization. We establish finite-sample oracle inequalities relative to the best available candidate, even under candidate-class misspecification. Our key insight is that Q-function errors and log ratios between candidate and true occupancy ratios provide oracle critics whose Bellman and adjoint Bellman moments control estimation error. Pairwise candidate differences approximate these unknown critics, while penalties account for comparator approximation error. For Q-function selection, we first develop unweighted PBV, which evaluates pairwise Bellman moments under the offline distribution and admits oracle guarantees under a pairwise coercivity condition relating the offline distribution to the target-policy dynamics. We then develop target-aligned PBV (TA-PBV), which uses marginalized importance weighting to provide error control without pairwise coercivity. For occupancy-ratio selection, we develop adjoint PBV (A-PBV), which evaluates adjoint Bellman moments against log-ratio critics. On Hopper and Deep OPE, unweighted PBV performs competitively, while target-occupancy weighting can improve performance in settings with controlled overlap.

title: Persistence Pays: Square-root condition-number dependence for Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin Monte Carlo with a non-reversibly updated accept/reject uniform
comments: 37 pages, 4 figures. Code and data in the ancillary files. Lean 4 formalization of the main results at https://github.com/nawafbourabee/persistence-pays-lean (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23671351)
summary: We prove accelerated mixing for a Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin sampler: the OBABO splitting with friction $2\sqrt m$, adjusted with Neal's non-reversibly updated uniform, which is redrawn after every epoch of $E$ steps. For targets $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $mI\preceq\nabla^2U\preceq LI$ and an $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian, started from a Gaussian at an approximate minimizer, the chain reaches total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ after $\tilde O\big(\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}(d/m)^{3/4}\big)$ gradient evaluations, where $κ=L/m$ and $\tilde O$ hides logarithmic factors. The $\sqrtκ$ term is necessary, already on Gaussian targets. The proof discretizes Lu's entropic hypocoercivity by means of an entropy inequality for free transport, so that the relative entropy of the unadjusted chain decays at a rate of order $\sqrt m$ up to a discretization bias. With the non-reversibly updated uniform, the leading energy errors of velocity Verlet telescope along a path. A coupling argument combines the two. On Bayesian logistic regression posteriors for two standard data sets, which satisfy these assumptions, the gradient cost of the chain with the non-reversibly updated uniform grows roughly like the square root of the condition number at the posterior mode, and that of standard adjusted OBABO roughly like its $3/4$ power.
comment: 37 pages, 4 figures. Code and data in the ancillary files. Lean 4 formalization of the main results at https://github.com/nawafbourabee/persistence-pays-lean (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23671351)

title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
summary:
We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition.
  The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures.
  For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $β$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $β> 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $β= 2$.

title: MedVTok: A General-Purpose Medical Visual Tokenizer
summary: Multimodal medical AI requires a common visual interface for encoding heterogeneous imaging evidence for patient condition modeling. However, existing medical visual tokenizers are often tied to a specific dimension and imaging modality, forcing multimodal systems to rely on fragmented and poorly reusable representations. We introduce MedVTok, a general-purpose visual tokenizer that maps 2D images and 3D volumes from diverse imaging modalities into a unified token space. Building such a tokenizer poses two key challenges: preserving anatomical structure across dimensions and capturing clinical semantics across modalities. To this end, MedVTok introduces (i) slice differential regularization, which explicitly models inter-slice anatomical coherence missing in previous per-pixel/per-voxel supervision, and (ii) multi-expert representation alignment, which integrates knowledge from multiple medical expert encoders while retaining modality-specific complementary knowledge. Trained on 28M images and 70K volumes across 9 imaging modalities, MedVTok supports classification, retrieval, segmentation, synthesis, visual question answering, and medical report generation through a single tokenizer. Across 24 benchmarks, MedVTok achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating a scalable token interface that unifies medical image dimension, modality, and task usage.

title: On the stability of learning
summary: Learning algorithms are usually analyzed under the assumption that informative gradients are continuously available. But this is not always true---learning signals in biological neural networks, for example, may be sparse, local, and only intermittently available at any given synapse. In this work, we show that if gradient information is noisy and only intermittently available, learning may be unstable. In particular, even if average learning dynamics converge to the correct optimum, variance in learning may be asymptotically infinite. We explore this point in a number of analytically tractable settings, including single-layer and multi-layer linear networks, and derive explicit conditions under which learning is stable. These conditions complement, but are conceptually distinct from, existing conditions related to the stability of stochastic gradient descent. Our work demonstrates that unbiased credit assignment is not enough for reliable learning; sufficiently frequent and informative feedback is also required, which yields an additional constraint on models of biologically plausible learning.

title: A note reviewing Turing's 1936
comments: 14 pages, for more information see http://paolacattabriga.wordpress.com/
summary: By closely rereading the original Turing's 1936 article, we can gain insight about that it is based on the claim to have defined a number which is not computable, arguing that there can be no machine computing the diagonal on the enumeration of the computable sequences. This article provides a careful analysis of Turing's original argument, demonstrating that it cannot be regarded as a conclusive proof. Furthermore, it shows that there is no evidence supporting the existence of a defined number that is not computable.
comment: 14 pages, for more information see http://paolacattabriga.wordpress.com/

title: Using RngStreams for Parallel Random Number Generation in C++ and R
comments: 20 pages; original supplementary code included. Corrects notation, references and code descriptions; clarifies stream allocation, mclapply, importance sampling and LSAT Section VII. Numerical examples and timing results unchanged. Corrections made with Codex (GPT-6 Astra). First-author audit disclosure included
summary: The RngStreams software package provides one viable solution to the problem of creating separate random number streams for simulations in parallel processing environments. Techniques are presented for effectively using RngStreams with C++ programs that are parallelized via OpenMP or MPI. Ways to access the backbone generator from RngStreams in R through the parallel and rstream packages are also described. The ideas in the paper are illustrated with both a simple running example and a Monte Carlo integration application.
